Noewe Accounting , the accounting business set up by integrated business services group Noewe, has secured €500,000 from private investor Philip Van Goethem, in a deal that values the company at €2.5m.

The capital will go towards building an accounting offering underpinned by automation and artificial intelligence, giving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) on-demand access to structured financial data, insights comparable to those of a CFO, and tax recommendations.

The funds will be spent on developing technology and refining the service model, setting the stage for further growth in Lithuania and across other EU markets.

The firm is targeting a common frustration for business owners: financial figures that arrive too late to be useful. At conventional accounting practices, much of the work, including handling invoices and transactions, recording ledger entries and producing financial statements, is still done by hand and can stretch over several weeks. As a result, the numbers managers rely on may not be ready until a month or more after the fact.

company_description: post-quantum security company focused on digital assets
article_title: Quantum risk puts digital asset insurance under scrutiny
article_excerpt:
Project Eleven , a post-quantum security company focused on digital assets, has partnered with Relm Insurance to explore how quantum-resistant security measures could influence insurance assessments for institutional digital asset custody.

The development partnership will focus on Project Eleven’s Strongpoint custody product, examining how institutions’ preparations for quantum computing threats could be evaluated within existing digital asset insurance frameworks. The initiative aims to establish a clearer understanding of how post-quantum security controls could factor into future assessments of institutional risk.

Quantum computing presents a potential challenge for digital asset security because a sufficiently powerful machine could derive private keys from exposed public keys, potentially compromising assets. This prospect is prompting institutions to consider how their custody infrastructure can adapt its cryptography before such a capability becomes available.

Strongpoint is designed to support this transition by combining conventional and post-quantum signing methods. Its architecture separates institutional controls from the cryptographic layer, allowing organisations to replace signing algorithms while retaining their existing approval rules and audit history.

The partnership will investigate several areas relevant to insurance underwriting, including exposure involving cryptographic keys, signing systems, transaction approval processes, readiness for cryptographic migration and dependencies on third-party providers. The findings are intended to help both companies assess how these factors could be considered when evaluating digital asset risks.

Relm will also contribute to the design and development of Strongpoint, providing an insurance perspective on how institutional custody infrastructure can support risk assessment. The work will inform the product’s approach to security controls and auditability, as well as the evidence institutions may need to demonstrate their post-quantum preparedness to insurers.

Project Eleven CEO and co-founder Alex Pruden said, “Every institution holding digital assets will eventually need to prepare for post-quantum cryptography. The open question is whether that transition happens on the institution’s schedule or under pressure. Insurance plays a critical role in how markets assess and manage risk. We believe there is an opportunity for institutions that invest in stronger post-quantum defenses to eventually see that reflected in how their risk is evaluated. Working with Relm is an important first step toward understanding what that could look like in practice.”

Relm Insurance founder and CEO Joseph Ziolkowski added, “Insuring exposures across the digital asset ecosystem requires underwriters to anticipate how risks will evolve. Quantum computing is a clear example of an emerging threat that should shape the way we assess risk today. Our work with Project Eleven will explore how institutions identify their exposure, demonstrate effective controls, and prepare for the transition to post-quantum readiness. Bringing underwriting expertise into that process early can help lay the groundwork for insurance solutions that support confidence, resilience, and continued growth in digital assets.”

The companies said the partnership remains exploratory, with the immediate focus on understanding quantum-related risks and the controls that may help mitigate them. Any future changes to insurance underwriting or premiums would require further evaluation and remain subject to Relm’s independent underwriting processes.

Citrea , an application layer for digital assets backed by Founders Fund and Galaxy Ventures , has acquired Crest , a self-custodial privacy wallet, as it looks to make private digital asset transactions easier for users.

The wallet is expected to launch in the coming weeks with automatic shielding, private asset transfers and onboarding from both Bitcoin and Ethereum networks.

Crest founder Meliksah Gurtemel will join Citrea as product lead as part of the acquisition. The two companies said they share a vision of making privacy a simple and intuitive part of using digital assets.

Citrea said public blockchain ledgers expose information including user balances, transaction counterparties and transaction histories. The company said this transparency could become more significant as the digital asset market grows and surveillance technology develops.

Users seeking greater privacy currently face several alternatives, according to Citrea, including giving up self-custody, using technically complex processes or moving into other privacy-focused digital assets. The company pointed to Zcash as an example of demand for simpler privacy features and said the acquisition will help bring a similar experience to the wider digital asset market.

Citrea provides an application layer designed to give institutions and users access to digital asset capital markets while remaining anchored to its underlying security model. Its backers include Founders Fund, Galaxy, Maven 11, Delphi Digital, Erik Voorhees and Balaji Srinivasan.

Crest is a self-custodial mobile wallet that uses zero-knowledge privacy pools through Citrea. Its planned features include automatic shielding, private asset transfers and private cross-chain payments. Users can currently join the wallet’s waitlist.

Chainway Labs co-founder and CEO Orkun Mahir Kılıç, a core contributor to Citrea, said, “Solving Bitcoin privacy is the single largest unlock for meeting real user demand on a Bitcoin layer. article_title: Stand hits $1bn valuation with $70m Series C raise
article_excerpt:
Stand , the InsurTech that strengthens and insures homes in regions exposed to natural catastrophes, has secured $70m in a Series C round that values the business at $1bn.

Saga Ventures led the investment, joined by backers including Lowercarbon, Eclipse, Equal Ventures, Inspired Capital, Neotribe and Jackson Square Ventures. The latest round lifts the company’s total funding to $130m. Over the past year, the value of property covered by Stand has climbed tenfold, rising from $1bn to more than $10bn.

The company is targeting a growing problem for homeowners. According to Stand, the US now experiences a weather disaster costing at least $1bn roughly every ten days. Many households are facing rising premiums, difficulty renewing policies and uncertainty over cover, even when their property itself has not changed. Stand argues this happens because insurers still set prices based on historical catastrophes, and that a physics-led approach offers a better alternative.

At the heart of the business is the Stand World Model, which builds a digital version of each home and tests how it would cope with wildfire, wind and other hazards. The model factors in how a property is built, what surrounds it and the weather conditions it is exposed to. Rather than relying on decades of loss data, the technology identifies what leaves a particular home at risk and the most cost-efficient ways to reduce that risk.

Stand then recommends upgrades designed to improve safety while keeping a home’s character intact. It supports owners throughout the process by guiding them through each stage, introducing them to trusted partners and verifying finished work on their behalf. Once a property is made more resilient, Stand passes on the reduced risk through discounts of up to 70%, while homeowners and their brokers benefit from competitive pricing and steadier coverage over the long term.

Stand underwrites and services policies issued by Concert Specialty Insurance Company, rated A- by AM Best, in California, and by Stand Insurance Exchange, rated A by Demotech, in Florida.

Alongside the funding, Stand has appointed two senior executives to support its expansion. Drew Saad has been named president of property & casualty, having previously served as chief underwriting officer at PURE Insurance, where he oversaw underwriting for one of the leading high-net-worth insurers in the US.

Tony Landi joins as CFO from Nephila, one of the largest catastrophe reinsurance fund managers globally, where he was head of strategic growth. He has also held roles as head of reinsurance & capital management at Openly and head of portfolio management at Everest Re. At Stand, Landi will oversee finance, reinsurance, capital markets and growth strategy.

Stand co-founder and CEO Dan Preston said, “Disasters follow the laws of physics, and insurance should too. If your home is resilient, you should be rewarded with a low premium and never have to worry about losing your coverage. We want to insure every resilient property in the world, and help make every property safe.”

Stand president of property & casualty Drew Saad said, “The companies that reshape a market for decades are the ones that identify a fundamentally better way to understand risk, and Stand has done that for the homes exposed to natural disasters.

“With the science already in place, the opportunity now is to build an insurance operation that matches it and scales it to every market that needs it. That is the work I have spent my career preparing for, and it is why I joined Stand.”

article_title: Cyera lands $400m from Goldman Sachs to secure AI agents
article_excerpt:
Cyera , a data security company building a unified data and identity platform for enterprises, has secured a $400m investment from Goldman Sachs to strengthen control over what AI agents can access and do.

The capital comes from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives as an extension to Cyera’s Series G, which was led by Evolution Equity. The funding supports the company’s goal of creating one platform to govern access for every human, machine and AI agent operating within an organisation.

Cyera plans to put the money towards new features on its AI Security product roadmap. It will also use the funding to expand further into the federal market and to keep growing internationally across EMEA and APAC, regions where enterprises increasingly want oversight of their agents.

The raise comes as AI agents take on a growing share of enterprise work. These agents differ from conventional software because they reason, adopt identities, call on tools, reach sensitive data and act on their own at machine speed. The broader their access, the more useful they are, but the damage also grows if that access is breached or drifts away from what the business intends.

According to Cyera, this makes agents one of the quickest-growing security threats enterprises have faced. Existing security architecture was designed around people and applications rather than millions of autonomous actors, and the company argues that protecting the agentic enterprise requires a model that unites data and identity.

Cyera began by protecting the data layer and this year extended that protection to the agents working with it. Its Agent Guardian and Cyera Endpoint products let enterprises monitor and hold AI agents accountable. They track prompts and responses as well as the tool calls, database queries and actions that happen between them. This coverage runs from the cloud to endpoint devices, where local agents such as Claude Code and Cursor are increasingly handling sensitive tasks.

Cyera also acquired Oasis Security, which merges this visibility with non-human identity (NHI) management in one system. The combined platform links where sensitive data sits with who or what can reach it. This gives enterprises a single way to govern access across humans, machines and AI agents.

Cyera is valued at more than $12bn. Its backers include Accel, Blackstone, Cyberstarts, Georgian, Lightspeed and Sequoia.

Cyera cofounder and CEO Yotam Segev said, “Global 2000 enterprises are telling us the same thing: they need to trust what AI agents can see and do before they can scale them.

“AI infrastructure is moving faster than the security architecture around it. This investment accelerates our work to bring data and identity together, so enterprises can give agents access with confidence and keep that access aligned with business intent.”

Goldman Sachs Alternatives managing director within Growth Equity Irit Kahan said, “Securing AI will be one of the defining categories in enterprise technology over the next decade.

“Cyera was the first to bring data and identity together, and as agents multiply faster than anyone can track, the gap between what they’re trusted to do and what they can actually reach is becoming increasingly dangerous. Cyera’s technology, customer traction, and execution position it to become the platform enterprises rely on to secure AI.”

article_title: Ryft secures £20m in UK’s largest payments Series B
article_excerpt:
Ryft , a Manchester-based payments company that builds infrastructure for marketplaces, platforms and multi-location businesses, has closed a £20m Series B funding round to support its next stage of international growth.

The round was led by Gresham House Ventures, with additional backing from existing investors Pembroke VCT and Ingenii Capital. The fresh capital will be used to fund Ryft’s expansion into Europe and the US, while also accelerating its product roadmap and its push into serving larger, enterprise-scale clients.

The raise follows a period of rapid growth for the company. Ryft has tripled its transaction processing volume over the last year, and its platform is now relied upon by more than 6,500 businesses, including Epos Now, Chaiwalla, the Disasters Emergency Committee, Daytrip and Sprive. As part of its European growth plans, Ryft has submitted an application for a full EU licence with the Malta Financial Services Authority, a move that would allow it to passport its services throughout the European Economic Area.

Since it was established in 2021 by Alex Mackenzie, Richard Kirby and Sadra Hosseini, Ryft has focused on building payment infrastructure for marketplaces, platforms and businesses operating across multiple locations. Its technology helps these organisations manage seller onboarding and handle intricate transaction flows, such as recurring billing, automated split payments and cross-border payouts, all through a single integration, an approach designed to help merchants scale quickly while also opening new revenue opportunities from the payments they process.

The company has built partnerships with several major payment providers since launching, among them Global Payments, Visa, Mastercard, American Express and Nuvei.

Economic Secretary to the Treasury Lucy Rigby said, “Ryft’s success is a vote of confidence in Manchester’s thriving fintech sector and shows how British businesses can start, scale and compete on the global stage. This Government is backing the industries and companies like Ryft that are creating jobs, attracting investment and driving good growth in every postcode.”

Ryft CEO and co-founder Sadra Hosseini said, “This round of investment means we can take what we’ve built in the UK into new European markets and compete on the global stage. Payments have been dominated by a small number of incumbents for a long time. We want to provide a powerful and efficient alternative to businesses, not just in Europe, but globally.”

Gresham House Ventures Partner Rohit Mathur said, “As commerce shifts to instant, multi-party platforms and increasingly agent-initiated payments, ownership of the infrastructure rails becomes a question of national economic sovereignty, not just merchant cost. We’re backing Ryft because the UK needs domestic champions with payment architecture for the next era of commerce, and Ryft is one of them. Sadra, Alex, Richard and the wider team are executing at an impressive pace, and we are proud to back this category-defining Manchester FinTech!”

article_title: Tabby raises $233m at $6.5bn valuation
article_excerpt:
Tabby , the Saudi Arabia- and UAE-based buy now, pay later and financial services provider, has raised $233m in a new equity round.

The financing was led by existing backer Blue Pool Capital, with participation from current shareholders HSG, Wellington Management and Arbor Ventures, and values Tabby at $6.5bn.

Tabby has been profitable since 2023 and now handles more than $18bn in annualised transaction volume, serving 25 million registered users through partnerships with 70,000 businesses. The fresh capital is earmarked for Tabby’s push beyond BNPL into a wider suite of credit and money management products across its two core markets.

As part of the deal, employees will be given a liquidity option. Tabby has run share tenders since 2023, through which staff, past and present, have cashed out more than $100m in share sales.

Tabby has spent the last year building out its licensing footprint. The Saudi Central Bank has awarded the company consumer and SME finance licences, letting it extend larger, longer-term credit to individuals and working capital to businesses.

Tabby also bought Tweeq, a digital wallet licensed by SAMA, adding accounts, cards and transfers to its offering.

In the UAE, the Central Bank granted Tabby a Stored Value Facilities licence, paving the way for Tabby Cash, a fee-free alternative to a debit account that pays cashback on card spending and supports domestic and international transfers.

Tabby was founded on the idea of letting shoppers split the cost of a purchase at checkout, and the company says every product and licence it has added since has extended that same mission. Completion of the round still depends on regulatory sign-off, including clearance from SAMA.

Hosam Arab, CEO and Co-Founder of Tabby, said: “ We began with a button at an online checkout to help people spread costs over time. Everything since, every product and every licence, has come back to the same idea: people deserve more from their money. This round means we can build further on that, without changing how we think about growth or discipline.”

Christopher Wu, Chief Investment Officer at Blue Pool Capital, said: “ Tabby has demonstrated an impressive ability to innovate for their customers, evolving beyond payments to become the trusted platform for millions of people managing, spending and growing their money across the region. We are proud of our partnership with Tabby over the past three years, and we are excited to continue supporting the impressive growth of the company with this financing.”

article_title: Aqua raises $18.8m to build alternatives infrastructure
article_excerpt:
Aqua , a next-generation alternatives infrastructure provider, has launched what it describes as the industry’s first turnkey alternative investments platform (TAIP), alongside $18.8m in total funding to support the rollout.

The capital was raised in two stages: a $3.8m seed round backed by Google’s AI Fund, Y Combinator and other investors, followed by a $15m Series A round led by Arthur Ventures with participation from Alumni Ventures.

Aqua intends to put the funding towards accelerating business and platform development, growing its engineering and partnership teams, and deepening its integrations with custodians and fund sponsors.

The platform is built for wealth managers, RIAs, banks, trust companies and fund sponsors that want to construct, run and expand institutional-grade alternatives programmes.

It is designed to replace the fragmented marketplaces, manual processes and spreadsheets that many firms currently depend on, bringing fund creation, operational workflows, investment lifecycle management, marketplace access, document intelligence and investor servicing together within a single environment. This unified approach is intended to let firms design their own alternatives strategy and grow it at a pace that suits them.

Aqua positions itself as addressing a shift taking place across the alternatives space more broadly. Where the sector’s initial growth phase was largely about widening access, the company argues the next stage requires scalable infrastructure to help firms manage alternatives effectively, a gap it says its platform is built to close.

Aqua’s leadership brings together backgrounds spanning wealth management and financial technology. Co-founder and chief executive Rohan Marwaha previously developed solutions across technology and alternative investments for major alternative asset managers, while David Coyle has spent more than 25 years driving technology adoption within advisory firms.

Head of growth partnerships Joe Ujobai has over 35 years of experience in financial services and technology, including leadership roles in private banking and international expansion. Together, the team frames its approach to alternatives infrastructure as coming from direct industry experience rather than an outsider’s perspective.

Aqua Co-Founder and CEO Rohan Marwaha said, “Demand for alternatives has grown fast, but most firms are still trying to meet client needs with spreadsheets, fragmented processes and manual solutions. Firms have already transformed the way they manage traditional investments through technology. As access to alternatives becomes increasingly democratized, they need similar infrastructure to build repeatable, scalable alternatives strategies. We built Aqua around the way today’s advisors operate, so they can develop customized alternatives programs without having to manage the systems behind them.”

Aqua Head of Growth David Coyle said, “Many firms still think a marketplace is the same thing as an alternatives strategy. It isn’t. Advisors need more than access to alternatives; they need a repeatable way to educate clients, manage operations, and deliver alternatives with confidence as part of a broader wealth strategy. Aqua is the enablement engine ushering in the next generation of alternative investing.”

article_title: Aggne delivers Duck Creek go-live for Capricorn Mutual
article_excerpt:
Aggne , a Wipro company and a leading InsurTech services provider, has confirmed the successful go-live of Capricorn Mutual on Duck Creek Technologies ‘ core insurance platform, representing a key step forward in the mutual’s technology modernisation programme.

The rollout forms part of Capricorn Mutual’s broader ambitions to reinforce its service delivery, boost operational efficiency, and lay the groundwork for continued expansion.

The project was carried out in collaboration with Duck Creek Technologies, with Aggne overseeing the transition away from Capricorn Mutual’s previous legacy infrastructure.

As part of the overhaul, Aggne worked alongside Capricorn Mutual and Duck Creek Technologies to roll out Duck Creek’s Policy, Rating, Billing, Claims, and Clarity solutions via Duck Creek OnDemand, moving the organisation onto a cloud-based, interconnected system.

Drawing on its specialist knowledge of the insurance sector and experience modernising core platforms, Aggne managed the integration of essential business functions spanning banking, financial oversight, vehicle and property data, and bespoke technologies, making use of Duck Creek’s open API framework throughout.

The result is a joined-up operational structure that gives Capricorn Mutual greater automation, tighter governance, improved data accuracy, higher efficiency, and the flexibility required to adapt to shifting business demands.

Aggne noted that the successful go-live reflects a wider trend among insurers and mutuals looking to update their core systems in order to enhance service delivery, streamline operations, and get ready for future capabilities built around data and artificial intelligence.

Capricorn Mutual Limited is Capricorn’s member-owned risk protection body, set up to give Capricorn Members an alternative to conventional insurance. Operating since 2003, it has provided risk protection services tailored specifically to the automotive sector, supporting Members in safeguarding their businesses, assets, and livelihoods.

Aggne, a Wipro company, is a technology, managed services, and advisory firm delivering measurable outcomes for clients through a distinctive set of capabilities and intellectual property within the Property & Casualty insurance space. It provides IP- and AI-driven consulting, implementation, and managed services designed to speed up deployment results for insurers, transform their operations, execute agentic AI efficiently, and deliver strong customer experiences.

Capricorn Chief Financial Services Officer Damon de Nooyer said, “This investment is about ensuring Capricorn Mutual is well positioned to support our Members now and into the future.

“By modernising our core systems, we’ve strengthened the foundations of the business and created new opportunities to improve how we work, make decisions and serve our Members. Aggne was a valued partner throughout the project, helping us successfully deliver a platform that will support our continued growth and commitment to providing Members with the protection and service they rely on.”

Aggne CEO Asha Kalidindi said, “Successful core system transformations require a combination of industry expertise, proven implementation capabilities, and close collaboration .

“We are proud to have partnered with Capricorn Mutual and Duck Creek on this important initiative. This go-live provides the foundation for future innovation while enabling improved operational efficiency, greater agility, and enhanced experiences for Capricorn Mutual’s members.

company_description: Calgary-based payments platform Helcim has raised $53m in a Series C funding round, taking its valuation to $250m as it looks to capitalise on a gap left by banks retreating from merchant services.
article_title: Helcim raises $53m as banks retreat from SME payments
article_excerpt:
Calgary-based payments platform Helcim has raised $53m in a Series C funding round, taking its valuation to $250m as it looks to capitalise on a gap left by banks retreating from merchant services.

The round was led by BDC Capital’s Growth Venture Fund, with participation from new investors Curql, a strategic investment vehicle backed by more than 160 North American credit unions, and Gold House Ventures.

Existing investors including Headline, Aquiline, Information Venture Partners, Vesey Ventures, Clocktower Ventures and Alberta Accelerate Fund also participated. The latest raise brings Helcim’s total equity funding since its Series A in 2022 to $100m. Its valuation has increased from $97m at its 2024 Series B.

The funding comes as several major banks in Canada and the US have scaled back their merchant services operations, either selling or outsourcing those businesses. Helcim is looking to fill the gap by providing small and mid-sized businesses and credit unions with an alternative payments platform.

The company offers in-person and online payments alongside transparent pricing and direct customer support, while increasingly targeting larger businesses.

Founded in 2020, Helcim built its payments infrastructure in-house rather than relying on third-party technology. It says this allows it to offer volume-based interchange-plus pricing rather than the flat-rate fees common across the payments market.

The company now has 200 employees and serves more than 22,000 active merchants across Canada and the US. It has also surpassed $150m in annual recurring revenue and is approaching $10bn in annual payment volume.

In January, Helcim launched an AI-powered Payment Extension, allowing merchants to integrate its payment processing capabilities into existing software without being tied to a single embedded payments provider.

The company said adoption of the tool has been rapid, with the technology contributing to demand for its platform. Helcim plans to use the latest funding to expand its platform, move further into financial services and strengthen partnerships with regional banks and credit unions.

Nic Beique, founder and CEO of Helcim, said, “There’s a real void in the market right now – merchants are coming to Helcim faster than ever, looking for a modern alternative.”

“This round lets us act on this at scale: expanding our platform, growing our team, and moving up-market so no business outgrows what we can offer them,” he added.

BDC Capital Growth Venture Fund partner Jack Fraser said Helcim was “growing fast and building a real advantage in the market”.

“ [Its] recent AI-powered integration tool is a good example of the kind of fast-moving innovation we’re backing, and exactly what it will take to capture that opportunity,” Fraser said.

Curql president and CEO Nick Evens said credit unions need to upgrade their offerings for small business members as they compete to remain relevant and retain deposits.

“Helcim’s payment hub is the best we have seen and their value proposition for the CUs is far more robust than what is currently in market,” Evens said.

The investment comes as banks and credit unions increasingly reassess how they deliver payments infrastructure to small businesses, creating an opening for independent PayTech providers to build deeper relationships with financial institutions.

article_title: August Equity backs InsurTech MGA Starpeak
article_excerpt:
August Equity , a UK private equity firm focused on the lower-mid-market, has agreed to invest in Starpeak , a specialist digital insurance distributor serving niche SME and personal lines markets.

The transaction marks the sixth deal completed under the firm’s Fund VI and remains subject to sign-off from the Financial Conduct Authority.

Starpeak operates as a technology-enabled managing general agent under the leadership of Andy Brownsell and Andy Pilgrim, running several brands including Protectivity and SportsCover Direct to serve more than 175,000 customers across the UK annually, with a focus on underserved, high-growth niches.

Backing from August will go towards further development of Starpeak’s in-house technology platform, iTraps, which supports quick product launches, largely automated underwriting, and streamlined direct-to-consumer sales, enabling the rollout of highly tailored insurance products in specialist markets. Alongside organic growth, the company is also considering acquisitions to expand further.

The deal reflects August’s established approach of investing in adjacent sectors where management teams already carry deep experience, extending its footprint in financial services. It comes after the firm exited AAB to Goldman Sachs Alternatives and follows fresh backing for financial services business Superbia and legal firm Higgs LLP.

Peter Thompson has been appointed Chair of Starpeak as part of the transaction, bringing with him substantial industry knowledge gained as CEO of BGL Group, a business he took through a successful sale to the Pollen Street-backed Markerstudy Group.

In a joint statement, Starpeak CEO Andy Brownsell and CTO Andy Pilgrim said, “This investment represents an exciting new chapter for our team. We have built a scalable platform that combines strong insurance expertise with sophisticated technology and data capabilities. Partnering with August now gives us greater resources to accelerate our growth while continuing to deliver exceptional service to our customers.”

August Equity Partner Kishan Chotai, who previously worked on the firm’s investments in AAB and Superbia, said “Starpeak has built a strong reputation and demonstrated sustainable >25% annual growth in highly attractive markets. The UK insurance services sector continues to benefit from increasing demand for niche, hyper-personalised solutions, something that Starpeak has at its core. We believe the business has a highly scalable technology platform and an ambitious leadership team, both of which provide excellent investment dynamics.”

article_title: Payhawk raises $280m to build AI-era Finance OS
article_excerpt:
Payhawk , the Sofia-founded spend management and finance platform, has closed a $280m Series C round led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The deal values the company at $2bn.

The raise takes Payhawk’s total funding past $515m. Every existing backer returned for the round, among them QED, Greenoaks, Lightspeed, Hedosophia and Bek Ventures.

They were joined by first-time investors Galdana Ventures, Cogito Capital, Inveready and Invus, as well as European founders Tomas Okmanas and Didac Lee.

Payhawk plans to put the money towards a broader goal: creating a worldwide Finance Operating System designed for the age of AI.

Goldman Sachs Alternatives managing director James Hayward will also take a seat on the company’s board.

The business began in Sofia and now has 12 offices and a presence in 33 countries. Its platform handles many currencies, banking networks, payment rails, regulatory regimes and local business customs. Payhawk sees that complexity as something it can turn into a global edge.

The company notes that many finance tools, including ERP systems, banks, procurement and treasury products, travel software and spend platforms, are gaining intelligence through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. However, it argues that upgrading individual applications does not by itself produce a more intelligent finance function.

To address this, Payhawk is structuring its Finance Operating System around three connected layers. The first is AI agents that carry out financial tasks. The second is payments infrastructure that lets those agents handle money safely. The third is enterprise controls that set the limits on what agents can do and decide when a human must step in. By combining these layers, the company aims to move AI from a supporting role into the core of how finance teams operate.

Payhawk CEO Hristo Borisov said, “The role of the finance team is rapidly moving away from manual checks, lengthy reconciliations and labor-intensive work towards becoming more strategic. While most companies use AI to speed up existing processes, we built AI agents to fundamentally rethink how finance operates.

“Through our technology, finance departments can benefit from ‘zero-touch finance’, where neither the finance professional nor the employee deals with any admin work. 77% of our customers use our agents daily across financial control, procurement, travel and reporting to save time and money for their businesses. But AI alone cannot deliver this transformation, it must be combined with a robust payment infrastructure and enterprise controls to truly unlock the potential of every enterprise in the new AI era.”

Goldman Sachs Alternatives managing director James Hayward said, “Payhawk’s exceptional growth reflects the strength of its engineering DNA, global footprint and clear vision for the future of modern spend management systems.

“As payments, AI and enterprise software increasingly converge, we believe Payhawk is well positioned to emerge as a leader in this rapidly evolving market. We are excited to partner with the team as they continue to scale globally and enter their next phase of growth.”

article_title: Zigram: A7’s $6.9bn trail exposes global sanctions screening gaps
article_excerpt:
A7 , a Russia-linked cross-border payments network, has channelled billions of dollars through major international banks, exposing weaknesses in sanctions screening and raising questions about how financial institutions identify transactions linked to sanctioned entities.

Established in 2024 by Promsvyazbank (PSB) , a Russian state-owned lender with close ties to the defence sector, and Moldovan oligarch Ilan Mironovich Shor, the network operates through three central entities: A7 LLC, A71 LLC and A7 Agent LLC. These businesses oversee an extensive structure of shell companies and financial intermediaries spanning at least 83 countries and approximately 435 financial institutions.

A Financial Times investigation based on leaked internal documents traced approximately $6.9bn in payments involving A7-linked entities between late 2024 and August 2025. The transactions passed through accounts at several major international banks, including Standard Chartered ($1.1bn through Hong Kong), First Abu Dhabi Bank (more than $1.8bn across 17 entities), DBS ($273m), Citigroup ($74m) and Deutsche Bank ($18m).

One front company registered in Kyrgyzstan accounted for approximately $2.4bn in transactions. More than $2bn in export earnings linked to Russian oil company Rosneft was also reportedly channelled through at least 16 trading businesses.

Figures from US authorities suggest the network’s activities extend considerably further. The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) estimates that A7 sub-agents processed more than $17bn in dollar-denominated transactions between January 2025 and June 2026. These flows included payments associated with Iranian oil sales and weapons procurement.

US filings also place the network’s overall transaction volume above 7.5 trillion roubles, equivalent to approximately $91.5bn. However, this figure covers a different period and measure of activity from the $6.9bn identified in the Financial Times investigation, meaning the amounts should not be combined.

The network allegedly concealed the nature of payments by making them resemble routine international trade. Transactions generally fell within the mid-to-high six-figure range, while supporting invoices referred to consumer products, equipment and commodities. Military-related goods, including night-vision equipment, were reportedly described as “hardened glass” in export documentation.

A7 also allegedly maintained counterfeit stamps, seals and document templates, alongside changing restricted Harmonised System (HS) codes to unrestricted alternatives. Its operations extended beyond traditional banking infrastructure through the use of A7A5, a rouble-backed stablecoin issued by affiliated company Old Vector LLC.

Regulatory scrutiny escalated on October 1, 2026, when the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated A7 as a significant transnational criminal organisation under Executive Order 13581. The action blocked property belonging to A7 LLC, A7 Agent LLC, Old Vector LLC, Garantex, Grinex and individuals including Shor and Sergey Mendeleev.

FinCEN also issued an industry alert and proposed a rule that would prevent US financial institutions from processing transactions involving A7 sub-agents across both traditional currencies and virtual assets. The developments followed an August alert from the UK’s National Crime Agency highlighting concerns about the network.

A7 maintains that it supports legitimate trade, while not every transaction associated with the network has been subject to a court ruling.

The investigation highlights how conventional sanctions screening can struggle to identify risks when financial institutions assess individual customers rather than the wider networks behind their transactions. Nominee ownership arrangements below the 50% threshold, apparently legitimate sub-agents and disconnected trade, shipping and payment information reportedly helped the network avoid conventional checks.

article_title: MSCI and UBS join forces to crack private markets opacity
article_excerpt:
MSCI, the index and analytics provider listed on the NYSE, has formed a strategic partnership with global banking group UBS to tackle the lack of transparency that has long hampered private markets investing.

The alliance will pair MSCI’s independent data, analytics and modelling capabilities with the alternatives expertise and worldwide client knowledge held by UBS. The two firms intend to build out MSCI’s AI-powered platform, which is designed to resolve persistent problems in the asset class, including fragmented information and poor visibility for investors.

Drawing on the Limited Partner, Wealth Management and Asset Management viewpoints UBS contributes, the collaboration aims to deliver a more joined-up and standardised experience spanning the entire private markets investment lifecycle. The goal is to let investors reach insights faster and assess opportunities with stronger conviction. UBS, described as the world’s largest truly global wealth manager and a leading asset manager, will be among the platform’s earliest users and will work alongside MSCI to push for wider adoption and common standards across the industry.

The platform unites fund discovery, portfolio management, analytics and benchmarking within one ecosystem. It also simplifies data handling and links private and public markets, with automated processing and MSCI’s independent performance figures giving investors timelier and more consistent portfolio-level insights. Beyond this, the tie-up is intended to nurture an ecosystem connecting General Partners with institutional and private wealth investors.

MSCI chairman and CEO Henry Fernandez said, “MSCI has long been committed to bringing independence, transparency and innovation to global investors. As private markets become an increasingly important part of the investment landscape, investors are looking for the insights, rigor and accessibility that they have come to expect in public markets. By combining MSCI and UBS’s respective strengths, we aim to help build the infrastructure that can shape the future of private markets investing.”

UBS Group CEO Sergio P. Ermotti said, “This partnership builds on our long-standing relationship with MSCI and our shared ambition to increase transparency in private markets. As a leading LP, our Unified Global Alternatives business brings extensive industry insights and a deep understanding of clients’ evolving needs. Through our collaboration with MSCI, our goal is to help to shape the next generation of private markets portfolio management solutions and transform the decision-making process for clients across public and private markets.”

article_title: Velocity raises $38m to push stablecoins into treasury
article_excerpt:
Velocity , a stablecoin treasury and settlement platform targeting enterprise payments infrastructure, has raised $38m in Series A funding as businesses explore alternatives for cross-border settlement and liquidity management.

The round was co-led by Dragonfly and FirstMark, with participation from Activant Capital, Capital One Ventures, QED Investors, Coinbase Ventures, Wintermute Ventures and Ripple. The raise brings Velocity’s total funding to almost $50m since the company was founded in May 2025.

Founded in 2025, London-based Velocity provides infrastructure for merchants, payment providers, FinTech companies and financial institutions looking to use stablecoins within existing treasury operations. Its platform enables businesses to hold, transfer and settle funds using stablecoin networks, while connecting those flows with banking infrastructure, compliance processes, custody, liquidity management and settlement systems.

The company is targeting a growing interest among enterprises in using stablecoins for payments and treasury operations, as firms look to reduce settlement times, manage liquidity across markets and improve visibility over global cash positions.

Velocity said its platform is designed to allow CFOs and treasury teams to adopt stablecoin-based settlement without replacing existing financial workflows. The technology combines stablecoin infrastructure with traditional banking connections to support cross-border money movement and settlement.

The funding will be used to expand Velocity’s banking and payments network, accelerate product development, strengthen regulatory capabilities and support enterprise adoption.

Dragonfly general partner Rob Hadick said, “We first met Velocity over a year ago, and it was clear from the beginning they have a uniquely deep understanding of the global payments stack and how it can be disrupted. What sets them apart is their ability to connect traditional payments and banking infrastructure with stablecoin networks and unlock significant value.”

FirstMark partner Adam Nelson commented, “The most enduring technology companies are built around shifts that fundamentally change how industries operate. We believe stablecoins have the potential to transform the movement of money as profoundly as the internet transformed the movement of information.”

QED Investors partner Gbenga Ajayi said stablecoin adoption will depend on infrastructure that integrates with existing business processes, adding that Velocity has built a platform designed around treasury workflows.

Velocity founder and CEO Eric Queathem added that the company has focused on the needs of CFOs and treasury teams rather than only crypto-native users.

“Stablecoins are moving beyond payments and becoming core infrastructure for how businesses manage and move money globally,” Queathem said.

The funding comes as stablecoins continue to move beyond digital asset markets into areas including payments, settlement and financial infrastructure, with enterprise providers building platforms aimed at connecting blockchain-based systems with traditional financial networks.

article_title: Kalepa raises $75m to scale AI across insurance
article_excerpt:
Kalepa , the New York-based InsurTech developing artificial intelligence for insurance professionals, has raised $75m in a Series B funding round at a $470m valuation, following a year in which its revenue and client base each tripled.

The round was led by Updata Partners , with existing investors IA Ventures and Inspired Capital also participating. The investment brings Kalepa’s total funding to $91m, following a $14m Series A in 2021 led by Inspired Capital, with IA Ventures also taking part.

Kalepa plans to use the proceeds to expand its AI product portfolio, enter additional markets and double its workforce during 2027. The company said it has maintained positive cash flow for more than two years while achieving its recent growth. Its customers include major insurance carriers and managing general agents (MGAs), such as W. R. Berkley, Bowhead Specialty and AmRisc.

The investment comes as insurers face growing pressure to improve underwriting efficiency, manage rising claims costs and address the loss of experienced professionals. As established employees leave the industry, insurers risk losing specialist knowledge, while newer AI-focused competitors are raising expectations around speed and operational performance. Softer insurance pricing is adding further pressure, leaving businesses with less room for underwriting mistakes.

Kalepa’s platform is designed to coordinate work across insurance operations, underwriting, pricing and portfolio management. Its technology uses a purpose-built AI harness to manage underlying agents, adapting to changing conditions and determining how much autonomy each task should receive according to its risk. Human professionals remain involved where specialist judgement or approval is required, while outputs are checked to maintain traceability and auditability.

The company reports that customers have achieved between 30% and 60% more premium per underwriter, a 58% reduction in quoting times, a 960-basis-point improvement in combined ratios and a doubling of quote-to-bind rates. The volume of work processed through the platform also increased fourfold over the past 12 months.

Alongside its funding, Kalepa has strengthened its leadership team with the appointment of Garrett Schlesinger as chief technology officer. He joins from Affirm, where he spent 12 years, having joined as its 12th employee and contributed to the development of its real-time underwriting engine.

article_title: CoComply raises £1.9m to expose hidden workforce risk
article_excerpt:
CoComply , a UK RegTech scale-up focused on external workforce compliance, has secured £1.9m to speed up product development and expand its presence both at home and abroad.

NPIF – Mercia Equity Finance led the round. The fund is run by Mercia Ventures within the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II). UK venture capital firm Haatch, which pairs capital with hands-on support for founders, also took part, alongside management and other investors.

Those backers include Richard Law, the former CEO of GBG and a technology investor with a portfolio that features Vypr, who will take on the role of chair. They also include Seb Timpson, co-founder of With Intelligence, a financial data and intelligence firm that S&P Global bought for $1.8bn in November 2025, and Stephen Cann, CEO of Bollin Group, owner of brands such as Mountain Equipment, Sprayway, Ronhill and Bridgedale.

The raise comes as reliance on people outside the payroll keeps rising. Oversight of these workers is often split between HR, procurement, finance and legal teams. Many contractors, agency staff and service provider personnel sit inside supplier agreements, statements of work and service contracts. As a result, organisations can lose track of who is actually doing the work, on what terms, and which obligations follow.

CoComply serves mid-market and large organisations. Its platform surfaces external workers, including those concealed within supplier contracts, and maps how each person is engaged. It then sets out which compliance checks apply. The AI-native system pairs automation with specialist classification expertise and operates at the moment work first arrives in a business.

From there, it helps teams define the work required, choose a suitable engagement route, classify workers accurately and settle the approvals needed. The emphasis is on prevention. The goal is to catch exposure around worker classification and IR35, Right to Work and modern slavery before it becomes a liability.

Commercial traction has been strong. Revenue rose 240% in 2025, and the company expects growth of more than 120% in 2026.

Customer expansion has tripled year on year. Clients range from mid-market firms to FTSE 100 groups, including Aston Martin, Take-Two, RS Group, Thredd, Quint Group, Dementia UK and the Royal Yachting Association. CoComply also received an Innovate UK Smart Grant in 2024.

The new capital will fund product work and a larger sales, marketing and delivery operation. This supports the company’s long-term aim of categorising and classifying the global workforce so that compliance holds everywhere.

CoComply founder and CEO Michael Cleavely said, “Despite growing reliance on external workers in every industry, many businesses still struggle to answer a very basic question: how many people actually work for us, what are they doing and how are they engaged?”

“That becomes a serious governance and compliance problem when responsibility is spread across business functions. Our mission is to provide the decision and governance layer across these teams, helping them choose the right engagement model and classify work correctly from the outset.”

Cleavely added, “We’ve brought together investors with first-hand experience of building substantial businesses who can help us make better decisions, challenge our thinking and introduce us to the right people as we grow. That experience matters enormously at this stage.”

article_title: Synctera raises $24.5m as banks return to BaaS
article_excerpt:
Synctera , the embedded finance and banking as a service (BaaS) platform, has raised $24.5m in new funding as sponsor banks renew their interest in embedded banking, bringing its total capital raised to $126.7m.

The San Francisco-based company secured investment from Multiplier Capital, Fin Capital, 1st & Main Growth Partners, Diagram and NAventures. The funding will support its work with sponsor banks and FinTechs, strengthen its balance sheet and provide additional runway as it targets break-even.

The raise comes as financial institutions reconsider their approach to BaaS, with some looking to establish or expand partnerships after reassessing the complexity and costs of building the infrastructure themselves.

Synctera is positioning its platform around operational resilience and regulatory compliance, arguing that banks need dependable technology to support programmes that can run for years and carry significant reputational responsibility.

Compliance is a central part of that strategy. In April 2026, Synctera acquired Cable, a compliance technology provider that enables continuous testing of controls across banks, FinTechs and service providers. Rather than relying on periodic sampling, the technology allows institutions to assess whether controls are operating effectively on an ongoing basis.

Synctera has also established a dedicated programme management team, introduced supporting operational processes and registered with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) as a money services business (MSB). The company says these measures provide the ongoing oversight required to protect consumers and businesses using its banking and payments programmes.

The company operates as a software provider rather than a bank, working with multiple sponsor banks that retain responsibility for their individual programmes. This model is designed to distribute operational risk across banking partners, reducing the potential disruption if one institution changes its strategy or risk appetite.

Massachusetts-based Main Street Bank is the latest sponsor bank to join Synctera’s network, taking the active total to eight. Two additional banks are nearing the end of implementation and are expected to launch programmes in the fourth quarter.

Founded in 2020, Synctera provides the infrastructure companies need to develop banking and payments products, while giving sponsor banks tools to oversee their FinTech partnerships and associated compliance obligations.

The company is also expanding its offering through Synctera Labs, launched in October. The initiative gives FinTechs developing embedded finance propositions access to live accounts, cards and customers, with compliance and oversight built in. The model is designed to reduce the upfront costs associated with launching bespoke programmes, with its first launches scheduled for February 2027.

Synctera has signed 20 clients during 2026 across financial services, property management and small and medium-sized business (SMB) lending. Its customer base ranges from early-stage FinTechs to publicly listed companies.

The company also reported that gross merchandise value (GMV) and interchange revenue have doubled year on year. Since joining Synctera, Cable has added one banking client and four FinTech clients, with its services now provided free of charge to sponsor banks within the Synctera network.

Multiplier Capital managing director Ash Vaidya said, “Embedded finance only works when banks can trust what’s happening on their charter, and Synctera has built its platform around exactly that: an independent ledger, automated reconciliation and, with Cable, continuous compliance testing. At Multiplier, we back companies that provide mission-critical infrastructure and have earned their place as category leaders. As banks return to BaaS, Synctera is the partner they need, and we’re proud to support Peter and the team in this next phase of growth.”

article_title: Elio Mortgage raises $5.1m to rebuild lending with AI
article_excerpt:
Elio Mortgage , a New York-based mortgage company using artificial intelligence across the home loan process, has emerged from stealth with $5.1m in pre-seed funding as it targets the cost and complexity of mortgage origination.

Motive Partners and Social Leverage co-led the round, with Jeff Horing, co-founder and managing director of Insight Partners, also participating as an angel investor. Elio plans to use the funding to develop its product, expand its licensed mortgage business nationwide and hire loan officers for its AI-native brokerage.

Elio said that mortgage technology has largely focused on improving individual stages of the lending process rather than connecting the full journey. This leaves loan officers and back-office teams responsible for manually coordinating multiple systems and workflows.

Rather than developing software separately from the lending process, Elio’s engineers work alongside loan officers within its mortgage operation. The company says this approach allows its technology to evolve around the practical requirements of day-to-day origination.

Elio operates as a licensed mortgage provider rather than a standalone software vendor, with an agentic platform at the core of its model. The technology is designed to handle more of the operational workload, allowing loan officers to dedicate more time to client relationships, advice and lending decisions.

The company is targeting changes to both mortgage workflows and the economics of originating loans, while enabling loan officers to serve more borrowers and build their client books. The same platform also supports Elio Embedded, through which the company provides mortgage services for registered investment advisers, real estate agents, homebuilders and owners of single-family rental portfolios.

These businesses already have relationships with potential homebuyers but would otherwise need to establish their own lending infrastructure to offer mortgage services. Elio Embedded is designed to let them provide financing as an extension of their existing customer relationships.

Elio Mortgage CEO and co-founder Oren Michaely said, “Mortgage is one of the largest financial markets in the world, yet the way loans are originated has changed remarkably little. The industry has spent years digitising individual processes, but people are still responsible for stitching those processes together. AI gives us the opportunity to redesign the entire origination model, changing how work is divided between people and technology, how organisations are structured, the cost of originating a loan, and the borrower experience. We’re building Elio to show what a fundamentally better mortgage company can look like.”

Motive Partners partner, venture Harsh Govil also commented, “The next generation of financial services are being built around AI, with intelligence systems coordinating and executing work across the business rather than automating isolated tasks. In truly AI-native companies, the technology largely disappears into the operating model, while customers and employees experience a fundamentally faster and improved service. We believe Elio represents that shift in mortgage, an industry where we see enormous opportunity to redesign operations and economics.”

Social Leverage managing director Matt Ober added, “We invest in founders who challenge entrenched industries with new business models, and Elio represents exactly that kind of opportunity. By combining an AI-native operating model with an embedded distribution strategy, Elio enables financial advisors and other businesses with trusted customer relationships to make mortgage financing a seamless extension of the services they already provide. We look forward to supporting them as they redefine how borrowers access home financing.”

Key Indian FinTech investment stats in H1 2026:

Indian FinTech investments increased 73% YoY in H1

Funding is expected to grow 29% in 2026 as investors prioritise larger deals

Indian FinTech investments increased 73% YoY in H1

The Indian FinTech market attracted $2.8bn across 94 deals in H1 2026.

That represents a 73% increase in funding and a 36% rise in deal activity compared to the $1.6bn raised across 69 deals in H1 2025.

Measured against 2025, which saw $4.4bn raised across 180 deals, H1 2026 has already accounted for 65% of that annual funding total within just the first half of the year.

Should the current pace be sustained across the second half of 2026, the sector would be on course to raise $5.6bn across 188 deals for the year.

The gap between those two figures is telling.

Funding is set to grow at a far faster rate than deal volumes, pointing to a maturing investment landscape where rising deal values and growing investor conviction are doing more of the heavy lifting than a simple increase in transaction activity.

article_title: Sprive raises $10m Series A to grow mortgage app
article_excerpt:
Sprive , an AI-driven consumer FinTech app that helps UK homeowners pay down their mortgages faster using everyday spending, has closed a $10m (£7.7m) Series A funding round to fuel its next stage of growth.

The round was backed by all of Sprive’s existing investors, including impact investor Ascension, broadcaster-owned Channel 4 Ventures and the Velocity EIS Technology Fund, alongside a group of new backers made up of consumer-focused investment firm Active Partners, Wealth Club, Rank Ventures and a number of angel investors with deep FinTech experience.

This latest raise takes the total amount Sprive has secured since launch to more than $15m. The company was founded in 2019 by Jinesh Vohra and Saad Hashim, two former Goldman Sachs bankers.

Sprive’s app allows users to put cashback earned from everyday shopping towards automatically overpaying their mortgage, helping them reduce interest costs and, in some cases, shorten the length of their loan. The app also tracks the mortgage market so customers can spot and move to cheaper deals.

So far, Sprive customers have cut their combined mortgage balances by £26m and stand to save more than £300m in interest as a result. The app now has 567,000 registered users and supports approximately £42bn worth of mortgages.

The company appeared on the BBC’s Dragons’ Den earlier this year, not long after closing a seed funding round in 2025. Since January 2025, Sprive’s revenue has grown more than 25-fold, while annualised spend processed through the app has increased 35 times over the same period to reach £328m. The business has also turned cash flow positive, with an annual revenue run rate now above £18m.

Sprive founder and CEO Jinesh Vohra said, “Given the cost-of-living crisis, with mortgage rates going through the roof, and borrowers being pushed into extending their mortgage terms in cases well into retirement, the ability to use your weekly shop to reduce your mortgage interest, and ultimately the term of the loan, is hugely appealing. Over time these payments can really add up.

“The fact that even in this tough investment market we managed to pull off this Series A raise is a huge vote of confidence, particularly as so many of our previous backers had no hesitation coming back for more. With these new funds under our belt, and having convincingly shown the viability of our product and our business, we are now in a strong position to step up our marketing push significantly and accelerate both customer acquisition and revenue growth.”

Ascension managing partner Jean de Fougerolles said, “Sprive is a great example of the businesses Ascension wants to back. Technology that changes the systems we all rely on in everyday life. For most people, a mortgage is the biggest financial commitment they’ll ever make, yet managing it is still surprisingly passive. Sprive is changing that, starting with mortgages and ultimately giving people a much easier way to take control of debt more broadly.

“Since we invested, the user base has grown 10x and last month 1.2% of mortgaged homeowners shopped through Sprive. With 8.5 million owner occupied mortgages in the UK, the headroom from here is significant. We’re excited about what that could become at scale: a platform that genuinely changes people’s relationship with debt and gives households more control over their money.”

article_title: APX Lending launches five-year digital asset-backed line of credit
article_excerpt:
APX Lending , a Canadian regulator-approved digital asset lending platform, has launched a five-year revolving line of credit that allows borrowers to use Bitcoin, Ethereum or a combination of both as collateral.

The facility allows eligible clients to establish a credit line once and then draw, repay and redraw funds as their needs change. Interest is charged only on the amount drawn, with no interest applied to unused credit.

The line of credit has no origination, prepayment or liquidation fees, while client collateral is covered by insurance of up to $250m. Annual interest rates range from 10.49% to 11.99%, depending on the outstanding balance.

Unlike APX’s existing fixed-term loans, which use either Bitcoin or Ethereum as collateral, the new facility allows both digital assets to be combined when calculating borrowing capacity.

For example, a borrower holding $200,000 in Bitcoin and $100,000 in Ethereum could use the combined $300,000 value to support a single facility. At a 60% loan-to-value ratio, this would provide up to $180,000 in borrowing capacity.

The available credit adjusts as the market value of the underlying digital assets changes. The launch expands APX’s digital asset lending offering, which includes fixed-term loans, revolving credit and a Lending-as-a-Service platform. The latter allows financial institutions and FinTechs to offer digital asset-backed lending products without building the underlying infrastructure themselves.

APX’s lending platform includes segregated cold-storage custody through BitGo Trust, with client assets not rehypothecated, alongside 24/7 on-chain collateral verification and automated risk management.

Its 90/85 Standard is designed to limit liquidations by reducing loan-to-value from 90% to 85%, rather than liquidating more collateral than required. The company’s security programme is supported by SOC 2-audited controls.

Founded in 2023, APX Lending provides digital asset-backed loans directly to borrowers and supports partner-branded lending products through its Lending-as-a-Service platform. The company combines technology, underwriting, capital, collateral management, servicing and compliance within its lending infrastructure.

APX said it was the first digital asset-backed lender approved by Canadian securities regulators and is registered with FINTRAC and FinCEN. The new Line of Credit is available to eligible borrowers in supported jurisdictions.

APX Lending founder and CEO Andrei Poliakov said, “At APX, we’re constantly asking how credit against digital assets can be made safer, more flexible and better for the borrower. A revolving line of credit is something our clients have asked us for repeatedly. You may need money for a purchase today, an investment three months from now and a business expense later in the year. You shouldn’t have to start a new loan every time. We built the Line of Credit so you establish the facility once, then draw, repay and redraw as your needs change.”

Poliakov added, “Digital assets do not need to live in a separate corner of finance. The people using them want the same things everyone else wants: access to financial products that give them greater freedom and control over their lives, confidence that their assets are safe, complete transparency into who they are dealing with, and a system they can rely on when they need it. We have spent years building APX around that idea, because trust is what ultimately brings these two worlds together.”

The launch comes as digital asset infrastructure providers continue to develop products designed to connect digital assets with more traditional financial services, including lending and credit.

article_title: Provable Markets lands Schwab-led Series B to scale Aurora
article_excerpt:
Provable Markets , the SEC-registered broker-dealer behind the Aurora Alternative Trading System for securities finance, has closed a Series B funding round led by Charles Schwab.

The size of the deal was not disclosed. The round saw The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) come on board as a new investor, alongside continued backing from existing shareholders including Dialectic Capital Management and Inkef, among others.

The capital injection arrives during a period of rapid expansion for the New York-based company. Its ATS has delivered record performance for four straight quarters, now handling upwards of $30 trillion in order volume each month.

The proceeds will be used to expand headcount across its commercial, product and engineering teams as the firm looks to keep pace with a fast-growing client base, while preserving its standard of client service and the scalability of its technology architecture. Additional funds will be channelled into new products and entry into new geographies, as well as deeper connectivity with core market infrastructure.

Provable Markets delivers pre-trade, execution and post-trade capabilities for both cleared and uncleared securities financing transactions through a fully cloud-native platform.

The business maintains links into central pillars of US capital markets plumbing, including DTCC’s clearing subsidiaries the National Securities Clearing Corporation (NSCC) and The Depository Trust Company (DTC), as well as the OCC and Tri-party Agents. At the heart of its SEC-regulated ATS sits a novel matching engine designed to boost trade automation on a neutral basis, with a smooth transition into its Aurora post-trade offering that removes longstanding bottlenecks front-end tools alone cannot address. Through access to NSCC’s SFT Clearing Service, clients can also achieve meaningful capital relief under Basel rules, generating additional ROI and widening their trading opportunities.

DTCC managing director, president, clearing & securities services Brian Steele said, “As demand for securities financing transactions continues to grow, market participants are increasingly seeking solutions that improve capital efficiency while reducing operational complexity. Provable Markets’ integration with DTCC’s SFT Clearing Service helps participants streamline post-trade processing and unlock the balance sheet benefits of central clearing. By supporting and connecting to innovative platforms like Provable, we are helping create a more efficient and scalable securities finance ecosystem that can support continued growth across the market.”

Provable Markets co-founder and CEO Matt Cohen said, “We started Provable Markets with the belief that modernizing securities finance is a market structure story that requires a foundational pipes and plumbing approach to rebuild core infrastructure from the bottom up. By maintaining that focus, we have been able to solve real problems for our clients that not only drive scaled automation, but also alleviate the increasingly acute pressures of operational and regulatory capital constraints. Charles Schwab and DTCC’s investment validate and fuels our next stage of growth to execute on our vision of becoming core market infrastructure for the rapidly expanding securities finance landscape and beyond.”

article_title: Finpilot raises $10m to put AI agents to work for institutions
article_excerpt:
Finpilot , an AI-native operating system built for institutional capital, has secured $10m in a Series A round as it aims to free long-term investment teams from time-consuming data work.

Lobby Capital led the investment, and Madrona, an existing backer of the company, also took part.

The firm is targeting a group of investors that collectively oversee vast sums. Universities, public pension schemes, foundations, hospital systems and family offices all employ teams responsible for billions of dollars held over long horizons.

The returns on this money support medical research, healthcare provision and retirement savings. Despite this, staff at these organisations spend much of their working week on information gathering, such as reviewing reports delivered in PDF format, extracting figures by hand and matching data across disconnected systems.

Finpilot centralises an institution’s knowledge in a single platform and deploys AI agents to act on it. The system maintains one reliable record of every holding and document an organisation has, maps the relationships between them, and runs agents that process incoming reports, refresh figures, produce analysis and monitor changes.

Each figure links back to its original source, and the agents hand matters to human staff whenever judgement is required.

Current users include Seattle Children’s, Children’s Health of Dallas, Hackensack Meridian Health, TIFF, Blue Cross Blue Shield and the Wyoming Retirement System.

The company plans to put the new capital towards expanding its workforce to support institutional clients, as well as broadening the product so its agents can tackle a wider range of client challenges. Finpilot is recruiting across client success, product, marketing, sales and engineering.

Finpilot founder and CEO Lakshay Chauhan said, “The teams managing this capital make decisions that fund research, health care and people’s retirements. Finpilot’s job is to take the routine work off their plate so they can focus on those decisions. This funding lets us grow our team and bring Finpilot to more institutions.”

The company also plans to expand beyond home warranty into extended warranty, original equipment manufacturer (OEM) warranty and equipment breakdown insurance.

Polygrade is targeting a part of the insurance market where claims systems have traditionally focused on recording information, routing tickets and tracking progress rather than carrying out the work needed to resolve a claim.

Its platform uses AI agents across five stages of the claims process: first notice of loss, pre-dispatch triage, authorisation, parts procurement and payment. Each agent operates within rules and limits set by the warranty provider, with cases outside those parameters referred to human staff.

The company is already working with warranty providers including Fidelity National Home Warranty, which uses the platform in production, and Cinch Home Services, which uses it for appliance dispatch triage and parts sourcing. Its supplier network includes Encompass, UED, Sibi and Marcone.

Polygrade’s software sits on top of existing warranty systems, using information from those platforms to determine and carry out actions across the claims process. article_title: mika raises €6m to make German tax advisers optional
article_excerpt:
mika , a Berlin-based vertical AI business building an alternative to the traditional tax firm, has secured €6m in seed funding to support its growth and continue developing its platform.

Pan-European investor Smedvig Ventures led the round. Basel family office Wecken & Cie. (Care4 AG) also took part, as did studiVZ co-founders Dennis Bemmann and Michael Brehm, limango founder Johannes Ditterich and Martina Pfeifer of encourageventures. Existing backers Keen Venture Partners and Dutch Founders Fund added to their holdings.

The company is not simply putting a digital layer on top of conventional tax advisory. Instead, it has designed accounting, tax and finance from scratch as an AI-native financial operating system for SMEs. For small GmbHs and UGs, the platform handles day-to-day bookkeeping, VAT returns, annual accounts and tax filings.

Germany is home to almost one million small incorporated firms, and every one of them must legally keep books, file VAT returns and produce annual accounts, mika said. Management could in principle do this work itself, but few attempt it. A single error can lead to back-taxes or fines, and the relevant rules sit across tax codes that are revised every year. As a result, nearly all small companies pay a tax adviser or firm to take care of it.

Founder and CEO Agnieszka Walorska has first-hand experience of this hurdle. She started her first business without entrepreneurial role models, family wealth or a network to rely on. For some founders, an annual adviser bill of a few thousand euros barely registers. For others, it stops a company from being launched at all, and it turns German bureaucracy into an obstacle for people without savings or connections.

At the core of mika is a proprietary AI-native general ledger built specifically for German accounting. Its AI interprets each receipt and payment, and it draws on different models depending on the job. Those models operate within domain knowledge and rules that mika has developed in-house. The system categorises and books transactions and tells users what each entry means, often with no manual input required. Qualified accountants on staff review the output and take over when a case is too complex for automation.

Users can also query their own financial data, either within mika or through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in assistants such as ChatGPT or Claude. Customers can upload confusing letters from the tax office and receive an immediate explanation along with next steps, and the AI chat answers questions about their accounts at any hour. mika does not yet provide individual tax advice, so it refers those cases to licensed tax advisers in its network.

The customer base has grown from about 250 GmbHs and UGs at the start of the year to more than 750 today. mika first served digital-first service firms such as agencies and consultancies. It has since expanded into SaaS, property and e-commerce, with retail and skilled trades the newest segments. Revenue has risen by more than 20% each month, and the company passed €1m in annual revenue in July 2026.

mika founder and CEO Agnieszka Walorska said, “The moment you start a GmbH in Germany, you’re told you need a tax adviser. It goes so far that some founders think it’s a legal requirement. To me, it’s obvious that this cannot be how it works. At mika, we use AI to tear down that barrier, so that your bank balance or the family you were born into no longer decides who gets to start a company.”

Smedvig Ventures principal Freddie Kalfayan said, “Nowhere else in Europe is accounting and tax as demanding or costly for small businesses as in Germany, where the two are so tightly linked that a single mistake carries straight through to the tax bill. It is the reason big international players never gained a foothold here, and why SMEs were left with no real alternative.
