article_title: Aurenity secures Great Hill investment for growth
article_excerpt:
Aurenity , a technology-enabled excess & surplus (E&S) managing general agent headquartered in Connecticut, has secured a strategic investment from Great Hill Partners, a private equity firm known for backing high-growth, disruptive businesses.

Agman, the founding investor behind Aurenity, along with the company’s leadership team, will hold on to a substantial share of their equity following the deal, the terms of which have not been disclosed.

The capital injection is intended to support the company’s next stage of growth by widening its underwriting bench, launching additional specialty insurance programmes, and continuing to build out the automation and systems infrastructure that underpins its scaling strategy.

Set up in 2022, Aurenity operates in the E&S insurance space and was established by a leadership group with extensive backgrounds in underwriting, operations and technology, including chief executive Nick Davies, chief underwriting officer Doug Trainor, chief operating officer Pat Safino, and EVPs Janet Beaver and Mark Fuderanan.

The company now runs six core E&S programmes covering primary, lead and excess casualty, alongside public entity, religious organisation and property lines, supported by EVPs Kevin Thommes and John Woie and a network of carrier partners.

Alongside the investment, Great Hill managing directors Matt Vettel and Nick Cayer, together with principal Bob Anderson, will take up seats on Aurenity’s board. Great Hill’s existing insurance portfolio spans payments network One Inc, employee benefit group captive provider Pareto, and Second Nature, which supplies tenant insurance to the single-family rental sector.

Ardea Partners and Oliver Wyman advised Great Hill on financial and actuarial matters, with Goodwin Procter LLP as legal counsel, while Evercore and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP advised Aurenity.

Aurenity Chief Executive Nick Davies said, “From the very beginning of Aurenity’s journey, our team has been focused on building a business that earns the trust of our carrier partners through disciplined risk selection.

It also allows us to further invest in AI to enable smarter and faster decisions while preserving the expertise-led underwriting culture that’s been central to our success. We look forward to partnering with Great Hill to capitalize on the significant opportunities ahead.”

Great Hill Principal Bob Anderson said, “Aurenity is exactly the kind of company we look for, with a high-caliber founding team, a track record of earning the trust of its carrier partners, and the technology infrastructure to continue scaling.

“The structural shift of complex risks into the E&S market and toward specialized underwriters gives us strong conviction that Aurenity is well-positioned for the near and long term, and we look forward to partnering with the Aurenity and Agman teams to build on what they have already accomplished.”

company_description: London-based AI platform helping professional investment teams scale portfolio research and management
article_title: Itoflow bags $2.5m to bring AI to portfolio management
article_excerpt:
Itoflow , the London-based AI platform helping professional investment teams scale portfolio research and management, has secured $2.5m in pre-seed funding.

The round was led by Balderton Capital, with participation from a group of angel investors including Cleo founder and CEO Barney Hussey-Yeo. Itoflow said the fresh capital would be used to grow its engineering and quantitative research teams, speed up product development and support its commercial and regulatory efforts.

Set up in 2026, Itoflow is developing AI agents that absorb how individual investment firms approach research, risk management and portfolio reviews. Rather than pushing a fixed investment philosophy, the platform converts each team’s existing methodology into governed, repeatable workflows capable of running continuously across asset classes such as equities, bonds, ETFs, commodities and digital assets, spanning global markets.

Because its agentic infrastructure was built in-house, the firm says it has closer oversight of the security and dependability of agents designed to keep operating for months or years as conditions shift.

Itoflow was founded by three graduates of the Indian Institute of Technology who bring together experience from leading finance and technology firms. Co-founder and chief executive Aditya Jha worked as a quantitative researcher for nine years at JPMorgan, RBC and, most recently, Tower Research Capital, where he led the mid-frequency trading business. His fellow founders have built large-scale infrastructure at Apple, Google and Microsoft and also carry quantitative research backgrounds from JPMorgan.

In pilots currently under way, investment teams describe in plain English the strategy, risk limits and review standards they want applied. Itoflow’s agents then use that guidance to run quantitative research and backtesting, keep portfolios under constant watch and flag material changes along with the evidence behind them. The aim is to let teams cover more investments, track more portfolios and apply their processes more consistently without having to substantially expand their quantitative research headcount.

Customers keep authority over how the system behaves, including deciding which actions and thresholds require sign-off from a person. Institutional clients also have the option of running Itoflow inside their own infrastructure, keeping sensitive data and proprietary strategies within their own environment. The company is currently piloting its technology with a number of hedge funds and family offices worldwide and is in discussions with exchanges, brokerages and financial-data providers.

Itoflow co-founder and CEO Aditya Jha said, “Our long-term research goal is to build self-improving investment agents. As an agent supports a mandate over months and years, it should learn which approaches continue to hold up, identify promising new signals and recognise when an apparent edge has decayed. Within the parameters set by each investment team, these agents could become a powerful tool for continuous discovery.”

Balderton Capital principal Sivesh Sukumar said, “The most sophisticated investment firms spend years building the systems and research teams needed to test ideas, manage risk and respond as markets change. Aditya and the team are changing the economics of that model, giving many more investment firms access to systematic capabilities that were previously too expensive and complex to build. They combine a rare depth of quantitative trading experience with the technical ability to deliver it at scale.”

article_excerpt:
Aisot Technologies AG , the Zurich-headquartered, ETH Zurich spin-off building AI-driven portfolio intelligence tools for institutional investors, has wrapped up a CHF2m extension to its seed round.

The additional capital came from a mix of existing backers and newcomers, including family offices and seasoned angel investors. Among the fresh names on the cap table is Felix Haldner, who previously held a partner role at Partners Group and once led the Swiss Funds & Asset Management Association (SFAMA) as its president.

Aisot Technologies builds AI-based tools aimed at asset and wealth managers, as well as family offices, with a focus on portfolio optimisation and risk management.

Founded in 2021 as an official spin-off from ETH Zurich, the firm is based in Zurich and works with a network of partners and staff spread across Europe, Asia and the US, drawing on specialists in artificial intelligence, natural language processing and financial mathematics.

article_title: Vero Security raises $11m as AI security jobs go unstaffed
article_excerpt:
Vero Security , a start-up developing a platform for AI Security Engineering, has closed an $11m seed round as large enterprises struggle to staff a responsibility that most still treat as a side duty.

TLV Partners led the investment, joined by GTM Capital, Maple Capital and a group of angel backers. Vero was established in 2025 and has already signed several Fortune 500 businesses as customers.

Alongside the raise, it is introducing AISecurityEngineering.org, an open community and knowledge hub offering practical field guides, workshops and the ASE credential track for practitioners shaping this new specialism.

The timing reflects a structural gap. Research by IANS and Artico Search showed that 65% of firms with revenues of $10bn or more had appointed someone to oversee AI security, yet just 18% had turned it into a standalone position. Elsewhere, the duty was bolted onto an existing leader’s workload. That person must keep pace as staff adopt AI tools and agents, link them to company systems and give them access to sensitive data, while vendors keep shipping models, plugins and integrations that can alter the risk profile of settings already in place.

Vero aims to absorb that ongoing workload. Security teams set the policy, and the platform converts it into enforced controls, refreshes them when vendors modify their products and escalates only the choices that need human judgement.

Its AI Runtime Governor examines supported prompts, tool calls and agent actions, applying approved rules at the point of execution. It can, for instance, prevent a coding agent from accessing secrets it does not need, halt agent behaviour that breaches policy and stop malicious skills or prompt injection from causing unauthorised activity, all without waiting for a manual review.

The platform plugs into the endpoint, identity, AI and security tools an organisation already uses, so staff install nothing new. It pairs continuous discovery with in-house security analysis and runtime enforcement, tracking AI tools, agents, linked systems, configurations and permissions. Teams decide which changes Vero may handle on its own; the software then applies controls, coordinates fixes with relevant owners, confirms completion and keeps safeguards current.

In one case, a new Fortune 1000 customer set a single rule restricting AI agent access to code repositories and code execution to developers. Within minutes, Vero turned that rule into more than 15 controls spanning coding agents, MCP servers, skills, identities and runtime actions.

GTM Capital backed the company after its network of Fortune 500 CIOs and CISOs tested Vero directly. Vero was started by CEO Elad Tessler, formerly head of product at Astrix Security, which Cisco bought in 2026, and CTO Daniel Meirov, the first hire at Sightfull, where he ran R&D and product. The pair previously co-led a cyber operations unit of over 100 people in Unit 8200. The capital will fund platform development, broader coverage of enterprise AI technologies and security workflows, and US go-to-market expansion.

Vero Security co-founder and CEO Elad Tessler said, “CISOs have seen enough dashboards and tables that tell their teams what’s wrong and leave the work to them. AI Security Engineering deserves a better operating model, designed for AI rather than borrowed from other areas of security.

“We’re working alongside the first generation of AI security leaders and building Vero around what they actually need: a platform that does the work, keeps protections current as AI changes, and brings them only the decisions that require human judgment.”

The company also opened offices this year in Paris, Madrid, Tokyo, Singapore and Dubai so it can support clients across their various locations.

article_title: Corma hits $1bn valuation with $125m Series A
article_excerpt:
Corma , an AI research lab building foundation models for defensive cybersecurity, has secured $125m in Series A funding at a $1bn valuation, only three months after revealing its seed round.

NEA led the investment, with participation from returning backers Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue. The latest raise takes the company’s total funding to $185m.

Corma’s $60m seed round , led by Sequoia, was announced in August.

The funding arrives as large organisations move quickly to integrate Corma’s model into their security operations amid mounting concern over AI-driven attacks. Since the company launched publicly, interest has climbed among Fortune 100, Fortune 500 and Fortune Global 500 businesses, which are handing a growing share of their security workload to Corma’s autonomous AI workforce. To keep pace, the firm has expanded its server capacity 24-fold.

At its August launch, Corma cautioned that AI was advancing far faster on the offensive side than the defensive one. That concern was borne out in October, when a series of serious vulnerabilities and breaches affecting widely used software, nicknamed “Black October,” left security teams under pressure and prompted warnings from governments in Washington, Tokyo and elsewhere.

According to Corma, the imbalance stems from the industry’s focus on coding. As leading labs pour resources into models that write software, those same models become more adept at spotting flaws, since vulnerabilities are effectively bugs. When combined with agents, they can now carry out exploits from start to finish. Defensive work outside code security, however, calls for different skills, such as sifting through large amounts of audit logs, security events and network flows, linking faint signals across systems over extended periods, and remaining consistent through long chains of decisions. Coding models were not designed for these tasks.

Corma trains foundation models specifically for this defensive work and deploys them as an AI workforce that sits alongside human security teams, operating within their existing tools and handling a broad range of security tasks.

Corma co-founder and CEO Alon Pluda said, “Cybersecurity is now a battle of intelligence against intelligence, and Black October made that impossible to ignore. Since we came out of stealth, demand from the world’s largest organizations has been overwhelming, and one of our hardest problems has been securing capacity fast enough to keep up with the demand

NEA partner Aaron Jacobson said, “Corma is building the intelligence layer that defensive security needs. As AI gives attackers an advantage, Corma’s combination of frontier AI research and deep cybersecurity expertise has the potential to help organizations defend against these threats at scale. Corma is the only company taking this on in a way that is scalable across organizations to prevent the next big cyberattack.”

Alongside the research, Bloomberg pointed to its recently launched BQuant Assistant, a conversational AI coding tool grounded in financial domain knowledge. Embedded within BQuant Desktop and BQuant Enterprise, the assistant lets Bloomberg Terminal subscribers use plain-language prompts to generate code, create dynamic applications and speed up their analysis of financial data.

Bloomberg head of go-to-market, BQuant Product James Jarvis said, “Technology is driving a shift in how traditional quant roles and techniques, which once demanded a highly specialised skillset, are opening up to a broader range of people with a variety of backgrounds and expertise, including those with arts degrees.

“This democratisation expands the effective talent pool dramatically and in turn drives innovation and extends the art of what is possible. However, while AI lowers the barrier to entry, it does not lower the barrier to knowing when and how to use these tools well. Judgement, critical thinking and human expertise are more crucial skills than ever.”

He added, “Domain-grounded coding tools like BQuant Assistant mean that a wider pool of financial users can now use natural language prompts to build apps and conduct quantitative research that previously was confined to a smaller subset of experts.

“With conversational AI now built directly into BQuant’s Python development environment, it has never been more accessible for users to test ideas, refine quantitative financial analyses, and build investment strategies, dashboards, and visualizations.”

It first confirms that a business genuinely exists and is actively trading, and it uses that confirmed identity to head off incorrect labelling and to push carriers to remove it. Verified firms can then layer on branded calling, so their name appears on outgoing calls.

The company positions itself as the default intelligence layer for participants across the global ETF ecosystem, spanning issuers, asset managers, liquidity providers, hedge funds and capital markets desks.

The business says recurring revenue has more than doubled annually over recent years. Its offering is split across three areas: programmatic data access via API, analytics delivered through a proprietary web application, and a workforce layer that combines verified ETF data with clients’ own sources for large-scale data operations. Beyond the US push, ETFBOOK plans to grow its presence in Hong Kong and expand its technology hub in Cracow, while broadening data coverage and enhancing its web application across more use cases.

article_excerpt:
Skyfire , an identity and payments infrastructure provider for AI agents, has expanded its partnership with Forter , a trust intelligence platform for digital commerce, to help merchants approve legitimate agent-driven purchases while limiting fraud risk. The integration incorporates Skyfire’s Know Your Agent (KYA) tokens into Forter’s fraud decisioning, as demand for agentic commerce continues to grow.

Under the integration, Forter uses Skyfire’s KYA protocol data within its Fraud Management for Agentic Commerce product, providing additional intelligence to assess purchases made by AI agents. The companies said the volume of agentic orders flowing through Forter’s network has more than quadrupled since August.

The partnership aims to address a growing challenge for online retailers. Traditional bot management systems are designed to identify and block automated activity, but legitimate AI agents shopping on behalf of consumers can trigger the same signals. This can lead merchants to reject genuine purchases, while fraudsters may attempt to disguise malicious activity as trusted agent traffic.

By distinguishing authorised AI agents from harmful automation, the integration is designed to improve checkout authorisation rates without introducing additional fraud exposure. The new identity signals are incorporated into existing risk data, meaning merchants do not need to change their checkout interfaces or add extra steps for legitimate agent-driven purchases.

Skyfire provides identity and payment infrastructure that enables AI agents to transact on their own. Its open KYA protocol supports verified identity for web access and account creation, tokenised credit cards, real-time micropayments and programmatic checkout across APIs, websites and marketplaces. The company is backed by investors including Evolution, DCVC, a16z CSX, Coinbase Ventures, Neuberger Berman and Brevan Howard Digital.

Forter provides trust intelligence and payments infrastructure for digital commerce, using AI and a global identity network to make real-time decisions across sign-up, checkout and returns. Its customers include Nordstrom, Instacart and Priceline, alongside almost one million businesses using its platform.

Jomashop general manager Osher Karnowsky said, “Our customers are starting to shop through agents, and we didn’t want to be the reason a legitimate purchase was declined. With Skyfire and Forter working together, we can better understand who the agent is, who sent it, and whether to trust the transaction. That clarity gives us confidence to support agentic buyers without introducing additional risk to the business.”

Forter chief technology and product officer Eran Vanounou added, “Agentic commerce fails if retailers can’t tell the difference between an authorised buyer and a script trying to look like one. Leveraging Forter and Skyfire lets businesses confidently validate both the identity of the AI agent and the trustworthiness of the underlying consumer. We are empowering digital commerce leaders to welcome AI-driven purchases while protecting their bottom line from fraud.”

Skyfire co-founder and head of product Craig DeWitt also commented, “AI agents represent an entirely new channel for commerce, but today’s fraud and security systems weren’t built to recognise them. By integrating Skyfire’s Know Your Agent (KYA) identity directly into Forter’s fraud decisioning, we’re giving merchants the ability to distinguish trusted, authorised agents from malicious bots. This is a critical step toward making agentic commerce as secure, seamless, and scalable as traditional online shopping.”

article_title: Zaria bags $5.2m to scale structured finance infrastructure
article_excerpt:
Zaria Systems , a provider of real-time infrastructure for mark-to-market credit and structured finance, has secured $5.2m in seed capital to expand its fiduciary platform.

Lightspeed Venture Partners led the round. The fresh capital will help Zaria grow its existing services and back its bid to establish Zaria National Trust Bank (ZNTB). The company recently filed an application for this charter with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). ZNTB is planned as a special-purpose national bank whose activities would be restricted to trust company operations and associated functions.

The raise arrives as structured finance faces pressure to move beyond its traditional reliance on periodic, batch-driven reviews of collateral. Growth in lending backed by securities, digital assets and tokenised instruments is increasing demand for continuous monitoring and automated margin calls.

Zaria aims to meet that need by delivering loan servicing, backup servicing, collateral management and agency services to participants in structured finance markets and to lenders working with digital asset collateral. Should the OCC approve the charter, Zaria intends to bring these offerings together under one federally regulated trustee. Deal stakeholders would then deal with a single regulated counterparty throughout a transaction, instead of coordinating a patchwork of separate providers.

Zaria builds infrastructure designed for modern structured finance. Through the proposed trust bank, it plans to provide corporate trustee and agency services, loan servicing, collateral management and backup servicing to banks, lenders and asset managers active in both traditional and digital asset markets.

Zaria co-founder and CEO Emily Barron said, “This financing lets us accelerate growth and scale our existing services.

“We’re currently running servicing, backup servicing, collateral management, and agency infrastructure for structured finance and digital asset-backed loans. This investment lets us grow that team, extend the technology, and build on to a strong foundation.”

Lightspeed Venture Partners partner, Fintech, Aaron Frank said, “Zaria has already built real traction with structured finance and digital asset-backed lenders.

“Emily and her team have combined deep structured finance expertise with the technical rigor to build that infrastructure from the ground up, and we’re proud to have been able to back them from the earliest days.”

article_title: SAP-backed Tereina launches agentic B2B payments platform
article_excerpt:
Tereina , a Palo Alto-based financial services company backed by SAP , has launched a platform designed to let businesses automate payments across traditional banking and digital currency networks.

The company’s technology enables finance teams to initiate, optimise and execute payments from within the enterprise software they already use, with transactions able to settle in either fiat currencies or digital assets.

SAP customers can access the service through SAP Pay, which supports supplier, incoming, employee and intracompany payments. Other business applications can connect to Tereina’s payment infrastructure through APIs.

Tereina said the platform is designed to support a shift towards agentic payments, where AI agents can recommend and ultimately execute transactions on behalf of businesses.

The company is also positioning stablecoins as an alternative settlement method for corporate payments, citing their ability to facilitate 24/7 cross-border transfers. Its platform can route transactions across fiat and stablecoin networks based on the payment requirements, while giving suppliers and customers options over how they send and receive funds.

Tereina said its platform is intended to reduce the operational friction involved in corporate payments by automating payment routing and removing manual intervention. The company is targeting a 25% reduction in total cost of ownership compared with what businesses currently spend on average.

It also claims that automated payment processes can reduce the number of manual exception points in the payment journey, while allowing businesses to retain control over payment timing and approvals.

The company said its technology allows businesses to access digital currencies, starting with stablecoins and with tokenised deposits planned for a later stage, without requiring additional systems or specialist expertise.

Tereina also claims the platform can reduce settlement and reconciliation times, potentially allowing businesses to access working capital more quickly.

Tereina is led by CEO Cedric Bru and describes its model as “Embedded Payments to Ignite Commerce” (EPIC). The company provides payment infrastructure across traditional and digital rails, with agentic capabilities embedded into business applications.

Vladimir Fedoroff, CFO at Winncom Technologies, said, “Winncom has dealt with complicated payments and supplier processes throughout our company’s history. Tereina brings us the future of payments, simplifying those processes and making our money move exactly when we need it, smarter than ever.”

Cedric Bru, CEO at Tereina, said, “Total B2B payment volume is expected to exceed $200 trillion by 2030, fueling even faster global commerce. Businesses deserve the best of what’s possible today and what’s coming next. We’re proud to bring our customers best-in-class financial services alongside our technology, banking, issuing, and fintech partners – starting with the future of payments: embedded, digital, and agentic. Tereina is making that future available now.”

article_title: Spiko raises $90m Series B to make cash earn by default
article_excerpt:
Spiko , an issuer of tokenised cash funds, has secured $90m in a Series B round as it looks to give businesses of all sizes access to yield on idle money.

New Enterprise Associates (NEA) led the investment, joined by Index Ventures, Bpifrance, Speedinvest, Flourish Ventures, Shapers, White Star Capital, Blockwall, Frst, EQNX, Mirana Ventures and Wintermute Ventures. A number of high-profile angel investors also took part, among them Axel Weber, who previously served as president of the Bundesbank, along with the founders of Qonto. The latest raise lifts the total capital Spiko has secured to $120m.

The company will direct the fresh capital towards three priorities: rolling out additional funds, expanding into new markets and increasing its headcount. Alongside its London and Paris hubs, Spiko is assembling local teams in Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and the Nordics.

According to the firm, roughly $50tn sits in cash and deposits across Europe and the US, with the majority generating minimal or no returns. With central bank rates spanning approximately 2.5% in the eurozone to nearly 4% in the US, each percentage point of yield on that pool equates to $500bn annually. While banks and major institutions capture these returns through wholesale markets, smaller firms, entrepreneurs, non-profits and smaller financial institutions typically miss out.

Although money market funds have long offered a route to returns on cash, Spiko notes they have never achieved mainstream adoption beyond the US. The company builds its own suite of regulated cash funds, ranging from intraday liquidity products to term offerings, available in euros, dollars, sterling and Swiss francs. Businesses can use them through desktop and mobile apps, while other companies and financial platforms can integrate them into their own services via an API. Its client base spans startups, scale-ups, research institutes, public bodies, VC funds and medical practices.

Because its funds are issued onchain, Spiko says it has overtaken BlackRock and Franklin Templeton to become the largest tokenised cash fund issuer.

The company now manages $2.7bn in assets across four currencies and several public blockchains, having grown AUM more than fivefold over the last year. Over 10,000 businesses and individuals in more than 25 jurisdictions use its services.

Spiko co-founder and CEO Paul-Adrien Hyppolite said, “Every person and every organization holds cash, yet whether it earns anything still depends on who you are and how much you have. Yield should be universal. Our ambition is to make all cash earn by default, around the clock.”

NEA managing director and head of Europe Philip Chopin said, “We looked at dozens of companies solving pieces of this problem. We believe Spiko is the only one that’s solved the regulatory piece and the product piece at the same time. Paul-Adrien and Antoine are building the default home for cash. Money market funds are where trust is earned, and the same model extends naturally to new markets and new products.”

company_description: open finance platform focused on institutional assets
article_title: Plume expands onchain fixed income with Fidelity-backed vault
article_excerpt:
Plume, an open finance platform focused on institutional assets, has launched its nBND vault, offering investors access to a tokenised structure backed primarily by the Fidelity Total Bond ETF (FBND).

The launch gives onchain investors exposure to a broader mix of fixed income assets through Fidelity’s actively managed bond fund. FBND invests primarily across investment-grade, high-yield and emerging markets debt, moving beyond the short-duration government securities that have dominated tokenised fixed income to date.

Plume said the product is intended to support the development of a broader onchain bond market rather than simply provide another source of yield. The company believes blockchain-based capital markets will need access to a wider selection of established financial assets if they are to develop beyond their current use cases.

The firm highlighted the expansion of tokenised US Treasuries as evidence of growing demand for onchain fixed income. The market increased from $12bn in April 2026 to $15bn by June, according to Plume. However, the company noted that this remains a small portion of the global fixed income market, which it puts at more than $100tn.

Plume said bringing more traditional financial assets onto blockchain networks will require greater collaboration between digital asset firms and established financial institutions. It argues that digital asset native infrastructure can provide programmability and accessibility, while traditional financial firms bring decades of experience managing investment products and assets.

The company said institutional interest in established assets that generate yield onchain is already evident, with nBND intended to build on that demand by introducing greater duration and active management to the tokenised fixed income market.

Plume describes itself as an institutional open finance platform that serves more than half of real-world asset holders. Its platform is designed to move institutional assets from closed financial systems into open and programmable markets accessible globally.

Its Plume Nest Vaults protocol provides compliant, non-custodial access to assets from financial firms including Apollo, WisdomTree and Hamilton Lane.

Plume’s backers include Apollo Global Management, Galaxy Digital and Brevan Howard. The company also has an SEC transfer-agent registration through Kimber Transfer Agency LLC.

Plume CEO and co-founder Chris Yin said, “While the onchain fixed income market was originally concentrated in short-duration Treasuries and money market equivalents, these are the starting points, not the destination. Institutional allocators want duration, and active management, the same building blocks they use offchain.”

Fidelity Investments head of digital asset management Cynthia Lo Bessette said, “As tokenised assets and on-chain applications become more integrated into mainstream market infrastructure, a collaborative ecosystem is essential to expanding investment access. We’re excited to collaborate with Plume to bring financial products on-chain, providing a broader set of investors with access to greater programmability to build custom portfolios, alongside investment solutions that unlock new forms of collateral utility and access to capital.”

company_description: New York-based provider of infrastructure for stablecoins and tokenised money
article_title: HIFI lands $37m to rebuild the plumbing of tokenised money
article_excerpt:
HIFI , the New York-based provider of infrastructure for stablecoins and tokenised money, has secured $37m in Series A funding as it pushes beyond payments into cards and capital markets.

Left Lane Capital led the round, and Left Lane’s Matt Miller will take a seat on the HIFI board. The company said it selected the investor for its track record of supporting founders who tackle difficult problems in complicated markets, as well as for the hands-on operational help it gives firms as they scale.

HIFI plans to put the capital to work in three areas. It intends to secure further regulatory licences so that a larger share of its technology stack operates directly under its own authorisation. It will expand headcount in New York and in a limited number of overseas markets. It also aims to move its product beyond payments into cards and capital markets, where issues around custody and control remain unresolved and, according to the company, carry the greatest value for whoever solves them. The firm is currently recruiting across engineering, compliance and go-to-market roles.

The business now handles upwards of $7bn in annual volume, and activity among its existing clients has risen more than fourfold across the last six months. Firms building on HIFI have collectively brought over 10,000 businesses and 200,000 individuals onto their platforms.

HIFI has also been active with institutional players. In July, its platform took part in DTCC’s tokenised repo pilot. It additionally supported a live tokenised repo transaction on Tradeweb between DRW and Marex, which settled on the Canton Network using USDCx for the cash leg. On the payments side, developers can combine HIFI’s stablecoin settlement with Visa Direct, including newly launched stablecoin push-to-card payouts, while an integration with the Circle Payments Network gives clients additional settlement routes.

Founded in New York in 2022 by Mo Afifi and a co-founder, HIFI lets companies design new financial products built on stablecoins and tokenised money.

The company argues that stablecoins have shifted from a parking place for dollars between crypto trades into a form of money that moves globally within seconds, settles around the clock and can be embedded in software.

More than $250bn now circulates as stablecoins, and the GENIUS Act established a federal legal framework for payment stablecoins in July 2025. HIFI expects Treasuries, money market funds, receivables, credit and, over time, most securities to follow dollars onto tokenised rails, allowing cash and assets to interact directly rather than through layers of intermediaries reconciling records after the fact.

It likened the current moment to 1968, when the New York Stock Exchange shut on Wednesdays so back offices could clear paperwork, a problem eventually fixed by rebuilding the infrastructure beneath trading. HIFI believes the firms that progress fastest will start where tokenised money already functions, such as payments, treasury and collateral, and expand from there.

article_title: Nasdaq deepens Payward tie-up with $100m investment
article_excerpt:
Payward , the parent company of Kraken, has widened its relationship with Nasdaq through a $100m investment from Nasdaq Ventures, continued work on a shared tokenisation framework and a new market surveillance agreement.

Nasdaq Ventures, the exchange group’s strategic investment arm, backs technologies and market infrastructure that it views as central to the long-term development of global capital markets, and its stake in Payward is being positioned as a reflection of the strategic depth of the two firms’ joint work. The tie-up is designed to support the continued build-out of tokenised market infrastructure while keeping an issuer-focused model rooted in governance, regulatory compliance and market integrity. Digital Liquidity Networks (DLN), Nasdaq’s markets division tasked with building always-on infrastructure for the movement of capital, assets and liquidity, is leading the collaboration from Nasdaq’s side.

The two companies will keep building out the operational and commercial groundwork behind Nasdaq Equity Tokens (NETs), with a launch targeted for the second quarter of 2027. Nasdaq had earlier this year unveiled its intention to create NETs, alongside a framework linking them to Payward’s xStocks ecosystem, laying the groundwork for tokenised equities to circulate across varied market settings without compromising the rights and protections due to issuers and investors. The upcoming phase of the partnership is set to focus on the global distribution, trading and post-trade functions required to widen adoption of tokenised equities.

Alongside this, Payward will bring in Nasdaq’s surveillance technology across its trading venues, spanning crypto, equities, tokenised equities, futures and options, broadening the alliance to cover tools aimed at protecting market integrity and investor trust. The two firms describe the goal as pairing contemporary tokenised infrastructure with safeguards that can support transparent, trusted markets at scale.

Nasdaq frames the next stage of market development as reliant on infrastructure that lets assets travel across markets more fluidly, without eroding the protections and standards participants rely on, and positions its work with Payward as central to delivering that at scale.

Nasdaq President Tal Cohen said, “The next era of market evolution will be defined by how efficiently and seamlessly capital and assets move across the financial system with durable, high-integrity liquidity. Expanding our relationship with Payward reflects our conviction that Kraken can play an important role in building the infrastructure that supports this evolution. Our partnership advances our work on Nasdaq Equity Tokens and helps build a more connected financial system while preserving the trust, transparency and integrity that underpin capital formation.”

Payward Co-CEO Arjun Sethi said, “More than $2 trillion of stock trades run through the U.S. clearing system every day. Buys and sells net down by about 98 percent, and the clearing house holds $10 billion to $20 billion of collateral against what is left while it waits a day to settle. Cutting that wait from two days to one in 2024 released $3 billion. On-chain settlement removes the wait. The next phase of the collaboration is planned to advance Nasdaq Equity Tokens onto rails that do not close, with shareholder rights intact.”

company_description: digital asset wallet and payment card provider
article_title: Bitget Wallet shifts card cashback towards digital assets
article_excerpt:
Bitget Wallet , a digital asset wallet and payment card provider, has launched a new rewards scheme that lets cardholders receive up to 3% cashback in Bitcoin, gold, tokenised US stocks, ETFs or USDC.

The new Assetback programme replaces traditional cash rewards with assets that users can select based on their preferences. The scheme is available to eligible Bitget Wallet Card users across the UK, Europe, Asia, Latin America and other supported markets.

Under the programme, cardholders receive a base cashback rate of 2%, while new users and those meeting a monthly spending threshold can unlock a 3% “Booster” rate. The higher rate applies for the month in which the threshold is reached and the following calendar month.

Rewards are calculated and applied automatically, meaning users do not need to open a separate brokerage account or manually invest their cashback. The programme offers seven reward options: Bitcoin, tokenised gold, Nvidia, Tesla, Google, the S&P 500 and USDC. Tokenised stock and ETF exposure is provided through xStocks.

Users can change their selected reward asset once a month through their card settings, although changes only apply to future cashback. USDC rewards are credited directly to the card balance, while other assets are transferred to a Rewards Account once a user has accumulated at least 1 USDC worth of rewards.

Redemptions become available seven days after the qualifying transaction. Rewards remain subject to monthly caps, merchant category exclusions and risk controls, while refunded, reversed or cancelled transactions are excluded from the programme.

The launch adds another layer of investment functionality to Bitget Wallet Card, which allows users to top up with digital assets including USDT and USDC and spend through merchants accepting Visa or Mastercard. The card can also be linked to Apple Pay, Google Pay and other supported payment services.

Bitget Wallet Card is currently available across the UK and EEA, alongside selected markets in Latin America, APAC, South Asia, South Africa and China. The move comes as digital asset-linked card payments continue to grow. Monthly transaction volume across the sector reached $656m in May 2026, more than double the $271m recorded in May 2025, while cumulative volume has surpassed $7.8bn.

Bitget Wallet said its own card spending nearly tripled during the first half of 2026, with usage increasingly resembling traditional consumer payment behaviour. The company is also planning further regional campaigns and a user-generated content campaign following the launch. Details are expected to be announced through its social channels.

article_excerpt:
Centricity raises Rs 280 Cr in Series A led by SMBC Asia Rising Fund
Centricity will use this funding for strengthening tech stack, expanding distribution network and deepen market reach.
Centricity, a technology led wealth management firm, has raised Rs 280 crore in a Series A round of funding led by SMBC Asia Rising Fund.
The round also saw participation from existing investors such as Lightspeed India Partners, Burman Family Office, RAAY Investments (Amit Patni Family Office), and Kuldeep Rathi (Ask Automotives Ltd.) Family Office, Stride Venture, and Innoven Capital, along with other returning investors.
According to a statement, the funding will be deployed towards strengthening the company's proprietary technology stack, expanding its B2B2C wealth distribution platform, accelerating the growth of its private wealth and NRI global private client businesses, and deepening its presence across domestic and international markets.
Founded in 2022 by seasoned private bankers, Centricity operates across multiple business verticals, including its partner-driven B2B2C distribution platform One Digital, Invictus Private Wealth, and NRI Global Private client business.
On the fund raise, Centricity Founder & CEO Manu Awasthy said, “This investment is a defining endorsement of Centricity's vision, business model, and execution. After the early backing of Lightspeed, the partnership with SMBC's venture capital arm is another strong vote of confidence in what we have built in just three years.”
Centricity now manages more than Rs 15,000 crore in Assets Under Management (AUM), with 60% of ARR assets, serves a network of over 20,000 partners, supports more than one lakh investors, works with over 250 family offices, and has built a workforce of 800+ professionals. The firm said it is on track to surpass Rs 150 crore in revenue in FY27 and claimed that over the past year alone, the business has recorded nearly 200% growth, reflecting increasing adoption of technology-enabled wealth advisory across both advisor and client segments.
This wealth management firm said unlike traditional private wealth models that are often closely aligned with proprietary product distribution, Centricity has built an advisor/distributor -first platform designed around transparency and open architecture.

article_title: Trustly lands $60m to turn payments into AI intelligence
article_excerpt:
Trustly, the Stockholm-headquartered Pay by Bank specialist, has secured $60m in new capital as it moves to reposition payment data as a source of commercial intelligence for the merchants it serves.
According to FinSMEs, Nordic Capital, Alfvén & Didrikson and BlackRock all participated in the round. The Swedish firm plans to channel the money into building new AI-powered products designed to extract insight from transaction flows.
Its stated aim is to give businesses sharper tools for attracting customers, keeping them engaged over a longer period and anticipating risk before it materialises.
The raise marks a notable strategic direction for the company. Rather than treating a payment as the end point of a transaction, Trustly intends to use the data generated at checkout as a lever for growth and protection, a shift that could change how merchants evaluate their payment providers.
Trustly offers account-to-account payments built on Open Banking infrastructure, allowing consumers to pay directly from their bank accounts with speed and security, in real time. Its network links more than 9,000 merchants with in excess of 650 million consumers, drawing on connections to 12,000 banks across upwards of 30 markets. Well-known names including PayPal, Virgin Media O2 and Booking.com count among its partners.
The business was established in 2008 and is run by CEO Johan Tjärnberg. During 2025, it handled more than $100bn in payment volume.
On the regulatory front, Trustly is overseen by several authorities across its key markets. These include Sweden’s Financial Supervisory Authority, the Financial Conduct Authority in the UK, France’s ACPR and state-level regulators in the US.

article_title: Zepto to raise Rs 1,000 cr in pre-IPO round at USD 4.5 bn valuation; public listing delayed
article_excerpt:
Zepto to raise Rs 1,000 Cr in pre-IPO round at $4.5B valuation; public listing delayed
The capital infusion is expected to be led primarily by domestic investors to raise Indian shareholding in the company, which currently stands at around 40%.
Quick-commerce unicorn Zepto is set to raise approximately Rs 1,000 crore in a pre-IPO funding round at a valuation of around $4.5 billion, and has pushed back its initial public offering timeline, sources privy to the matter said.
The capital infusion is expected to be led primarily by domestic investors to raise Indian shareholding in the company, which currently stands at around 40%.
Zepto’s IPO, earlier targeted for July 2026, is held off for the time being, sources said.
A mail sent to Zepto did not elicit any response.
The $4.5 billion valuation marks a moderation from $7 billion valuation Zepto commanded in October 2025, when it raised $450 million in a funding round led by the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS).
Founded by Stanford University dropouts Aadit Palicha and Kaivalya Vohra, Zepto filed its preliminary IPO papers in December 2025 through the confidential pre-filing route with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi).
According to the updated draft papers filed with markets regulator Sebi, Zepto is set to raise Rs 8,010 crore through a fresh issue of shares as part of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
Along with the fresh issue, there will be an offer for sale (OFS) of 11.35 crore equity shares by existing shareholders.
If the listing goes through, Zepto will join Eternal and Swiggy on the stock exchanges, competing directly with their respective quick-commerce arms, Blinkit and Instamart.
For FY26, Zepto reported revenue from operations of Rs 22,624 crore and net receivables value (NRV) of Rs 24,816 crore.
The company processed an average of 17.5 lakh orders per day during the year and had 1,139 stores as of March 31, 2026. Its annual transacting user base stood at nearly 48 million.
During the quarter ended March 2026, Zepto handled around 210 million orders, translating into about 23.3 lakh orders per day.

company_description: Brahma AI is expanding beyond its existing media and entertainment focus into sports, healthcare, and advertising, while developing new AI applications.
article_title: Brahma AI raises $150M led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management
article_excerpt:
Brahma AI raises $150M led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management
Brahma AI is expanding beyond its existing media and entertainment focus into sports, healthcare, and advertising, while developing new AI applications.
Enterprise AI company Brahma AI has raised $150 million in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, as it looks to expand its AI platform across media and entertainment, sports, healthcare, and advertising.
Multiples invested $100 million through the issuance of preferred shares, while Brahma AI has received a further $100 million in investor interest.
The company works with global customers such as Warner Bros, the NBA, and Mayo Clinic. Its strategic distribution partners include Google, Hakuhodo, and DNEG.
Founded and led by Prabhu Narasimhan, Brahma AI brings together technology and capabilities developed across DNEG, Metaphysic, and Prime Focus Technologies. Narasimhan serves as Founder and CEO, while Jo Plaete, Co-founder and CTO, heads the company's technology and R&D division.
The company's AI-native platform comprises Brahma AI Core and Brahma AI Studio. Its technology combines enterprise content intelligence and management with AI creation capabilities spanning visual AI, digital humans, voice, and multilingual performance.
"Brahma AI is reimagining the content supply chain in the age of AI. Our investment is anchored in the belief that every enterprise is becoming a content enterprise. Multiples Private Equity will be an active partner as the company navigates the next phase of growth through investments in R&D, global market expansion, and talent & process build-out,” said Renuka Ramnath, Founder, MD & CEO of Multiples.
Brahma AI plans to expand its technology into new use cases and is working towards interactive digital humans. The company is also developing its platform to be model agnostic, while focusing on security, authenticity, and provenance.
“We are close to launching interactive digital humans, we are building Brahma AI to be model agnostic, and we are taking our technology into entirely new use cases. And security, authenticity and provenance are such an important part of what we are building," said Prabhu Narasimhan, Founder & CEO of Brahma AI.

company_description: Cold-chain logistics provider Celcius Logistics is in advanced talks to raise ₹100 Cr in a Pre-Series C funding round from existing investors IvyCap Ventures, Omnivore, and Eurazeo, alongside new investor wealthtech plat
article_title: Exclusive: Celcius Logistics Eyes ₹100 Cr To Expand Cold Chain Network
article_excerpt:
Cold-chain logistics provider Celcius Logistics is in advanced talks to raise ₹100 Cr in a Pre-Series C funding round from existing investors IvyCap Ventures, Omnivore, and Eurazeo, alongside new investor wealthtech platform Centricity, sources told Inc42. The proposed round is expected to comprise equity and debt, the sources said. The startup plans to use the capital to strengthen its technology infrastructure, expand its presence across India, and scale its pharma and hyperlocal logistics businesses, the sources added.

Celcius is also looking to raise a Series C funding round by mid-2027.

Inc42 has reached out to Celcius for comments on the development. The story will be updated on receiving a response. The funding talks follow Celcius’ ₹250 Cr Series B round in May 2025 , which comprised equity and debt. Eurazeo and Omnivore co-led the equity component, with participation from IvyCap Ventures.

At the time, Celcius said it would use the debt to meet working capital requirements, while the equity would support expansion into Tier III and IV markets and industries such as pharmaceuticals.

Founded in 2020 by Swarup Bose, Rajneesh Raman, and Arbind Jain, Celcius operates a digital platform that connects shippers with transporters and cold storage providers. It centralises bookings and shipment data for temperature-controlled transportation and storage. The startup serves businesses across quick commerce, ecommerce, agriculture, and healthcare, transporting temperature-sensitive products such as pharmaceuticals and fresh produce.

Its specialised verticals include pharma-focused Celcius+ and Celcius Green, which provides refrigerated last-mile deliveries using electric vehicles.

Celcius has over 50 distribution hubs and a presence in more than 200 additional cities over the preceding year. The startup competes with cold-chain logistics players including Indicold and JustDeliveries, both of which raised funding in 2024. Celcius’ expansion comes amid gaps in India’s cold-chain infrastructure. According to a FICCI–Grant Thornton Bharat report , India had 40.22 Mn tonnes of cold storage capacity across 8,815 facilities by June 2025, with about three-quarters of the capacity used for potatoes. According to the report, India loses between 17 Mn and 47 Mn tonnes of horticultural, dairy, meat, poultry, and fish products annually across the value chain. It identified gaps in packhouses, pre-cooling facilities, refrigerated transport, and ripening chambers.

company_description: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capit
article_title: PowerUp Money Raises $10 Mn To Expand Wealth Management Services
article_excerpt:
Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC.

The startup plans to use the capital to expand its AI-led wealth management offerings, scale its managed advisory business and develop personalised financial planning solutions for Indian investors.

“We started by making high-quality investment advice accessible to every Indian. Today, AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally and at a fraction of traditional costs. A significant portion of this investment will go towards building an AI-powered wealth manager that brings personalised financial planning and ongoing portfolio guidance to every Indian,” PowerUp’s founder and CEO Prateek Jindal said.

Jindal, who has also cofounded fintech major Uni Cards, launched PowerUp in 2025 to help customers manage their mutual fund portfolios. It claims to have over 15 Lakh customers, who track mutual fund portfolios worth over ₹2.5 Lakh Cr on its platform. Its mutual fund advisory subscription, PowerUp Elite, has over 1 Lakh paid members.

Beyond mutual funds, the startup is now looking to combine investment advice, managed wealth services and digital advisory, becoming a full-stack financial planning platform in essence.

The first step towards its new avatar has now come with the launch of its end-to-end digital wealth advisory offering, Elite Prime. The service includes an AI wealth coach and personal assistant, considers users’ financial goals, risk profiles and existing portfolios while helping them manage their portfolios and supporting their investment decisions.

It is also seeking to scale up its managed wealth advisory offering, Infinite, to a broader customer base.

Aimed at investors seeking more hands-on financial support, Infinite combines personalised financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation, goal-based strategies, ongoing portfolio management and dedicated adviser support.

PowerUp claims that Infinite has scaled to nearly ₹500 Cr in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch.

company_description: Wealthtech startup Zomint has raised ₹36 Cr (about $3.7 Mn) in a seed funding round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners.
article_title: Zomint Raises ₹36 Cr To Scale Wealth Management Platform
article_excerpt:
Wealthtech startup Zomint has raised ₹36 Cr (about $3.7 Mn) in a seed funding round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners.

The startup plans to use the fresh capital to strengthen its technology and investment capabilities, expand its team of wealth and investment experts, and grow its content-led distribution across new formats and regional languages.

Founded in 2025 by Aman Mittal and Shavir Bansal, Zomint is a wealth management platform targeting working professionals and families building long-term wealth. It pairs customers with dedicated wealth experts, supported by investment research and AI tools.

Mittal, the startup’s CEO, previously held product leadership roles at Flipkart and Pine Labs. Bansal, its COO, also founded personal finance content platform Bekifaayati, which claims to have more than 50 Lakh subscribers.

Zomint allows customers to start with a monthly SIP of ₹25,000 or a lump sum investment of ₹5 Lakh, positioning its services beyond the high-net-worth individuals (HNIs) traditionally served by wealth managers.

The platform provides a dashboard to track investments, while its experts review portfolios and recommend actions based on customers’ goals and fund performance. Its technology brings together portfolio information, financial goals, past conversations, and investment research to flag issues and track agreed actions. According to its website, Zomint operates as an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor. Its listed offerings span equity, debt, hybrid, gold and silver, and global funds, including GIFT City funds. The startup said it plans to broaden its services beyond domestic mutual funds to address other investment and financial needs. Zomint claims to have acquired its entire customer base organically, led by Bekifaayati’s presence on YouTube and Instagram, without spending on paid customer acquisition.

The startup said it has retained 97% of its clients since launch, while nearly one in three clients made additional investments through the platform within three months of their initial engagement. Each relationship manager currently serves more than 250 families, supported by investment specialists and AI tools, it added.

The fundraise comes amid investor interest in startups offering wealth management, investment research, and portfolio tools. The broader segment includes platforms such as Centricity, Novelty Wealth, Tijori, and StockGro, although their offerings and target customers differ.

Inc42 reported yesterday that IPO-bound StockGro has raised ₹110 Cr as part of its ongoing Series B round. This follows earlier tranches comprising ₹150 Cr from Param Capital founder Mukul Agarwal and $13 Mn from existing investor BITKRAFT Ventures.

company_description: Wealthtech startup Centricity has raised ₹280 Cr (around $29 Mn) in a funding round led by SMBC Asia Rising Fund, comprising ₹230 Cr in equity and ₹50 Cr in venture debt.
article_title: Centricity Raises ₹280 Cr To Expand Wealthtech Platform, NRI Business
article_excerpt:
Wealthtech startup Centricity has raised ₹280 Cr (around $29 Mn) in a funding round led by SMBC Asia Rising Fund, comprising ₹230 Cr in equity and ₹50 Cr in venture debt. The round valued the startup at around ₹1,800 Cr (about $190 Mn)

Existing investors Lightspeed India Partners, the Burman Family Office, RAAY Investments (Amit Patni Family Office), the Kuldeep Rathi Family Office (Ask Automotives Ltd), Stride Ventures, and Innoven Capital also participated in the round.

The Gurugram-based startup plans to use the fresh capital to strengthen its technology stack and expand its B2B2C wealth-distribution platform. It will also deploy the funds to grow its private wealth and NRI client businesses and deepen its presence in India and overseas.

Founded in 2022 by Manu Awasthy, Aditya Shankar, Gaurav Tiwari, Manish Sharma, and Pushpendra Singh, Centricity offers wealth management and investment solutions to independent financial advisers, retail investors, HNIs, UHNIs, and family offices.

Its platform automates processes such as portfolio consolidation, reporting, risk analytics, and investment monitoring for financial advisers and family offices.

Centricity operates multiple business verticals, including its partner-led B2B2C distribution platform One Digital, Invictus Private Wealth, and its Global Private Client business for NRIs.

The startup is expanding the Global Private Client business, which allows NRIs and other global investors to access Indian and international investment opportunities through its offerings based in GIFT City and the Dubai International Financial Centre.

Centricity claims to manage assets worth more than ₹15,000 Cr and serve over 20,000 partners and more than 1 Lakh investors. It also claims to have onboarded 250 family offices since its incorporation.

The startup is targeting revenue of more than ₹150 Cr in FY27. Its operating revenue stood at ₹6.2 Cr in FY25, while its net loss was ₹4.4 Cr, according to Tofler. Centricity is yet to disclose its financial results for FY26.

Prior to this, Centricity raised $20 Mn in its seed funding round at a valuation of $125 Mn in 2024. At the time, the startup said it would use the capital to develop generative AI-led modules, among other initiatives.

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in India’s wealthtech sector. Last month, Veriqus Group raised ₹387 Cr to build an integrated wealth and asset management platform with technology and AI at its core.

Similarly, Neo Group also raised about ₹350 Cr from Peak XV Partners to invest in talent, technology, and new product capabilities as the company expands its presence across India.

Fintech and stockbroking companies such as Paytm, MobiKwik, and Groww are also expanding their wealth management offerings to tap the growing market.

At the heart of this push is India’s rapidly growing wealthtech industry, which is projected to become more than $95 Bn opportunity by FY30 , driven by a new generation of digital-first investors.

company_description: Wealthtech startup Veriqus Group has raised ₹387 Cr (about $40.1 Mn) in a funding round led by global VC firm Norwest.
article_title: Wealthtech Startup Veriqus Raises ₹387 Cr To Build AI-Led Investment Platform
article_excerpt:
Wealthtech startup Veriqus Group has raised ₹387 Cr (about $40.1 Mn) in a funding round led by global VC firm Norwest.

The funding will help the recently incorporated fintech startup to build its integrated wealth and asset management platform from the ground up, with tech and AI at its core.

This marks the second investment announcement to come from the global VC firm today. Earlier in the day, Norwest also led a separate $40 Mn funding round i n Hyderabad-based aerospace and defence manufacturer Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group, alongside Skegen Asset Management.

Founded in 2026 by former Julius Baer India chairman and CEO Ashish Gumashta and HDFC AMC senior fund manager Roshi Jain, Veriqus serves high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), family offices, entrepreneurs and institutions.

The wealthtech startup plans to offer wealth management, asset management, business advisory and lending services on a single platform. It also plans to expand into Tier-II and other fast-growing cities.

Gumashta has spent more than three decades in the wealth management space  and earlier helped establish DSP Merrill Lynch’s wealth management business in India. While Jain, who will lead Veriqus’ asset management arm, previously managed more than ₹1.35 Lakh Cr across the HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, HDFC Focused 30 Fund and HDFC Tax Saver Fund as of November 2025.

The new startup plans to use AI to sharpen portfolio analysis, monitor risk and improve client reporting and investment decisions.

Its asset management arm will rely on fundamental research and offer long-term investing solutions to investors, while its advisory and lending businesses will provide capital for expansion, acquisitions and liquidity needs.

The firm will follow an open-architecture model, allowing clients to choose from a wider range of investment products rather than being limited to those offered in-house.

“Veriqus intends to build a strong presence across Tier II and other high-growth cities, bringing institutional-quality advice and sophisticated investment solutions closer to entrepreneurs, business owners and multi-generational families,” Gumashta said.

Jain said the startup’s investment philosophy would combine fundamental research, prudent risk-taking and a long-term approach to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns.

India’s wealth management industry is expanding as rising incomes, entrepreneurship and the growing financialisation of savings increase the pool of affluent investors. The country’s asset management market is projected to grow from $2.7 Tn in 2026 to $5.82 Tn by 2031.

company_description: Google-backed spacetech startup Pixxel has raised $100 Mn (about ₹945 Cr) in its Series C funding round co-led by Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund Temasek and UK-based spacetech investor Seraphim.
article_title: Pixxel Bags $100 Mn To Ramp Up Satellite Manufacturing, Imaging
article_excerpt:
Google-backed spacetech startup Pixxel has raised $100 Mn (about ₹945 Cr) in its Series C funding round co-led by Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund Temasek and UK-based spacetech investor Seraphim.

New investors 360 ONE Asset and IMM Investment also participated in the round, along with existing backers Radical Ventures, growX ventures, and others.

The latest investment takes Pixxel’s total funding to $195 Mn. The startup said that the Series C was the single-largest funding round raised by a spacetech company in India.

While Pixxel did not disclose the valuation at which the funding was raised, ET reported that the round valued the startup at $400 Mn to $450 Mn.

The Bengaluru-based startup will use the fresh capital to expand its satellite sensing capabilities, further develop its Earth intelligence platform Aurora, deepen its work on sovereign space systems, and increase its satellite manufacturing capacity.

Pixxel said it would widen its sensing capabilities through its upcoming Honeybee constellation, high-resolution optical imaging satellites, and other technologies. Aurora will act as the software layer combining data captured by these satellites to generate insights for governments, businesses, and research institutions.

The startup will also ramp up production at Gigapixxel, its satellite manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. Inaugurated in 2024 , the facility was designed to handle more than 20 satellites simultaneously and manufacture up to 40 satellites a year.

“Years ago, we set out to build a health monitor for the planet. Hyperspectral imaging gave us a fundamentally new way to see Earth. This new investment gives us the scale to turn that vision into planetary infrastructure,” Pixxel founder and CEO Awais Ahmed said.

Founded in 2019 by BITS Pilani alumni Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel started by developing hyperspectral Earth observation satellites .

Unlike conventional imaging satellites, hyperspectral satellites capture light across a large number of narrow wavelength bands. This allows them to identify materials and changes on the Earth’s surface that may not be visible in ordinary satellite images.

The data can be used across agriculture, mining, oil and gas, environmental monitoring, defence, and disaster management.

Pixxel currently operates six Firefly hyperspectral satellites and claims that they form the world’s highest-resolution commercial hyperspectral satellite constellation. The first three Firefly satellites were launched aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-12 mission in January 2025, marking the deployment of India’s first private satellite constellation.

The startup has secured contracts from NASA and the US National Reconnaissance Office, besides winning multiple iDEX challenges from India’s Ministry of Defence.

It has also been selected to lead the development of India’s first public-private Earth observation satellite constellation under IN-SPACe. The proposed constellation will comprise 12 satellites carrying different types of imaging sensors.

Besides Earth observation, Pixxel has partnered with AI unicorn Sarvam to develop Pathfinder, a 200-kilogram orbital data centre demonstration satellite. Pixxel will design, launch, and operate the satellite, while Sarvam will enable AI training and inference in orbit.

Pixxel’s fundraise comes amid growing investor interest and commercial activity in India’s private spacetech ecosystem.

In May, Skyroot Aerospace raised $60 Mn at a pre-money valuation of $1.1 Bn , becoming India’s first spacetech unicorn. It followed this by completing the country’s first private orbital rocket mission in July, placing customer payloads into low-Earth orbit using its Vikram-1 launch vehicle.

article_title: slice Eyes $100 Mn Funding At 60% Valuation Cut As Bank Valuation Takes Shape
article_excerpt:
Fintech unicorn turned small finance bank (SFB) slice is set to raise around $100 Mn in fresh funding at a valuation of $450 Mn-$465 Mn, marking a sharp decline from the startup’s last valuation of around $1.25 Bn, sources told Inc42.

The round is expected to be backed by Peak XV-backed wealth management platform Neo Group, Japan-based Kado Global and existing investor Moore Strategic Ventures, according to people familiar with the development. The round could also include a secondary component, with the exact split between primary and secondary capital yet to be discerned.

Moneycontrol reported the development first.

The investment deal could potentially value the startup at roughly one-third of its last known valuation of $1.25 Bn. The startup entered the unicorn club in 2021 when it raised $220 Mn in its Series B round led by Tiger Global and Insight Partners.

However, the valuation dip comes amid slice’s bid to establish itself as a digital bank following its merger with North East Small Finance Bank (NESFB). The transaction gave the Bengaluru-based startup a small finance bank licence and marked a fundamental shift from its earlier lendingtech model.

slice’s original business was built around credit and prepaid-card products, but regulatory changes in 2022 disrupted that model. It subsequently acquired NESFB and completed the merger in October 2024.

Since then, slice has expanded its offerings across deposits, lending, UPI-linked credit and payments, while building out MSME and merchant lending businesses.

The transition also changes the metrics investors use to assess the company. Rather than being valued primarily as a consumer fintech business, slice is now positioning itself as an SFB. This means that banking-related metrics — deposits, lending growth, profitability and cost of funds — have gained importance.

An investor note by 8i Ventures founding partner Vikram Chachra, reviewed by Inc42, compared slice’s valuation with other banks on a price-to-book basis. The note puts slice at around 4.5X book value.

The valuation reset comes despite improving financial performance.

The SFB swung to the black in Q1 FY27, reporting a net profit of ₹50.9 Cr in the June quarter against a net loss of ₹10.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its profit for the quarter under review also surpassed the ₹48.4 Cr PAT it reported for the entire FY26.

slice’s total income rose 38.6% to ₹413.8 Cr during the quarter from ₹298.6 Cr in Q1 FY26. r.

Meanwhile, its gross loan book grew about 55% to ₹5,098 Cr from ₹3,284 Cr a year earlier. Its deposits nearly doubled to ₹5,765 Cr from ₹3,038 Cr during the same period, slice said in a statement. Current account savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 43.9%, with CASA and retail term deposits together accounting for 94.7% of its total deposits.

The bank’s total assets increased 54% YoY to ₹7,444 Cr, while its net worth rose 16.5% to ₹896 Cr. Its outstanding debt declined 23.2% to ₹507.3 Cr from ₹660.4 Cr a year earlier.

company_description: Wealth management startup Nexedge Capital has raised $20 Mn (₹191.4 Cr) in its maiden funding round co-led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment and Elev8 Venture Partners.
article_title: Nexedge Capital Nets $20 Mn To Scale HNI Wealth Management Platform
article_excerpt:
Wealth management startup Nexedge Capital has raised $20 Mn (₹191.4 Cr) in its maiden funding round co-led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment and Elev8 Venture Partners.

The startup, which offers bespoke financial services like investment planning, portfolio management, estate planning, to India’s HNIs, UHNIs, families and corporates, plans to utilise the fresh capital to strengthen its tech stack, expand network of senior bankers and its India footprint.

A portion of the funds will also go into building out complementary offerings such as a dedicated NRI proposition, an NBFC business, among other initiatives.

“Our maiden raise marks an important milestone in Nexedge’s journey… This capital gives us the ability to accelerate our banker onboarding, deepen distribution across the country, and offer our conflict-free Net Worth advisory to more families,” Nexedge Capital founder Anirudha Taparia said.

Launched in 2025 by ex-360 ONE Wealth executivesTaparia, Sidhartha Shaw, Vijeeta Sharma and Pankaj Walia, the wealth management and multi-family office platform claims to have crossed $3 Bn in assets under management (AUM) and over $5 Bn in assets under administration.

Over the eighteen months of its operations, the startup claims to have  grown its clientele to over 1,300 families, presence across 12 locations, and grown its employee base to over 240 and banker base to 95.

This is Elev8 Venture Partners’ second major investment since it closed its maiden ₹1,400 Cr fund in September 2025. Prior to the Nexedge investment, the VC firm led investment asset servicing startup Dovetail Capital’s ₹100 Cr Series A round in July.

“India’s HNI and UHNI wealth pool is at the start of a multi-decade compounding cycle. Wealth management rewards patience, and trust is earned over market cycles, not quarters. Nexedge stands out for its structural clarity, the depth of its founding team, and its ability to build client trust at a pace few platforms in this space have matched,” Elev8’s managing partner Navin Honagudi noted.

To note, startups providing wealth management services to UHNIs is emerging as a niche segment of sorts in the Indian fintech ecosystem. Besides Dovetail Capital, Nexedge, wealth management startup CREST also came out of stealth recently and raised $3.1 Mn in a pre-seed funding round in June. Meanwhile, ex-Share.Market CEO Ujjwal Jain left PhonePe earlier this year to launch an AI platform, Atyx .AI, in the wealth management segment back in July.

The India wealth management market is scaling at a significant rate, with projections of it breaching the $436 Bn mark by 2034 . The HNI segment is emerging as a key mover in this space, with the number of Indian millionaires projected to double to 18 Lakh by 2030 from 9 Lakh today, as per UBS Global Wealth report.
