article_title: MobiKwik Infuses ₹61 Cr In Lending Arm, Appoints Ex-Bajaj Markets’ Manish Pathania As Its CBO
article_excerpt:
Months after receiving a regulatory nod for its NBFC licence, MobiKwik has now completed the transfer of its digital lending operations and associated team to its wholly owned subsidiary, MobiKwik Distribution Services Private Limited (MDSPL).

Beyond the restructuring, the fintech company has also announced that it will be pumping ₹60.85 Cr as equity into MDSPL.

To strengthen the subsidiary’s operations, MobiKwik has appointed former Bajaj Markets exec Manish Pathania as the chief business officer (CBO) of MDSPL. Pathania, who brings nearly two decades of experience across financial institutions like GE Money and HDB Financial Services, will be responsible for supervising the digital lending business and drive its next phase of growth.

The development comes months after RBI gave a conditional nod to MobiKwik’s NBFC application , specifying that its lending service provider (LSP) business be migrated to an independent subsidiary before issuing the Certificate of Registration (CoR).

The NBFC licence will allow MobiKwik to launch a new lending division that will enhance its lending capabilities, credit products’ stack and serve a broader base of consumers and merchants.

The transfer of its digital lending operations to MDSPL has been executed to fulfill this criteria.

“We have built a strong lending franchise through partnerships with banks and NBFCs, while developing capabilities across the lending value chain. Consolidating the business and team under MDSPL, with Manish leading the subsidiary, gives us a dedicated structure to take this business forward,” MobiKwik cofounder, MD, and CEO Bipin Preet Singh said.

MDSPL was incorporated last year to oversee financing, leasing, and hire-purchase activities across commercial assets including machinery, equipment, plants, vehicles, aircraft, ships, and real estate.

Initially, MobiKwik had allocated an initial paid-up share capital of ₹1 Lakh for the newly set up subsidiary. Subsequently, in June, the fintech company also issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder consent to redirect unspent IPO proceeds toward its payments and lending businesses, along with a proposal to push the utilisation deadline for the remaining funds to FY27.

Under the proposed changes, MobiKwik expressed its plans to divert ₹60.85 Cr originally earmarked for the organic growth of its financial services business to MDSPL.

The company is doubling down on digital lending amid a strong financial momentum. In Q1 FY27, MobiKwik reported a consolidated net profit of ₹7.6 Cr against a net loss of ₹41.9 Cr in the year-ago period. Operating revenue rose a marginal 3.7% YoY to ₹281.5 Cr during the quarter.

Its financial services gross profit for Q1 FY27 skyrocketed 459% YoY on the back of improved credit quality, sharper risk management, and efficient loan recovery efforts, the statement added.

Revenue from the financial service segment , which includes ZIP EMI, wealth management, and stock broking, jumped 26% to ₹73.3 Cr in the June quarter from ₹58.3 Cr in the same quarter last year.

Lending disbursals for the quarter stood at ₹736.7 Cr, seeing a sequential dip primarily due to technology migration associated with the above mentioned transfer to MDSPL. Back then, the management said that disbursal volumes would bounce back starting Q2 FY27.

The company has now set a target to achieve quarterly loan disbursals of ₹1,000+ Cr in the upcoming quarters.

Shares of MobiKwik ended today’s trading session 1.8% lower at ₹198.85 apiece on BSE.

company_description: Household assistance startup Hulp has raised $2.6 Mn (about ₹25 Cr) in a seed funding round led by VC firms Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures.
article_title: AI Concierge Startup Hulp Raises $2.6 Mn From Sparrow Capital, BITKRAFT
article_excerpt:
Household assistance startup Hulp has raised $2.6 Mn (about ₹25 Cr) in a seed funding round led by VC firms Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures.

While early stage VC DeVC also participated in the round, multiple angel investors including PB Fintech cofounder and chairman Yashish Dahiya, also participated in the round.

The Delhi NCR-based startup will deploy the fresh capital to scale its AI platform, hire senior leaders, and strengthen technology infrastructure to expand service coverage across metro cities.

Founded in 2026 by ex-Policybazaar CBO Tarun Mathur, alongside ex-Mitgo India MD Neha Kulwal and Vishal Singh Khutel, Hulp operates a concierge service that combines AI automation with dedicated human assistants. Users can contact assistants through WhatsApp or its mobile app and delegate tasks through a voice note.

The platform claims to handle daily tasks across more than 15 categories including kitchen management, runner services, administrative filings, travel and event bookings, and restaurant reservations.

It plans to expand operations into Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai over the next two years.

India’s affluent consumers are projected to cross the 10 Cr mark by 2027, according to a report by Goldman Sachs Research . New-age tech companies are increasingly aiming to cater to this market, driving the rise of the convenience economy.

Quick commerce and instant home services are the most widely known examples of how this trend is playing out. However, startups offering concierge services are also seeking to serve the needs of aspirational Indians.

Notably, food delivery giant Swiggy operates in this segment, offering on-demand concierge services for wealthy customers via its Crew app . Former American Express executive Manoj Adlakha’s bootstrapped venture RedBeryl , founded in 2023, is another notable player whose services are invite-only and span a range of categories from fine dining to sports and entertainment.

Last year, Indulge Global of Shark Tank fame also bagged $1 Mn funding to scale its own luxury concierge services platform .

company_description: AI sales automation startup Revspot has raised $4.8 Mn (about ₹45.9 Cr) in its Series A funding round co-led by Inflexor Ventures and Info Edge Ventures.
article_title: Revspot Raises $4.8 Mn To Scale AI Sales Automation Platform
article_excerpt:
AI sales automation startup Revspot has raised $4.8 Mn (about ₹45.9 Cr) in its Series A funding round co-led by Inflexor Ventures and Info Edge Ventures. Pentathlon Ventures, Silicon Road Ventures and existing investor Titan Capital also participated in the round.

The Bengaluru-based startup said it will use the fresh capital to deepen its product and engineering capabilities in India, strengthen its buyer-intelligence and AI qualification infrastructure, expand into new high-ticket B2C sectors, and build customer presence in select international markets.

Founded in 2024 by Darshan Subash, Chirag Wadhera and Varun Garg, Revspot provides an AI-powered sales automation platform that helps high-ticket B2C businesses identify, qualify and engage potential customers more efficiently.

Its platform combines lead generation, campaign analytics, lead enrichment, voice AI, WhatsApp-led customer engagement, and sales handoff into a single workflow. According to the startup, this enables businesses to identify higher-intent buyers earlier and improve visibility into buyer fit, purchase readiness and conversion potential.

The startup claims to serve over 50 customers across real estate, education, automotive and wealth management, and is also expanding into broader BFSI categories. As part of its product roadmap, Revspot is developing Spot, an orchestration platform for qualified-pipeline workflows that connects campaign planning, Meta-native campaign analysis, lead enrichment, voice AI qualification, and downstream lead-quality feedback.

Prior to this round, Revspot raised $1.4 Mn in a seed round in late 2024, co-led by Info Edge Ventures and Titan Capital, with participation from angel investor Kunal Shah. With the latest infusion, the startup’s total funding stands at $6.2 Mn.

Revspot’s latest funding comes at a time when India’s enterprise tech sector continues to draw investor interest around AI-led workflow automation and customer engagement tools, especially as the segment strives to solve core issues like revenue acceleration, lowered operating costs, and higher employee efficiency.

For instance, enterprise tech startup for cloud automation NudgeBee raised $3 Mn in April this year in a seed round led by Kalaari Capital, while GTM-focused Kris@Work raised $3 Mn in its seed funding round led by Info Edge Ventures in February.

Overall funding for AI startups has also accelerated over the past year. As per Inc42’s ‘ Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, H1 2026 ’, Indian AI startups raised $676 Mn during the first six months of 2026 alone, up over 4X YoY. The number of funding deals also touched a fresh six-month high of 57.

company_description: Cleantech startup altM has raised $10.3 Mn (₹97.5 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter and Mela Ventures.
article_title: Cleantech Startup altM Raises $10.3 Mn To Scale Manufacturing
article_excerpt:
Cleantech startup altM has raised $10.3 Mn (₹97.5 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter and Mela Ventures. Existing investors Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact also participated.

The Bengaluru-based startup plans to use the fresh capital to expand manufacturing, build its sales pipeline and continue investing in research and development (R&D). A large chunk of the funds will go towards setting up a 1,000-tonne-per-year commercial manufacturing facility by 2028.

“We have three large focus areas for the company today. In the short term, we want to start converting revenues and building our sales pipeline from the pilot plant. From a manufacturing perspective, a large chunk of our investment will go into building the next 1,000-tonne-per-year commercial plant,” cofounder and CEO Apoorv Garg told Inc42.

The startup will also continue developing alternative materials and biochemicals. It plans to expand its sales team following the funding round. “The major influx will be on sales,” Garg added.

Founded in 2022 by former Tesla executives Garg and Yugal Raj Jain , altM develops specialty chemicals and biomaterials from agricultural residue for industrial applications.

Its platform converts lignocellulosic biomass, including sugarcane bagasse, rice straw and other agricultural residues, into materials for use in beauty and personal care, textiles, industrial chemicals, construction, packaging and consumer goods.

The platform uses the major fractions of biomass, including cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin, to produce multiple products from a single feedstock, offering an alternative to fossil-derived raw materials.

The latest round comes nearly three years after altM raised $3.5 Mn in a seed round in 2023. Since then, the startup has built an integrated R&D and pilot manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, bringing laboratory research, demonstration manufacturing and pilot production under one roof.

It has expanded its laboratory footprint nearly 5X, commissioned a demonstration manufacturing facility and advanced six molecules to the demonstration stage, with three selected for pilot production.

The first products advancing towards commercialisation include a lignin-derived SPF booster for suncare, a cellulose-based rheology modifier and bio-derived ferulic acid for cosmetics and personal care formulations.

The startup is currently focused on the BPC segment, while its R&D pipeline spans construction, electronics, automotive, polymers and battery materials.

Garg said altM has completed the installation of its 70-tonne-per-year pilot plant in Bengaluru’s Electronic City and is preparing to begin commercial production.

“We have been installing it since late 2025 and finally finished the installation in 2026. It’s still in pre-production, and we’re getting the right certifications and validations to take it to production this month,” Garg said.

The startup expects to begin fulfilling purchase orders in the current quarter, with its first product launches planned for the following quarter. It currently works with nearly 30 BPC customers at different stages of product development, testing and commercialisation. Around 16-18 of them are in testing and active validation, Garg said.

altM’s process involves breaking down plant matter into core polymers and upgrading these fractions into chemicals. Garg said the startup has filed six patents in India covering its deconstruction technology and processes for upgrading individual molecules. It is working on a seventh patent and plans to file patents in international markets as well.

The startup has carried out more than 15,000 reactions at the laboratory stage and translated over 500 reactions to the demonstration stage. It has also reduced the time taken to develop new molecules from 12-15 months to under six months, Garg said.

company_description: Bengaluru-based Nova Spectral AI has raised ₹21.2 Cr ($2.3 Mn) in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Equirus InnovateX Fund and angel investors.
article_title: Nova Spectral AI Raises ₹21.2 Cr To Build Indigenous Infrared Sensor Chips
article_excerpt:
Bengaluru-based Nova Spectral AI has raised ₹21.2 Cr ($2.3 Mn) in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Equirus InnovateX Fund and angel investors.

Founded earlier this year by IIT Kanpur alum Anish Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar, Nova Spectral is building short-wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chips using colloidal quantum dots (cQDs) and standard silicon CMOS manufacturing processes.

This will help drones, surveillance systems, robots and autonomous vehicles capture images in low-light conditions and through smoke, haze and dust. It aims to develop an indigenous alternative to conventional infrared sensors, which are largely imported and rely on expensive indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) technology.

The fresh capital will help the startup expand its team as well as develop a field-ready prototype within 18 months.

“India’s armed forces should not have to rely on an imported sensor to see at night or through smoke. We design and build our chip in India, with a roadmap to make the quantum dot materials and readout chip here too,” Nova Spectral AI cofounder and CEO Priyadarshi said.

Nova Spectral AI was founded earlier this year by Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar. Priyadarshi has built a quantum dot fabrication facility from the ground up and developed working indium arsenide sensors for SWIR imaging.

It also secured in-principle approval to incubate at IISc Bengaluru, where it planned to expand its team after the seed round.

The investment comes at a time when India’s deeptech sector continues to draw investor interest in strategic hardware and domestic chip design. Policy tailwinds from India’s indigenisation push, alongside support for semiconductor design and defence electronics manufacturing, have helped sharpen investor focus on locally built sensing technologies.

As per Inc42’s ‘ Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026 ’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals, compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025.

In this light, investors continue to launch funds to back startups in the deeptech space, where Unacademy cofounders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising a ₹700 Cr venture capital fund to back AI and deeptech startups, under the name Longshot Capital, a Category II AIF.

Prior to that, South Korean gaming giant KRAFTON disclosed its plans to invest an additional $250 Mn (₹3,300 Cr) in Indian startups across areas such as AI, robotics and deeptech over the next three to four years.

company_description: Climatetech startup Circolife has netted $4.5 Mn (around ₹40.45 Cr) in a pre-Series A round led by Polycab India’s joint MD Bharat Jaisinghani.
article_title: Circolife Raises $4.5 Mn To Scale Subscription-Based Air Conditioning
article_excerpt:
Climatetech startup Circolife has netted $4.5 Mn (around ₹40.45 Cr) in a pre-Series A round led by Polycab India’s joint MD Bharat Jaisinghani.

The round also saw participation from Nazara founder Nitish Mittersain, Intelliquity Ventures, Param Capital, Everest Fleet’s founder Siddharth Ladsariya, Anand Ladsariya of Everest Flavours, Indian Express’ executive director Anant Goenka, Sky Impact Capital, Ideas91’s founder Rohit Dev, and family offices S N Damani and Vyom Wealth, among others.

The Thane-based startup plans to deploy the fresh capital to expand its AC (air conditioning) fleet, enter new markets, scale its in-house installation and field-service operations, and invest in its IoT and AI capabilities.

Founded in 2023 by Abhishek Murarka, Tushar Patil and Devanshu Mishra, Circolife operates a subscription-based model for commercial AC, allowing businesses to use AC units for a monthly fee while the company handles installation, maintenance and eventual refurbishment or replacement.

The startup serves businesses across segments such as restaurants, hotels, gyms, salons and co-living operators. Circolife currently has around 10,000 active subscriptions across five cities. With the fresh capital, it is targeting growing its customer base by 4X over the next two years.

Circolife currently operates two refurbishment facilities in Mumbai and Delhi, where AC units are refurbished and redeployed at the end of their lifecycle.

Circolife’s AC units are connected through an IoT layer that monitors parameters such as temperature, power consumption and gas pressure. The data is used by its predictive-maintenance system to identify potential equipment failures before they result in breakdowns.

The startup is also developing digital twins of individual AC units and, subsequently, entire sites. It aims to use the data generated across its fleet to optimise cooling performance and energy efficiency at the unit and property level.

Cooling as a Service (CaaS) in India is growing significantly as subscription models, where businesses pay per unit of cooling instead of buying expensive equipment upfront, is picking up steam. Businesses increasingly look for alternatives to outright ownership of energy-intensive equipment, while the CaaS model allows service providers to retain ownership of the equipment and manage its lifecycle.

The investment comes amid continued investor interest in India’s climatetech sector across energy, mobility and climate-focused businesses. For instance, Bengaluru-based Newtrace secured $6.3 Mn (₹56.93 Cr) in a Pre-Series A funding round in March, to boost its commercialisation.

company_description: Ahmedabad-based waste management startup NEPRA has raised ₹110 Cr (about $11.7 Mn) in an equity funding round from the Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG), a London-based infrastructure development and financ
article_title: NEPRA Raises ₹110 Cr To Expand Plastic Recycling Capacity
article_excerpt:
Ahmedabad-based waste management startup NEPRA has raised ₹110 Cr (about $11.7 Mn) in an equity funding round from the Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG), a London-based infrastructure development and finance organisation, through its project development arm InfraCo. The company, which operates under the ‘NEPRA – Let’s Recycle’ brand, will use the capital to develop new material recovery facilities (MRFs), expand plastic recycling capacity, strengthen existing operations, and meet working capital requirements. NEPRA plans to more than double its waste processing capacity from around 900 tonnes per day to 1,880 tonnes. It also aims to increase its plastic recycling capacity from 6,200 tonnes annually to 18,000 tonnes.

According to the announcement, the transaction marks PIDG’s first equity investment in Asia’s waste management and recycling sector. PIDG joins NEPRA’s existing investors, including Aavishkaar Capital, Circulate Capital, Blue Earth Capital, and Asha Impact.

Founded in 2006, NEPRA collects, segregates, processes, and recycles waste. The company says it currently processes more than 900 tonnes of waste daily through its facilities in Ahmedabad, Indore, Pune, and Bengaluru.

It also operates a plastic recycling plant in Sanand, Gujarat, where it converts plastic waste into recycled granules. Non-recyclable waste is processed into refuse-derived fuel (RDF) for use in cement manufacturing.

NEPRA works with brand owners to help them meet extended producer responsibility (EPR) obligations through traceable recycling processes. Its collection network includes more than 1,500 registered waste pickers.

The company previously raised $18 Mn in a Series C round from Aavishkaar Capital and Circulate Capital in November 2020.

NEPRA’s fundraise follows investments in other Indian startups building waste collection, processing, and recycling infrastructure.

Earlier this week, Bengaluru-based Recove Ventures raised ₹56.3 Cr through a mix of equity and debt to expand its plastic waste collection, processing, and recycling infrastructure. It plans to invest more than ₹2,000 Cr across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh over the next decade.

Hyderabad-based Recykal also raised $23 Mn in a bridge round , with former cricketer Sachin Tendulkar subsequently joining its cap table . Recykal operates a B2B marketplace for recyclable materials and offers software to help brands track plastic and e-waste recycling.

Beyond plastics, Delhi NCR-based Karo Sambhav raised ₹56 Cr from Rainmatter in June 2026 to expand infrastructure for recovering critical, precious, and high-value materials from end-of-life products.

article_title: D2C Brand Lumov Eyes ₹33 Cr In Peak XV Surge-Led Round
article_excerpt:
Bengaluru-based D2C orthopaedic products brand Lumov is in talks to raise around ₹33 Cr (about $3.5 Mn) in a funding round led by Peak XV’s Surge programme, sources told Inc42. The startup’s existing investors are also expected to participate in the round, the sources said.

Lumov and Peak XV didn’t respond to Inc42’s queries on the development till the time of publication. Founded in 2024 by Saumaric Dangwal and Ankit Gupta, Lumov designs and manufactures orthopaedic braces and other aids for post-surgical recovery, rehabilitation, and pain management. Both founders have backgrounds in private equity. Dangwal previously worked with Bain Capital as a healthcare and consumer investor, while Gupta was associated with Brookfield Private Equity and Steinberg Asset Management.

The startup’s offerings include knee braces, insoles, and lower-back support belts. The brand sells through its own website, and its products are also listed on Flipkart and Blinkit. Lumov claims it develops products with orthopaedic specialists at Manipal Hospitals, Apollo Hospitals, Sakra World Hospital, and AIG Hospitals and designs them for Indian patients and local weather conditions. Prior to this, Lumov raised $1.2 Mn (around ₹10 Cr) in a seed round led by Incubate Fund Asia. QRG Investments and Holdings, the Havells family office, also participated, along with IIMA Ventures, SIDBI, and angel investors including Ashish Gupta of Helion Advisors, Saket Narang of Steinberg India, and Abhishek Goyal of Tracxn. At the time, Lumov said it would use the capital to strengthen manufacturing, scale sales operations, and develop more products for post-surgical recovery and rehabilitation. It also planned to expand its presence in Delhi NCR, Hyderabad, and Mumbai and deepen its clinical and sales partnerships. Lumov’s proposed fundraise comes on the heels of another deal in musculoskeletal care products. In September, Bengaluru-based preventive pain care brand Betterhood raised ₹11.5 Cr in a seed round led by Sauce VC.

Investors are also backing startups that provide pain management and rehabilitation services. In January, chronic pain clinic chain Nivaan Care raised $7 Mn in a Series A round led by Sorin Investments. Musculoskeletal care startup Stance Health, which offers physiotherapy and rehabilitation, raised $1 Mn in pre-seed funding in April 2025.

company_description: AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform Dreamteam, cofounded by former Freshworks executives, has emerged out of stealth mode.
article_title: Dreamteam Bags $53 Mn To Disrupt The CRM Space With AI
article_excerpt:
AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform Dreamteam, cofounded by former Freshworks executives, has emerged out of stealth mode. The startup has now raised $53 Mn (nearly ₹498 Cr) in a strategic funding round from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.

The startup did not elaborate how it plans to utilise the funds.

“… CRM is among the biggest software categories ripe for disruption. I’ve worked alongside Dreamteam’s founders since day one as their vision for an AI-native CRM took shape. Their deep CRM expertise and proven record of scaling enterprise software make them uniquely positioned to lead this reinvention,” said Together Fund cofounder and partner Girish Mathrubootham.

Founded in 2025 by former Freshworks executives Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, Dreamteam is building an AI-powered CRM platform. Its four AI agents help enterprises track commitments, flag pipeline risks and automate routine sales workflows.

The startup claims that its AI platform pulls data and context from customer conversations, emails and Zoom interactions to enable AI coworkers to automate regular work. In addition, it also allows businesses to create custom apps and dashboards using natural language without writing code.

Dreamtech claims to already cater to hundreds of companies across industries such as AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing, and consulting.

Going forward, Dreamteam said that it plans to focus on expanding its use cases across the entire customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding and upselling.

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in Indian AI startups. As per Inc42 data, homegrown AI ventures raised $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q2 2026 , up 265% YoY. Venture capital (VC) and private equity (PE) firms remain bullish on startups that help enterprises put AI to work across business functions.

Just last month, US-based AI code testing startup Blacksmith bagged $66 Mn in its Series C round led by Sequoia Capital. Prior to this in October itself, another enterprise AI startup AuxoAI also raised $20.7 Mn in its Series A funding round led by NTTVC.

Fractal Analytics CEO Srikanth Velamakanni also recently reportedly said that the AI analytics company is in discussions with 20-25 AI startups for potential acquisitions .

At the heart of all this is the growing Indian enterprise AI ecosystem, which is projected to become a $71 Bn opportunity by 2030 .

company_description: US-based AI healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 Mn (about ₹119 Cr) in a Series A extension led by Z47, taking its total Series A funding to $22.5 Mn.
article_title: Confido Health Raises $12.5 Mn To Automate Healthcare Administration With AI
article_excerpt:
US-based AI healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 Mn (about ₹119 Cr) in a Series A extension led by Z47, taking its total Series A funding to $22.5 Mn.

Existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures also participated in the round. Healthcare private equity investor Justin Saks has joined the startup as an investor and board adviser. The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its CareOS platform across healthcare organisations with multiple sites and develop AI agents for additional workflows and medical specialities.

Founded in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health develops AI agents to automate administrative tasks for healthcare providers, including patient calls, appointment scheduling, insurance verification, prescription refills, and payment collection.

Its CareOS platform integrates with more than 50 healthcare systems, including electronic health records, practice management software, and billing platforms. This allows providers to automate tasks across their existing systems without replacing their technology infrastructure.

Confido Health initially focused on voice AI for patient calls before expanding into broader healthcare administration. Its platform connects related tasks, allowing a patient interaction to trigger follow-up work such as scheduling an appointment, processing a prescription refill, or collecting a payment.

The startup primarily targets healthcare groups operating across multiple sites, particularly those backed by private equity firms. Its distribution strategy involves working with private equity investors to secure introductions to their portfolio companies.

Confido Health said it serves 3,200 providers across more than 1,500 sites in 27 US states, with its AI agents enabling one in 50 Americans to access healthcare. It claimed 15-fold growth since its previous funding round but did not specify the metric.

The startup reported AI handling rates above 95% across key end-to-end administrative workflows. It said deployments added operational capacity equivalent to three to five full-time employees on average within three months, while patient satisfaction averaged 4.55 out of five across approximately one million tasks.

The fundraise comes amid investor bets on AI applications across healthcare, from administrative automation to patient guidance and early disease detection.

Earlier, Inc42 reported that AI health companion startup August AI was in talks to raise about $4 Mn from Peak XV Partners . The startup helps users understand symptoms, prescriptions, medications, and medical reports.

Earlier this year, Practo cofounder Shashank ND’s new venture Cent raised about $5 Mn from his family office OneFlow Holdings and South Park Commons. Cent uses AI and health data to detect critical diseases early.

Indian healthtech startups raised $93 Mn across 13 deals in Q3 2026 till September 24.

article_title: GreenCell Mobility Raises ₹330 Cr To Expand Electric Bus Fleet
article_excerpt:
Everstone Capital-backed EV startup GreenCell Mobility has raised ₹330 Cr ($34.6 Mn) in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses currently under deployment.

The Mumbai-based startup is eyeing expanding its fleet to more than 5,000 e-buses across 105 cities across India.

“Our focus is on executing our order book with rigour, strengthening service delivery and ensuring that the organisation keeps pace with the size and complexity of our operations. This equity investment gives us greater headroom to accelerate our plans while maintaining the standards of reliability, efficiency and customer experience that are fundamental to our business,” GreenCell Mobility managing director and chief executive Devndra Chawla said.

Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility focuses on deploying and operating electric buses for public transportation. It acquires electric buses via contract manufacturing arrangements with vendors and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel.

Backed by Eversource Capital, a joint venture between Everstone Capital and Lightsource, GreenCell primarily operates under the brand NueGo.

It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses in India, including 900 on intra-city routes, 300 under its NueGo brand for inter-city travel, and 50 for MSRTC. The startup also runs over 270 charging stations to support its fleet.

The startup previously raised $37 Mn from World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and also counts Eversource Capital, British International Investment and Tata Capital among its backers.

India’s electric bus segment has so far drawn strong interest from development finance institutions and lenders backing vehicle deployments under long-term public transport contracts. GreenCell’s latest round suggested that investors are also beginning to back the operating platform layer in the category, not just asset financing.

The investment highlights the role of institutional capital in expanding electric public transportation infrastructure in India. Large-scale electric bus deployments require funding not only for vehicles but also for the operational capabilities and charging infrastructure needed to support them.

Earlier in March, electric bus manufacturer PMI Electro Mobility, along with its electric bus platform Allfleet, has signed a definitive agreement with private equity giant KKR for an investment commitment of up to $310 Mn, to help scale the electric bus platform and focus on expanding its presence across India. PMI subsequently filed for an IPO via the confidential route last month.

company_description: D2C lifestyle startup DailyObjects has raised ₹332 Cr ($34.3 Mn) in a Series C funding round co-led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
article_title: D2C Lifestyle Brand DailyObjects Raises ₹332 Cr To Expand Offline Presence
article_excerpt:
D2C lifestyle startup DailyObjects has raised ₹332 Cr ($34.3 Mn) in a Series C funding round co-led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital. The round, which included both primary and secondary transactions, valued the startup at  ₹1,050 Cr ($108.4 Mn).

As part of the secondary deal, DailyObjects’ early investor Roots Ventures partially exited with a 18X return on its initial investment.

Roots Ventures first invested $2 Mn in DailyObjects in February 2022. Following which, the investor doubled down on the startup during its $10 Mn Series B funding round in 2024.

The fresh funds will allow DailyObjects, which is known for its lifestyle and tech accessories like phone cases, watchbands, bags, wallets and wireless chargers, to scale its offline network, deepen its product and R&D capabilities, strengthen brand building and evaluate opportunities in international markets.

The startup is planning to expand its physical retail network to 150 exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years.

“We are looking at this as capital to build a ₹1,000 Cr business over the coming years and, ultimately, a global design-led consumer brand from India. As we scale, capital efficiency and profitable growth will remain at the core of how we build,” DailyObjects cofounder and CEO Pankaj Garg said.

Founded in 2012 by Garg and Adlakha, DailyObjects started off as an online store which offered users with a range of smartphone and tablet accessories. Through its journey, the startup expanded to other lifestyle product lines like bags, wallets, among other lifestyle related products.

The startup opened its first offline retail experience store DailyObjects ‘Playground’ in Gurugram back in 2023. Further, the startup expanded its offline footprint by setting up nine retail stores across Tier I cities like Delhi NCR and Bengaluru.

Prior to this round, DailyObjects claimed to have raised about ₹100 Cr in equity over the last decade. Its cap table includes investors like Lenskart founder Peyush Bansal, Unilazer Ventures and RedBus founder Phani Sama.

On the financial front, Garg projected its FY26 net revenue to double to ₹220 Cr to ₹230 Cr from ₹111 Cr reported in FY25. He also expects its top line to further jump to ₹400 Cr by FY27.

article_title: Exclusive: Leverage Edu Eyes ₹500 Cr Pre-IPO Funding, Targets ₹600 Cr Revenue In FY27
article_excerpt:
IPO-bound study abroad platform Leverage Edu is targeting ₹600 Cr in revenue in FY27, up over 60% from the ₹372 Cr it reported in FY26, sources told Inc42. The startup’s management wants to reach this revenue milestone before taking it public. Alongside its listing preparations, Leverage Edu is exploring a ₹500 Cr pre-IPO funding round to bring a large private equity firm onto its cap table.

The startup has held talks with a couple of global PE firms and is expected to close the round soon, the sources said.

“Akshay has committed to the board that the company will file DRHP by the end of next year. He is currently out in the market to finalise investment bankers for the IPO,” one of the sources said, referring to founder and CEO Akshay Chaturvedi.

Leverage Edu did not respond to Inc42’s questions till the time of publication.

Inc42 earlier exclusively reported that the startup is planning a ₹2,000–3,000 Cr IPO , comprising a fresh issue of shares and an OFS. The split between the two components is yet to be decided.

The startup is targeting a valuation of over $900 Mn for the IPO. Pitch decks prepared by investment bankers and accessed by Inc42 position Leverage Edu alongside platform businesses such as Zomato, ixigo, and Shadowfax, with expectations of similar valuation multiples.

It turned EBITDA profitable in FY26, posting an EBITDA of ₹9.5 Cr, according to the sources. Meanwhile, Leverage Edu has been expanding its international presence. In July, Inc42 reported that the startup entered South America through the acquisition of Brazil-based international education company Mundus Agency . Leverage Edu confirmed the acquisition but did not disclose the deal’s financial terms.

Founded in 2017 by Chaturvedi, Leverage Edu helps students apply to foreign universities . Besides its flagship app, it offers courses through the Leverage IELTS and Leverage TOEFL apps.

The startup’s services spanning fintech, accommodation, travel, and career support account for 25–33% of its total revenue. It also claimed to have added over 55,000 students in FY26, taking its total customer base to over 1.75 Lakh.

Leverage Edu has raised about $73 Mn in funding to date from investors including Blume Ventures, DSG Consumer Partners, and Kaizenvest.

Agritech startup Balwaan Krishi has raised ₹100 Cr (around $10 Mn) in its Series B funding round led by First Bridge India Growth Fund Private Equity, with participation from other institutional investors whose names were not disclosed. The Jaipur-based startup will use the capital to expand domestic manufacturing capacity, strengthen its dealer and service network in southern India, and develop new farm equipment.

company_description: Contract manufacturing company Aequs’ board has approved a fund raise of up to ₹650 Cr via a preferential issue of warrants to the promoter group, Mellwood Trustee Services Pvt Ltd.
article_title: Aequs To Raise ₹650 Cr Via Preferential Issue To Bolster Manufacturing Capacity
article_excerpt:
Contract manufacturing company Aequs’ board has approved a fund raise of up to ₹650 Cr via a preferential issue of warrants to the promoter group, Mellwood Trustee Services Pvt Ltd.

In a filing with the exchanges yesterday (September 25), the company said that its board has approved the issuance of 2.8 Cr warrants at an issue price of ₹231.55 per warrant. Of the total issue size, ₹325 Cr will be payable upfront upon allotment of the warrants, representing 50% of the issue size, and twice the regulatory minimum. The balance will be payable upon exercise of the warrants.

The promoter issued an investment commitment letter dated September 25, 2026 to the company, confirming its intention to subscribe to the warrants for cash consideration. On full conversion of the warrants, the aggregate holding of the promoter and promoter group will increase to 60.73% from 59.09%.

The issue is subject to the shareholders and regulatory approval. The company will seek shareholder approval via an EGM on October 22 (Thursday).

The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand capacity across its aerospace and consumer businesses, including the development of its Hosur facility, investments in subsidiaries and joint ventures, and other general corporate purposes.

“The equity will also provide the base against which the Company raises its term borrowings for the expansion. The board has assessed the Company’s current equity requirement through FY28 and has decided to meet it through this issue. A broader capital raise will be considered as and when required by the company’s growth plans,” the company said.

Founded in 2006 by Aravind Melligeri, Aequs provides manufacturing services to enterprises. It initially started with catering to the aerospace industry and later diversified its offerings to other sectors such as toys and consumer durable goods and products.

It counts the likes of Airbus, Boeing and Collins Aerospace among its clients.

Aequs is investing in building an aerospace engine component ecosystem in India. Its Hosur facility is expected to be operational next year, with shipments likely to begin by 2028.

Brokerage Nuvama Institutional Equities initiated coverage on the aerospace contract manufacturer with a ‘Buy’ rating and a 12-month target price of ₹444, implying an upside of over 90% from July 6 closing price.

The brokerage said Aequs’ $889 Mn order book provides strong revenue visibility, and projected a 42% revenue CAGR and an 84% EBITDA CAGR between FY26 and FY29.

On the financial front, Aequs reported a net loss of  ₹53.2 Cr in Q1 FY27 , against a net profit of ₹3.6 Cr in the last year quarter. Operating revenue for the June quarter jumped 55% YoY to ₹395.6 Cr.

The fresh fundraise comes almost a year after Aequs raised fresh capital via its initial public offering (IPO) in December 2025. The company’s  public offering comprised a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹670 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.03 Cr shares.

Amicus Capital, the Dempo family trusts, and individual shareholders Ravindra Mariwala and Raman Subramanian, alongside promoter entities Aequs Manufacturing Investments and Melligeri Private Family Foundation, offloaded shares via the OFS.

Since listing, the company’s shares have more than doubled from the IPO price of ₹124. Shares of Aequs ended Friday’s trading session 1.38% higher at ₹246.20.

article_title: Zelio E-Mobility To Raise ₹168 Cr Via Preferential Issue
article_excerpt:
Electric vehicle (EV) manufacturer Zelio E-Mobility’s board of directors approved a proposal today to raise up to ₹167.95 Cr via a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants to fund its growth initiatives.

The BSE SME listed company will issue up to 9.73 Lakh equity shares at an issue price of ₹853 per share to four non-promoter institutional and private investors, aggregating to nearly ₹83 Cr. The allottees would be Motilal Oswal Financial Services to get ₹40.1 Cr, Calliope Capital Advisors LLP (₹31.4 Cr), Param Value Investments (₹8.5 Cr), and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund (nearly ₹3 Cr).

Simultaneously, the board approved issuing over 9.96 Lakh convertible warrants at the same issue price to three promoters, Niraj Arya, Deepak Arya, and Kunal Arya, to raise an additional sum of nearly ₹85 Cr.

For the warrants, the promoters will pay 25% or ₹21.24 Cr at the time of allotment, while the remaining 75% (₹63.72 Cr) will be payable when the warrants are converted into equity shares. The warrants can be converted within 18 months of allotment.

Following the full conversion of warrants and allotment of equity shares, the promoter group’s stake in Zelio will dilute from 72.8% to 70.9%, whilst public shareholding will rise from 27.2% to 29.1%.

As the total issue exceeds ₹100 Cr, the board appointed SEBI-registered Brickwork Ratings India to monitor how the proceeds of the fundraise would be utilised in accordance with regulations.

The company will seek shareholder approval via an EGM, which is scheduled for October 20. Separately, shareholders will be asked to approve related-party transactions of up to ₹50 Cr each with five entities — Torque Innovation EV, AVR Auto Industries, Jai Bharat Engineering Tools, Jai Bharat Auto Components, Rajdhani Machinery Store.

Zelio says these transactions will be conducted in the ordinary course of business and on an arm’s-length basis.

Founded in 2021 by Neeraj Arya, Hisar-based Zelio manufactures electric vehicles, primarily low-speed electric scooters. It operates in over 25 states with a network of more than 300 dealers. The startup made its debut on the BSE SME platform in 2025, raising ₹78.34 Cr.

The EV manufacturer operated manufacturing units in Ladwa, Hisar, Alarpur, Cuttack and a warehousing facility in Chandan Nagar. It claims to have a footprint across 400 cities and towns across India.

In July, the company also inaugurated a manufacturing plant in Coimbatore to expand its presence in Southern India. With the establishment of the Coimbatore factory, Zelio is now looking to enhance its manufacturing capabilities from 1.8 Lakh units per annum to 2.4 Lakh units per annum in Q2 FY27.

“Coimbatore facility has an installed production and assembly capacity of 60,000 units per annum. During its initial phase of operations, the plant is expected to manufacture and assemble approximately 24,000-30,000 E2Ws annually, with production gradually scaling in line with market demand and operational ramp-up,” the company had said.

By the end of FY27, Zelio is looking to expand its dealership network to 550 from 400 in 25 states at the end of FY26.

On the financial front, Zelio’s standalone profit soared 75.4% to ₹28 Cr in FY26. The EV maker set up a new auto components manufacturing subsidiary, Zelio Auto Components, in May 2025. Including the financial performance of the newly set up subsidiary, Zelio’s consolidated operating revenue for FY26 stood at ₹310.7 Cr.

Meanwhile, Zelio is not the first listed new-age tech company to return to the capital markets to raise fresh capital. Among other listed competitors in the EV space, Ola Electric raised ₹780 Cr in June and Ather raised ₹1,300 Cr in July , both utilising Qualified Institutional Placements (QIPs). Ola Electric is mulling another QIP as of now, with its board approving the raise of ₹1,500 Cr via the markets three months after raising fresh funds.

Shares of Zelio ended today’s trading session 4.99% higher at ₹986.90.

company_description: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs has raised $47 Mn (about ₹439 Cr) to expand its data collection and robot deployment operations.
article_title: Humyn Labs Raises $47 Mn To Collect Training Data For Robots
article_excerpt:
Physical AI startup Humyn Labs has raised $47 Mn (about ₹439 Cr) to expand its data collection and robot deployment operations. The round comprises $26 Mn in Series A equity led by Accel and $21 Mn in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Other equity investors included Prosus, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finserv Intelligence, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Jump Trading LLC, and angel investor Anita Pramoda.

Founded earlier this year by former Nazara CEO Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs collects data across more than 20 countries. It works with AI research labs, robotics companies, and developers of world models, which simulate how physical environments change in response to actions. The startup claims it crossed $50 Mn in annualised revenue within six months of starting operations.

The San Francisco-based startup plans to expand its robot deployment operations to Brazil, South Korea, and India. It also plans to strengthen its data collection hardware and processing capabilities and build out its presence in San Francisco, London, and Seoul.

Humyn Labs claims to have crossed $50 Mn in annualised revenue within six months of starting operations.

The startup plans to expand its robot deployment operations to Brazil, South Korea and India. It will also strengthen its data collection hardware and processing capabilities and expand its presence across San Francisco, London and Seoul.

Physical AI refers to AI systems that interact with the real world through robots and other machines. Unlike conventional AI models that primarily process digital information, these systems need to understand how objects move, how humans perform tasks and how to respond to changing physical environments.

For instance, a warehouse robot must learn to pick up different objects, navigate obstacles and handle materials without requiring instructions for every movement.

Humyn Labs aims to address this challenge by recording how people perform tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. Its proprietary devices capture human movements and interactions, which are then converted into labelled datasets to train robotics models.

The startup also works with robotics developers to test robots in real-world environments and improve their performance.

The opportunity extends beyond building robots. According to a July 2026 report by Counterpoint Research, India’s data collection and annotation services for physical AI could unlock a $10 Bn revenue opportunity by 2030.

The country’s large workforce, diverse working environments and relatively low data collection costs could make it an attractive destination for companies seeking real-world training data for robotics systems.

However, the business also raises questions around privacy , consent and the ownership of training data.

Physical AI datasets can involve recordings of people inside their homes, factories and workplaces. Such footage may capture personal information, household activities, workplace processes and commercially sensitive details.

This makes informed consent, data storage and restrictions on how recordings are shared particularly important. Questions also remain around how workers are compensated and whether they retain any control over footage used to train commercial AI systems.

There is a broader labour question, too. The workers whose movements are being recorded are helping train systems that could eventually automate some of their jobs. Warehousing, packaging, assembly-line operations, cleaning and inventory management are among the activities that physical AI-powered robots could increasingly take over.

This creates a potential contradiction at the heart of the emerging industry: human labour is becoming an important input in developing technologies designed to reduce dependence on human labour.

article_title: Zavya Nets ₹22.6 Cr To Scale Everyday Silver Jewellery Biz
article_excerpt:
Budget jewellery startup Zavya has raised ₹22.6 Cr ($2.4 Mn) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment arm of Daksham Capital, with participation from existing investor Orios Venture Partners.

The investment values the silver jewellery brand at approximately ₹191.5 Cr on a post-money basis.

“With DGV joining us and Orios continuing to back us, we are excited to strengthen our presence across D2C and quick commerce, invest in long-term brand building and take our first steps into physical retail,” Zavya cofounder and CEO Poem Kabra said.

Founded in  2021 by Kabra and Ravi Malani, Zavya offers silver jewellery targeted for 22-35 year old women. Its everyday 925 sterling silver jewelry, including products like individual rings, pendants, earrings, and anklets, are priced between ₹699-2,299. The startup claims to come up with over 50 new styles every month.

The five-year old brand sees a robust opportunity in scaling in the world’s largest silver jewellery market by fabrication volume.

A report by Credence Research estimates India’s 925 sterling silver jewellery D2C market at $614 Mn in 2025 and projects it to reach $2.28 Bn by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 14%. The report identifies online channels as the largest distribution segment, accounting for 60% of market value in 2025, while quick commerce is expected to be among the faster-growing channels.

In this market, Zavya competes with legacy Beliram Legacy, TrueSilver, and Silver Emporium. Meanwhile, it is one of the up and coming new-age jewellery brands that bid to capitalise on the growing market opportunity and challenge the incumbents. Backed by strong venture capital backing, brands like Giva and Palmonas are also bidding to take on legacy giants with their select, premium-feel offerings at more affordable price ranges.

Omnichannel fast fashion brand Style Union’s parent Nexon Omniverse Ltd has raised ₹485 Cr (nearly $51.8 Mn) in its Series E funding round co-led by Venturi Partners and Elev8 Venture Partners.

article_title: Recove Ventures Nets ₹56 Cr To Expand Recycling Business
article_excerpt:
Bengaluru-based Recove Ventures has raised ₹56.3 Cr (slightly over $6 Mn) in a funding round from investors like Samara Capital’s CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global, Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust, 5F World’s Ganesh Natarajan and Chaitanya Kejriwal (Parkson’s Packaging).

Out of the total capital raise, ₹36.3 Cr came by way of equity allotment and the remaining is debt.

The recycling startup plans to invest in spreading its infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand its footprint in Karnataka.

The startup is targeting investments of over ₹2,000 Cr across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh over the next decade. It has signed 10-year MoUs with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, each involving proposed investments of more than ₹500 Cr.

Founded in 2024 by Viral Chhajer, Kunal Kumar, Aayush Killa and Sharan Subaiah, Recove recycles plastic waste and sells it to companies that use such plastic to make new products. The startup claims to source its plastic waste from over 200 suppliers and sells its recycled plastic to over 40 customers.

The startup is expanding across collection, segregation, washing and granulation. Its approach is to source and pre-process waste closer to where it is generated before moving it to larger facilities for further processing.

It currently operates a washing facility at Harohalli in Bengaluru, which procures around 600 tonnes of  plastic monthly as well as a pre-processing unit in Pune. Three more facilities are under development.

Of this, a granulation plant at Maharashtra’s Jalgaon is expected to produce a monthly capacity of 1,100 tonnes. For context, granulation is the process of grinding plastic scrap into small, uniform pieces.

The two year old startup sees a goldmine in waste plastic, claiming that billions of dollars worth recyclable plastic go to landfills each year in India. It sees a market opportunity of over $4 Bn up for grabs, and believes its organised supply chain infra could help save up a significant chunk of the $36 Bn plastic waste between 2025-30.

However, the opportunity spans multiple waste streams, including electronic waste and metals, with businesses building solutions across collection, processing, material recovery and compliance.

For instance, waste-management platform Recykal, which raised $23 Mn , is digitising waste management. Cricketer Sachin Tendulkar also backed Recykal justed a few days ago.

Other startups are targeting different parts of the value chain. ScrapUncle raised ₹22 Cr in January 2026 to expand its waste collection and fulfilment infrastructure across Delhi-NCR. Similarly,  Karo Sambhav secured ₹56 Cr from Rainmatter in June 2026 to scale its recycling infrastructure for recovering critical and high-value materials from end-of-life products.

company_description: offers US Stock tokens trading platform for Indian traders
article_title: Mochatrade Raises $5.5 Mn To Build A US Stock Trading Platform For Indian Traders
article_excerpt:
Fintech startup Mochatrade, which offers US Stock tokens trading platform for Indian traders, announced the raise of $5.5 Mn (₹52.3 Cr) in a seed funding round led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Zero Knowledge Ventures, among others.

The startup will use the fresh capital to bolster its trading engine and risk infrastructure and expand its reach among active Indian traders.

Founded in 2026 by Utkarsh Sinha, Chetan Manda and Parth Maheshwari, Mochatrade is building a trading platform that allows Indian retail traders and global investors to trade perpetual futures and price-tracking contracts linked to US stocks, cryptocurrencies, commodities and major indices.

Its waitlist has crossed 25,000 sign-ups, although it is yet to announce a public launch date.

The platform is expected to allow users to fund their accounts through UPI and track balances, margins and profit and loss (P&L) in Indian rupees (INR).

The platform’s perpetual futures contracts will allow traders to take long or short positions based on their expectations of price movements, without owning the underlying assets. Unlike conventional futures contracts, these instruments have no fixed expiry date.

Mochatrade will also offer leveraged trading, allowing users to take larger positions with less upfront capital. However, leverage can amplify losses as well as gains. The startup plans to earn revenue through trading fees and eventually introduce contracts linked to select pre-IPO companies, US stock options and social trading features, subject to regulatory approvals.

“India traded $1.9 Tn in options premium turnover last year. The appetite to trade is already here. But when Indians want to trade the US market, the product still feels foreign,” said Sinha, CEO of Mochatrade.

Sinha previously cofounded crypto wallet Martian in 2022, which recorded more than 2 Mn installs and $2 Bn in transaction volume. Martian raised $3.6 Mn from Race Capital, Superscrypt and Jump Crypto before being acquired by Lightspeed-backed Pontem.

Manda became Sprinklr’s youngest director of product in 2025, while Maheshwari worked on Photoshop for the web at Adobe before leading payments and credit infrastructure at Navi.

Mochatrade is entering the market as Indian investors increasingly look overseas for exposure to global assets, particularly US stocks.

According to RBI data, Indian residents remitted $2.65 Bn overseas for equity and debt investments in FY26, up from $1.51 Bn in FY24. Remittances reached $1.4 Bn between April and July FY27, with July alone accounting for $344.6 Mn, a 121% year-on-year increase. These figures cover overseas equity and debt investments across markets, rather than US stocks alone.

At the same time, regulatory changes are reshaping India’s domestic trading market. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has tightened futures and options (F&O) rules to curb excessive speculation and protect retail investors.

Measures include limiting weekly expiries to one benchmark index per exchange, increasing contract sizes and tightening margin requirements. The changes have weighed on trading activity and revenue at several brokerage platforms, including Zerodha and Groww, during FY26.

Against this backdrop, Mochatrade is betting that demand for global market exposure will create an opportunity for a trading platform built around Indian users. Its ability to convert waitlist interest into active traders will depend on its product experience, risk controls and the regulatory framework governing the contracts it plans to offer.

company_description: Fintech startup axiTrust is in talks to raise around $5 Mn in fresh capital in its Series A funding round, people aware of the matter told Inc42 on the condition of anonymity.
article_title: Exclusive: axiTrust To Raise $5 Mn From Argor.vc, Others
article_excerpt:
Fintech startup axiTrust is in talks to raise around $5 Mn in fresh capital in its Series A funding round, people aware of the matter told Inc42 on the condition of anonymity.

The fresh round is likely to be led by Singapore based Argor.vc, and will see participation from axiTrust’s existing investor General Catalyst.

Questions sent to axiTrust didn’t elicit any response at the time of publishing the story.

The fresh round has come almost a year after the startup raised $2.6 Mn in its seed funding round led by General Catalyst. Other investors  including Atrium Angels, YAN Network and Supermorpheous are also on the fintech startup’s cap table.

The fresh capital will help the startup build digital infrastructure to accelerate adoption of its surety bonds offering.

For context, surety bonds are insurance-backed guarantees that assure a buyer or project owner that a business will fulfil its contractual obligations. Instead of blocking the capital as collateral, they allow the buyers to pay a premium to secure the guarantee, helping free up working capital and reduce financial strain.

Founded in 2024  by Aditya Tulsian (CEO), Rajeev Chari (COO), and Mukund Daga (CRO), axiTrust issues, underwrites and manages digital surety bonds, providing an alternative to traditional, collateral-heavy bank guarantees.

As per the startup, more than ₹15 Lakh Cr of MSME working capital is locked up as collateral for bank guarantees, and replacing these traditional guarantees with insurance-backed digital surety bonds can free that capital, expand credit access, and improve trust in business transactions.

From digital underwriting and AI-based risk assessment to cashflow-based lending and embedded finance, they are filling long-standing gaps that traditional banks could not address efficiently. These solutions are helping businesses and consumers access credit with fewer delays, lighter paperwork, and better transparency.

Investors are actively backing such startups because the lending market in India is massive, still underserved, and primed for digital disruption offering both strong growth potential and meaningful financial inclusion.

As per Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026 , the fintech sector saw funding of $243 Mn across 13 deals. Of these, the heavy lifting was done by lendingtech startup Centricity ₹280 Cr round and Navi’s $100 Mn pre-IPO funding.

article_title: Swara Baby Products Secures SEBI Nod For ₹1,000 Cr IPO
article_excerpt:
Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products and a subsidiary of omnichannel kidswear brand FirstCry’s parent Brainbees Solutions, has received approval from SEBI for its proposed ₹1,000 Cr IPO. Swara Baby Products filed its DRHP in July this year. According to SEBI’s latest processing status update, the regulator issued the final observation today.

The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹500 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of shares aggregating up to ₹500 Cr.

Brainbees Solutions, which owns a 76.6% stake in Swara Baby Products, will sell shares worth up to ₹300 Cr through the OFS. Another promoter selling shareholder, Anadya Bon Merchari LLP, will offload shares worth up to ₹200 Cr. The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹100 Cr.

Swara Baby Products plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue primarily to expand its manufacturing capacity and pare debt.

Around ₹198.2 Cr will be used to set up a new manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh, while ₹100 Cr will go towards repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings. Another ₹27.5 Cr will be invested in subsidiaries Solis Hygiene, Swara Hygiene and K.A. Enterprises Hygiene Pvt Ltd (KAEHPL) for debt repayment.

The company also plans to pursue inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions, alongside general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2018 by Alok Birla, Rahul Bubna and Ritum Jain, Swara Baby Products manufactures disposable hygiene products across the baby care, adult incontinence, and feminine hygiene categories.

Its portfolio includes baby pant-style and tape-style diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins and panty liners. The company primarily operates as a contract manufacturer for corporate customers, while also selling its own brands, including Cuddles in baby diapers and Shield in adult diapers.

Swara Baby Products counts Brainbees Solutions, Piramal Pharma, and Himalaya Wellness among its customers. It acquired feminine hygiene manufacturer KAEHPL in December 2025.

According to the DRHP, Swara Baby Products was India’s largest hygiene contract manufacturer by value in FY25 across baby diapers, adult diapers and sanitary napkins.

It held a 37% market share by value in India’s baby diaper contract manufacturing segment in FY25 and grew 21.9% YoY in FY26. In adult diapers, it held an estimated 36% market share by value in FY25, with the business growing 24.9% YoY in FY26.

The company currently operates four manufacturing facilities spread across 24 acres in Pithampur and Indore in Madhya Pradesh. On the financial front, it reported a net profit of ₹95.6 Cr in FY26 , up 18.5% from ₹80.7 Cr in FY25. Operating revenue grew 23.4% to ₹1,163 Cr from ₹943 Cr in FY25.

company_description: D2C consumer appliance startup Atomberg’s board passed a special resolution to raise up to ₹450 Cr via an initial public offering (IPO) during an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) held last week, on August 12.
article_title: Atomberg Gets Board Nod To Raise Over ₹450 Cr Via IPO
article_excerpt:
D2C consumer appliance startup Atomberg’s board passed a special resolution to raise up to ₹450 Cr via an initial public offering (IPO) during an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) held last week, on August 12.

The proposed public issue will comprise a combination of fresh equity issuance and an offer for sale by existing shareholders, subject to market conditions and regulatory clearances from SEBI, as per the startup’s disclosures filed with the MCA.

Additionally, the startup’s board also approved the raise of up to ₹90 Cr via a pre-IPO placement of equity shares.

“In the event of a pre-IPO placement, the size of the offer would be reduced from the fresh issue portion to the extent of equity shares issued under the pre-IPO placement subject to the offer satisfying the minimum offer size requirements under the SCRR and applicable laws,” the filings read.

The development was first reported by Entrack.

The consumer appliance maker had taken the first step on its path of becoming a publicly listed company a few weeks ago by converting into a public entity .

Additionally, the size of its potential pre-IPO transaction appears to be significantly larger than earlier believed. Atomberg had earlier sought to raise ₹40 Cr in a secondary funding round led by Forj Capital, cofounder Sibabrata Das told Inc42 last year.

Founded in 2012 by IIT Bombay alumni Manoj Meena and Das, Atomberg began with B2B sales of energy-efficient BLDC fans before entering the consumer market in 2016. Since then, it has also further diversified into a range of product categories like mixer grinders, water purifiers, etc, though fans continue to generate the largest share of its revenue.

The startup sells its products via its own website, ecommerce platforms like Amazon and Flipkart, as well as via offline channels.

It has raised a total funding of about $126.5 Mn to date from investors like Inflexor Ventures, Trifecta Capital Advisors, Steadview Capital, Temasek Holdings, Jungle Ventures among others.

On the financial front, Atomberg reduced its net losses by 41% to ₹117 Cr in FY25. Meanwhile, its operating revenue jumped over 20% to ₹958.4 Cr while expenses rose 9% to ₹1,118.3 Cr. The startup is yet to disclose its financial results for the fiscal year FY26.

article_title: Compute Desk Raises $45 Million To Build Compute Risk Markets
article_excerpt:
Compute Desk has raised $45 million in a funding round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners to build infrastructure for pricing, trading, hedging, and clearing computing capacity. Other investors include Menlo Ventures, Hedosophia, Motive Partners, Crucible Capital, Inovia Capital, Soma Capital, Mythos Ventures, Blue Wire Capital, Firesteak Ventures and Drysdale Ventures.

The company is developing financial and physical market infrastructure intended to replace or supplement rigid multi-year contracts for graphics processing unit capacity.

Addressing Compute Contract Risk

Artificial intelligence developers require large quantities of computing capacity, but that capacity is often financed and sold through long-term offtake agreements.

Cloud infrastructure providers and their lenders may require customers to commit to years of usage even when future requirements remain uncertain.

These agreements transfer risk to the buyer and may expose sellers and lenders to counterparty defaults. Compute Desk wants to create tools that allow market participants to price and hedge those risks more efficiently.

Its team includes quantitative portfolio managers, commodities traders and GPU engineers with experience at Citadel, Two Sigma, Winton, Meta and Amazon Web Services.

Establishing Reference Prices

Compute capacity is commonly negotiated through private contracts, making it difficult for market participants to determine a transparent reference price.

Compute Desk has developed indexes based on private transaction data obtained through price-sharing relationships with cloud infrastructure providers.

Its benchmark family includes DESKB300, DESKB200, DESKH200 and DESKH100, which track pricing connected with different Nvidia GPU generations.

Compute Desk has partnered with Bloomberg and General Index to distribute regulated benchmarks to financial and technology professionals.

Its Compute Signal platform provides pricing assessments used by AI companies, cloud providers and other market participants.

Futures Options And Physical Settlement

Compute Desk is working with Nodal Exchange, Architect Financial and Liquid Compute as they pursue regulatory processes for compute futures and options based on its indexes.

The company has also formed a liquidity network of market makers, brokers, hedge funds, family offices and trading firms.

Its Compute Trader platform provides market access for organizations willing to assume compute-price risk.

Compute Clear, the company’s physical settlement technology, is designed to move computing capacity between buyers and sellers through clearinghouses. It could allow a derivatives position to settle through the delivery of usable compute.

The system may give sellers an alternative to transferring risk through long-term contracts while allowing buyers to obtain capacity for shorter periods. The market remains at an early stage, and its development will depend on liquidity, standardization, regulation and adoption.

KEY QUOTES:

We are building the best team on the planet at pricing and clearing compute risk.

Andrawes Bahou, Founder and CEO of Compute Desk

Compute is the largest input in the AI economy. Regardless of whether there is a compute glut or shortage, it is bought and sold through outdated contracts that can’t keep up with the magnitude of demand and its associated risks. The company is also opening a private beta for Atlas through a waitlist.

The AI agent learns user preferences, including frequent travel companions, preferred activities, and spending limits. This information is intended to reduce the need for travelers to provide the same requirements whenever they begin planning a new trip.

Atlas can book flights, hotels, and activities through supplier partnerships rather than only returning links to other websites.

The agent also supports local plans, including hikes, restaurant reservations, and free activities nearby. Voyage Labs is positioning the product for both major trips and shorter outings.

article_title: Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
article_excerpt:
Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences have entered into a strategic funding agreement under which funds managed by Blackstone will provide up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support the clinical development of berobenatide, Pfizer’s investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.

The agreement will help Pfizer advance its obesity drug development program while maintaining financial flexibility to invest in other therapeutic areas. In exchange for its funding commitment, Blackstone will become eligible for milestone-based payments tied to U.S. regulatory approval and commercial performance.

Berobenatide is being developed as a potential first-in-class monthly injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide. Pfizer is evaluating the treatment for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions, including knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea.

The transaction represents a significant investment in Pfizer’s cardiometabolic pipeline as the pharmaceutical company advances a broad portfolio of investigational obesity therapies.

How The $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement Works

Under the agreement, Blackstone-managed funds will cover up to $1.5 billion in development expenses associated with berobenatide through 2028.

In return, Blackstone will be eligible to receive payments if the drug achieves specified regulatory and commercial milestones.

These payments are contingent on U.S. regulatory approval of monthly injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management and the achievement of certain sales targets.

Any milestone payments earned by Blackstone would be distributed over multiple years.

The structure allows Pfizer to obtain external funding for a major clinical development program without selling ownership or commercial rights to the investigational medicine.

Pfizer will retain full operational control and decision-making authority over berobenatide, including its clinical development strategy.

The agreement also does not provide Blackstone with an ownership interest in the drug.

Funds managed by Blackstone’s perpetual private equity strategy, BXPE, will participate alongside funds managed by Blackstone Life Sciences.

The arrangement illustrates an alternative approach to financing pharmaceutical research, in which investment firms provide capital to support clinical development in exchange for payments linked to future milestones.

For Pfizer, the agreement provides an opportunity to share development costs while retaining control over a potentially important pipeline asset.

Berobenatide Targets Monthly GLP-1 Treatment

Berobenatide is an investigational GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide being studied for chronic weight management and related medical conditions.

GLP-1 receptor agonists act on biological pathways involved in appetite regulation, blood glucose control, and other metabolic processes.

Existing treatments in this drug class have established a significant market for obesity and metabolic disease therapies.

Pfizer is developing berobenatide as a potential monthly injectable treatment, which could offer a different administration schedule from therapies requiring more frequent dosing.

The company is pursuing an extensive clinical development program to evaluate the drug’s safety and effectiveness.

Pfizer plans to advance more than 20 clinical trials involving obesity and associated medical conditions during 2026.

These include 10 ongoing and planned Phase 3 trials for berobenatide.

The studies are intended to evaluate the treatment across chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.

Pfizer is also investigating berobenatide in combination with other investigational therapies.

The company is studying combinations involving nutrient-stimulated hormone peptides, including amylin analogs.

article_title: Apiary Therapeutics Raises C$7.3 Million To Advance Engineered B Cell Therapies
article_excerpt:
Apiary Therapeutics has closed a C$7.3 million seed financing to develop engineered B cells designed to produce therapeutic proteins inside the body over extended periods.

Genesys Capital and the Business Development Bank of Canada’s Life Sciences Venture Fund co-led the round. InBC Investment Corp. and Mission BioCapital also participated.

The Canadian biotechnology company will use the proceeds to advance its platform, move its first program toward preclinical validation, scale manufacturing and expand its teams in Vancouver and Toronto.

Developing An Off-The-Shelf Protein Delivery Platform

Many protein and enzyme therapies require repeated injections or infusions. Apiary is developing an alternative approach using B cells, immune cells naturally specialized for protein production.

The company aims to manufacture these cells from induced pluripotent stem cells rather than collecting and modifying cells from each patient. The resulting allogeneic platform is intended to support off-the-shelf treatments that produce a therapeutic protein following a single administration.

Apiary plans to use a common stem cell bank and a defined manufacturing process across its programs. Under that approach, developing a new therapy would involve a new gene edit while retaining the shared cell-production foundation.

Potential applications include enzyme replacement, protein deficiencies, autoimmune diseases and oncology. The financing supports testing and development of the platform; its proposed durability and therapeutic effects remain to be established.

Building On Canadian Research And Manufacturing Expertise

Apiary was founded using technology invented at the University of British Columbia and incubated through CCRM’s company creation and investment program.

Its founders include CCRM, UBC Professor Peter Zandstra and University of Manitoba Assistant Professor Yale Michaels.

The seed round adds to non-dilutive support from Genome Canada, Genome BC and the Stem Cell Network, alongside earlier investment from CCRM Enterprises and the Ontario Centre of Innovation.

The next stage centers on demonstrating the platform preclinically while developing a scalable manufacturing process for future protein-delivery programs.

Yale Michaels, PhD, Co-Founder Of Apiary Therapeutics And Assistant Professor At The University Of Manitoba
