company_description: Arva AI has raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand artificial intelligence models and agents designed for regulated banking and financial technology operations.
article_title: Arva AI Raises $20 Million To Automate Critical Banking Operations
article_excerpt:
Arva AI has raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand artificial intelligence models and agents designed for regulated banking and financial technology operations. Arthur Ventures led the round, with continued participation from Y Combinator and Gradient Ventures.

The company plans to prioritize investment in Arva Research, its internal model-development organization, while expanding its technology across banking back-office functions ranging from financial crime compliance to lending.

The financing follows several large deployments, including implementations at a top-10 U.S. bank, an S&P 500 payments company, and Wise.

Building Models For Explainable Financial Decisions

Banks make large numbers of decisions involving customer eligibility, financial crime risks, lending, transaction monitoring, and regulatory compliance.

Many of these decisions still require manual review because financial institutions must be able to explain their conclusions to auditors and regulators. General-purpose AI models may produce inconsistent or unsupported answers unless people verify the results.

Arva is developing proprietary models for decision stages where accuracy, evidence, and auditability are particularly important.

The company’s first research model, Arva Intel, investigates businesses and individuals using online information. In Arva’s internal testing, the model produced accuracy results 13% better than leading general-purpose alternatives.

Because this result comes from company testing, its broader performance will depend on the evaluation methodology, datasets, use cases, and models used for comparison.

Arva Intel operates alongside AgentCore, the company’s continual-learning infrastructure. AgentCore adapts the system to an individual bank’s policies, historical decisions, and operating processes.

The combination is intended to give banks AI agents that can perform research and operational tasks while producing results that institutions can review and explain.

Funding Follows Arva Research Launch

Arva launched Arva Research in September 2026. The new funding will support continued development of specialized models for banking operations.

The company’s strategy reflects a belief that financial institutions will require domain-specific systems rather than relying solely on general-purpose models. A banking agent must understand regulatory expectations, follow institutional policies, and maintain a record of how it reached a conclusion.

Boston Consulting Group has estimated that AI agents could reduce banking costs by between 30% and 40% by 2030. Achieving those savings would require institutions to move beyond pilots and allow AI systems to complete consequential work reliably.

Arva was founded in 2024 by CEO Rhim Shah and Chief Technology Officer Oliver Wales. Shah previously led financial crime products at Revolut Business, while Wales was formerly chief product engineer at Seal.

Their backgrounds combine regulated financial operations with AI product engineering. Arva is initially focused on financial crime compliance and lending, but it intends to extend its models and agents across additional back-office processes.

KEY QUOTES:

This year our customers started handing real critical decisions to Arva. How far that goes depends on accuracy, which is why we built Arva Research and why it’s where this funding goes first. Banks still run most of their back office by hand. We’re building the models that let them hand that work to agents and trust the result.

Rhim Shah, Co-Founder and CEO of Arva AI

Banks need AI they can trust with their most consequential decisions. Arva has built a rare combination of deep domain expertise, exceptional technical capability, and a clear commitment to accuracy and auditability. We’re excited to partner with Rhim and the team as they build the models and infrastructure for critical banking operations.

Patrick Meenan, General Partner at Arthur Ventures

article_title: Aarden Raises $8 Million To Build AI Platform For Land Markets
article_excerpt:
Aarden has raised $8 million to expand an artificial intelligence platform that helps landowners, developers, and investors evaluate potential uses and values for large properties. Overture Ventures led the round, with participation from Madrona and Propeller Ventures.

The financing brings Aarden’s total funding to $12 million within its first 15 months. The Seattle-based company previously raised a $4 million round led by Planeteer in June 2025.

Aarden will use the new capital to expand its team, support more landowners and land managers, develop real-time market intelligence, and prepare sites for transactions involving energy, data center, housing, industrial, and other infrastructure projects.

Analyzing Land For Energy And AI Infrastructure

Aarden has developed AI-based tools and services that evaluate land using hundreds of property and market attributes.

The platform is intended to help users understand how a particular site could be used, what it may be worth, and which landowners, developers, or investors could be appropriate transaction partners.

Demand for suitable land is increasing as companies build data centers, energy facilities, transmission infrastructure, housing, and new industrial projects.

These developments often require properties with access to power, suitable physical characteristics, clear title, supportive communities, and owners willing to sell or lease the land.

Identifying properties that satisfy these requirements can involve fragmented databases, manual research, lengthy due diligence, and relationship-building across multiple organizations.

Aarden plans to connect these activities through a combination of property intelligence, market data, landowner and developer networks, and transaction services.

Using Hundreds Of Land Attributes

Aarden’s platform analyzes historical market information and hundreds of attributes associated with individual properties.

Its models evaluate development suitability, valuation trends, entity ownership, and community sentiment. These factors can help users determine whether a property may be appropriate for timber production, conservation, solar energy, data centers, industrial development, housing, or another use.

The company says it validates the accuracy of its site-selection models by measuring how effectively they identify properties that developers later select and convert.

Aarden did not disclose detailed independent validation results, accuracy rates, or comparisons with competing land-analysis platforms.

Its technology is intended to support professional diligence rather than replace legal, environmental, engineering, financial, or regulatory reviews.

Working Across 14 Million Acres

The purchase agreement includes an upfront cash payment and additional payments tied to specified clinical and regulatory milestones.

Its initial therapeutic programs address essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis associated with mutations in calreticulin, known as mCALR.

Existing therapies frequently focus on managing symptoms and reducing complications.

Calytrix is developing an alternative approach intended to target the underlying disease-driving mutations.

Calytrix’s lead asset is an investigational biparatopic antibody designed to recognize mutant calreticulin.

A biparatopic antibody can bind to two distinct regions of a molecular target.

The company’s program is designed to target both Type 1 and Type 2 mCALR mutations, which are associated with certain myeloproliferative neoplasms.

Mutant calreticulin provides a potential tumor-specific cell-surface target.

Calytrix aims to develop a therapy capable of eliminating disease-driving mutant cell populations while preserving healthy blood-forming tissues.

The approach could potentially support earlier intervention and longer-term treatment if future studies establish an acceptable safety and efficacy profile.

However, the program remains preclinical and has not yet demonstrated clinical benefits in patients.

Expanding Lilly’s Blood Cancer Research

The acquisition will expand Lilly’s presence in myeloproliferative neoplasms and complement its existing capabilities in blood cancers.

Lilly intends to advance Calytrix’s lead program into clinical development and investigate its potential across relevant patient populations.

The transaction is designed to accelerate work on a precision medicine approach that targets a disease-associated mutation rather than primarily addressing its downstream symptoms.

Calytrix President and CEO Brad Prosek said the company was established with the goal of changing disease progression in patients with mCALR-driven essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis.

Company Formation And Financing

The company launched with Series A financing co-led by J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital and Westlake BioPartners.

It subsequently completed a Series B financing led by Avoro Ventures.

The proposed sale to Lilly follows a relatively short period of company development focused on advancing its lead therapeutic program toward clinical testing.

Centerview Partners is serving as exclusive financial advisor to Calytrix, while Goodwin Procter is acting as its legal counsel.

Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison is serving as legal counsel to Lilly.

The company takes a hardware-agnostic approach, allowing its technologies to work across different quantum computing and sensing platforms.

This approach positions Q-CTRL as a provider of infrastructure software that could support multiple participants across the quantum technology industry.

Ridero enables lenders and automotive retailers to offer products such as new- and used-vehicle leases and balloon financing. These structures depend on estimating the value a vehicle will retain at the end of an agreement and managing the financial exposure associated with that residual value.

Additional partnerships with lenders and automotive software providers are under development. Broad integration will be important because dealers typically use several systems for inventory, customer management, transaction processing, and lender submissions.

The company will also use the capital to expand its research, manufacturing, and operational capabilities as it advances multiple brain-computer interface technologies.

Science is focused on developing systems that establish connections between the nervous system and external technologies, with the goal of restoring capabilities that have been affected by disease or injury.

Its PRIMA platform represents an important part of that strategy, targeting vision loss associated with certain forms of advanced macular degeneration.

Expanding PRIMA In Europe And The United States

PRIMA is a brain-computer interface designed to restore a degree of functional vision in patients who have lost sight because of certain types of late-stage macular degeneration.

The technology has received CE marking in Europe, allowing it to be made available within the scope of its authorized medical indication.

The regulatory milestone represents an important step toward making the technology accessible to patients who have experienced severe vision loss.

Unlike conventional treatments that primarily aim to slow the progression of retinal disease, PRIMA is designed to help restore a specific form of visual function.

The system focuses on enabling form vision, which includes the ability to recognize shapes and visual information such as letters, numbers, and words.

For individuals with profound vision impairment, recovering even limited form vision could potentially improve their ability to perform certain reading and recognition tasks.

However, the degree of visual function restored may vary between patients, and the technology is not intended to provide the full range of capabilities associated with natural eyesight.

CE marking also does not establish that every patient who meets the treatment criteria will experience the same degree of benefit.

Science plans to use part of its new financing to expand access to PRIMA across European markets, supporting the infrastructure and operational capabilities needed for broader deployment.

Commercial expansion will require coordination among healthcare providers, medical specialists, and other participants involved in evaluating patients and delivering the technology.

As availability increases, the company will also need to support clinical implementation, patient selection, and ongoing evaluation of treatment outcomes.

Preparing For U.S. Regulatory Approval

In parallel with its European expansion, Science is pursuing authorization for PRIMA in the United States.

The company is seeking approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration through the Humanitarian Device Exemption pathway.

This regulatory framework is intended for certain medical devices designed to address diseases or conditions affecting relatively small patient populations.

Under this pathway, eligible devices are evaluated according to requirements that differ from those applicable to conventional medical device approvals.

The Humanitarian Device Exemption process considers whether the device meets applicable safety requirements and whether its probable benefit outweighs the risks associated with its use, among other criteria.

company_description: Vero Security has raised $11 million in seed funding to develop technology for securing the AI tools and autonomous agents used inside large organizations.
article_title: Vero Security Raises $11 Million To Build AI Security Engineering Platform
article_excerpt:
Vero Security has raised $11 million in seed funding to develop technology for securing the AI tools and autonomous agents used inside large organizations. TLV Partners led the round, with participation from GTM Capital, Maple Capital, and angel investors.

Founded in 2025, Vero already serves multiple Fortune 500 companies. It will use the capital to expand platform coverage, support more security workflows, and grow its U.S. commercial organization.

The company is also launching AISecurityEngineering.org, an open community providing field guides, workshops, and a credential program for professionals responsible for enterprise AI security.

AI Security Becomes A Distinct Responsibility

Research from IANS and Artico Search found that 65% of companies with at least $10 billion in revenue had assigned someone to lead AI security.

Only 18% had created a dedicated position. At most of the other organizations, responsibility was added to an executive’s existing duties.

The role involves tracking new AI tools, agent permissions, integrations, connected systems, plugins, and models while vendors continuously change their products.

Vero aims to perform much of this ongoing work rather than providing another dashboard that only lists problems.

Security teams define policies and decide which changes can be automated. Vero then implements controls, coordinates remediation, verifies completion, and adjusts protections as AI products evolve.

Runtime Governor Enforces Policy During Execution

Vero’s AI Runtime Governor inspects supported prompts, agent actions, and tool calls when they occur.

It can block an AI coding agent from reading unnecessary secrets, prevent an agent from performing prohibited actions, and stop malicious skills or prompt-injection attacks from triggering unauthorized behavior.

The platform works through existing endpoint, identity, AI, and security tools, avoiding the need for employees to install separate software.

One new Fortune 1000 customer established a policy allowing only developers to connect AI agents to corporate code repositories or execute code.

Vero translated the decision into more than 15 controls spanning coding agents, Model Context Protocol servers, skills, identities, and runtime actions.

Founders Elad Tessler and Daniel Meirov previously worked together in Israel’s Unit 8200. Tessler later led product at Astrix Security, while Meirov led research, development, and product at Sightfull.

KEY QUOTES:

CISOs have seen enough dashboards and tables that tell their teams what’s wrong and leave the work to them. AI Security Engineering deserves a better operating model, designed for AI rather than borrowed from other areas of security. We’re working alongside the first generation of AI security leaders and building Vero around what they actually need: a platform that does the work, keeps protections current as AI changes, and brings them only the decisions that require human judgment.

Elad Tessler, Co-Founder and CEO of Vero Security

AI Security Engineering is becoming a core responsibility inside enterprise security organizations. The professionals taking on that responsibility need technology designed for the pace and complexity of AI. Vero is bringing security expertise, continuous execution and runtime enforcement together in a platform built for how this new discipline needs to operate.

Rona Segev, Co-Founder and Managing Partner at TLV Partners

AI is becoming a new attack surface in the enterprise, and we’re hearing directly from CISOs how quickly AI Security Engineering is becoming a distinct responsibility. We evaluated dozens of companies in this space. Vero stood out because it’s building technology that helps security professionals do the work, from understanding risks to enforcing protections. It’s GTM Capital’s first investment in an Israeli-founded cybersecurity company since Cyera.

Saqib Awan, Founder and Managing Director at GTM Capital

article_title: Index Industries: $50 Million Seed Funding To Launch Tokenized U.S. Housing Investment Platform
article_excerpt:
Index Industries, a financial technology company developing infrastructure for housing-linked investment products, has emerged from stealth with $50 million in seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The financing included participation from Polychain Capital, Galaxy Ventures, Wintermute Ventures, and other institutional investors and will support the development of a platform designed to make the approximately $55 trillion U.S. residential housing market accessible through index-based financial products.

Founded in 2026, Index Industries is developing technology that combines housing market benchmarks, tokenization infrastructure, and institutional real estate expertise.

The company’s first initiative will be the U.S. Home Price Index, known as the USHP Index, a proprietary benchmark designed to track changes in residential property prices across the United States.

The index will be calculated daily and will integrate information from major existing housing indices into a single national measure.

Index Industries intends to use the benchmark to support housing market research, portfolio monitoring, and the development of financial products linked to residential property values.

The company believes the index could help investors gain broader exposure to housing market movements without directly purchasing and managing physical properties.

Making The $55 Trillion U.S. Housing Market More Accessible

Residential real estate represents one of the largest asset classes in the United States, with an estimated aggregate value of $55 trillion.

Despite its size, investors seeking exposure to changes in nationwide home prices have historically faced limited options.

Direct property ownership involves substantial capital requirements, ongoing maintenance, transaction expenses, and geographic concentration.

Real estate investment trusts and other existing property investment vehicles provide alternative approaches, but their performance does not necessarily correspond directly to changes in broad residential home prices.

Index Industries is developing infrastructure intended to support a new category of financial products connected to housing market benchmarks.

Its USHP Index will combine data from major residential property indices to provide a regularly updated measure of national home price performance.

The company plans to make the benchmark available for research, reporting, and the creation of housing-linked investment instruments.

The index is expected to launch in the near future.

Launching A Tokenized Housing Investment Product

The first product built on the platform will be USHP, a liquid index-linked product expected to be issued by USHP Limited.

USHP Limited is a British Virgin Islands company and subsidiary of the USHP Foundation, a Cayman Islands foundation company.

The product is intended to provide financial exposure linked to the U.S. Home Price Index through blockchain-based infrastructure.

USHP Limited plans to launch the product on Ethereum in 2026, with a subsequent expansion to Solana planned for 2027.

Tokenization involves representing financial assets or contractual interests through digital tokens recorded on blockchain networks.

Index Industries believes this technology can support the creation and distribution of investment products connected to markets that have traditionally been difficult to access through standardized financial instruments.

The company’s platform combines tokenization technology with real estate and capital markets services intended to support third-party housing-linked products.

Importantly, the proposed USHP product does not represent direct ownership of individual residential properties.

Its structure is designed around financial exposure to an index tracking housing prices.

Index Industries will manage the benchmark and provide supporting technology but will not issue, distribute, market, or redeem USHP.

Any offering of USHP will be conducted separatel

Its underwriting will consider equipment, contracted customers’ creditworthiness and an operator’s ability to service debt.

Angelo Goepel, Partner At Polychain Capital

That gives lenders a clearer basis for deciding how much they can lend and operators a clearer view of how much equity they’ll need to build the next cluster.”

Leon Marshall, Co-Founder And Co-CEO Of Marble

article_title: Lombard Systems Raises $4 Million To Develop Institutional Financing Infrastructure For Tokenized Assets
article_excerpt:
Lombard Systems, a financial technology company developing collateral infrastructure for tokenized securities, has raised $4 million across pre-seed and seed funding rounds led by Ethereal Ventures. The investment will support adoption of the company’s Delivery-versus-Lock (DvL) standard, which lets financial institutions use tokenized assets as loan collateral without transferring them out of existing securities accounts.

The financing included participation from Alps Capital, First Commit Capital, Veris Ventures, Atka, and other investors.

Previously operating under the SemiLiquid/PCP name, Lombard Systems develops technology and legal frameworks intended to modernize secured financing involving digital assets.

Its DvL standard seeks to address a gap between the growing availability of tokenized securities and the traditional infrastructure used for collateralized lending.

Tokenization allows securities and other financial assets to be represented through digital records, potentially supporting more efficient transfers and settlement.

However, financing arrangements involving such assets can still require complicated legal documentation, custody changes, and manual enforcement procedures.

Lombard Systems’ approach allows tokenized assets to remain in accounts maintained by custodians, broker-dealers, or transfer agents while being locked as collateral for a financing arrangement.

The lender receives a security interest documented through a cryptographically signed Credit Receipt.

Under the proposed structure, borrowers retain beneficial ownership of the pledged assets, with agreed enforcement procedures governing delivery of amounts owed following a validated default.

The company intends to support this approach through both technical infrastructure and legal opinions establishing how the framework operates under applicable securities and financing laws.

The new capital will help fund legal analysis in the United States, England, Wales, and five additional jurisdictions.

Lombard Systems will also expand institutional integrations and relationships with organizations capable of maintaining collateral under the DvL standard.

The platform is being designed for several applications, including Lombard loans, margin lending, financing backed by tokenized money market funds and stocks, securities lending, and collateral arrangements involving uncleared derivatives.

Financial institutions will be able to adopt the technology through white-label integrations within their existing systems or through technology partners.

Lombard Systems is targeting its first institutional deployment by the end of 2026.

It also expects to publish the complete DvL standard during the first quarter of 2027.

The company’s operations are based in Dubai and New York.

The financing supports its efforts to establish standardized collateral arrangements as banks, securities firms, and asset managers evaluate the use of tokenized financial instruments.

KEY QUOTES:

“Tokenized stocks and funds are scaling now. Origination and enforcement of loans against tokenized collateral have to be as fast as the assets can move, while staying grounded in existing securities law. DvL keeps assets in their existing securities accounts and gives lenders enforceable rights, with enforcement agreed upfront. That is what turns tokenized assets into usable collateral.”

Rico Van Der Veen, Co-Founder And CEO Of Lombard Systems

“Tokenization is creating real opportunities for financial institutions in trading and settlement, with significant potential to extend those benefits into financing. Lombard Systems is building a critical piece of that infrastructure with DvL, a standardized framework for financing tokenized assets.”

Eeshaan Sachatheva, Co-Chief Investment Officer At Ethereal Ventures

article_title: VersaBank Expands U.S. Structured Receivable Program Into Small Business Lending And Targets $3 Billion In Additional Funding
article_excerpt:
VersaBank, a London, Ontario-based digital bank, has expanded its Structured Receivable Program (SRP) in the United States to finance point-of-sale loans and leases for small businesses. The expansion introduces the bank’s established small business funding capabilities to the U.S. market, where its SRP activities had previously focused exclusively on consumer lending.

The initiative includes VersaBank’s Real-Time Structured Receivable Program, which enables financing companies to obtain funding for individual loans within hours rather than accumulating receivables over several days or weeks.

VersaBank estimates that adding small business lending and leasing will more than double the addressable market for its U.S. Structured Receivable Program. The expansion is intended to support the bank’s target of generating at least US$3 billion in additional U.S. SRP fundings in 2027. This figure represents management’s target rather than funding already committed or completed.

The launch represents another step in VersaBank’s efforts to expand its U.S. operations following the introduction of its Structured Receivable Program to the American market in August 2024.

VersaBank has offered its SRP to the Canadian small business sector since 2010, providing financing to companies that originate loans and leases for commercial customers.

The U.S. expansion will allow the bank to establish relationships with financing companies specializing in small business transactions while enabling its existing U.S. partners to obtain funding for additional loan categories.

According to VersaBank, the company has already developed a substantial pipeline of prospective U.S. SRP partners in anticipation of the launch.

Its Structured Receivable Program provides capital to financing companies that originate loans for consumers and small businesses, particularly for relatively large purchases.

These transactions can include consumer home improvement projects, heating and air conditioning equipment, and a broad range of commercial equipment purchased or leased by small businesses.

Rather than originating every underlying loan directly, VersaBank works with financing partners that maintain customer relationships and originate eligible receivables.

The program is designed to provide those partners with consistent access to funding, enabling them to originate additional loans while managing their capital requirements.

For small business financing companies, reliable access to capital can be particularly important when supporting customers making substantial equipment purchases or investments in their operations.

VersaBank’s expansion will allow qualifying U.S. partners to use its funding platform for these transactions, extending the types of receivables eligible for financing.

A central component of the strategy is the bank’s Real-Time SRP, which was developed to accelerate the funding process for point-of-sale lenders.

Under conventional receivables financing arrangements, lenders may need to accumulate multiple loans before transferring them into a warehouse financing facility or arranging longer-term funding.

According to VersaBank, this process typically requires five to 30 days or longer, potentially increasing financing costs and the amount of capital lenders need to maintain.

The Real-Time SRP is designed to eliminate much of that waiting period by allowing participating lenders to obtain funding for individual loans within hours.

By reducing the need to warehouse receivables before obtaining funding, the platform can help financing companies lower their financing expenses and reduce their reliance on separate warehouse credit facilities.

company_description: Cari has raised $32.5 million in the first tranche of its initial external funding round , with all of the capital coming from banks.
article_title: Cari Raises $32.5 Million From Banks To Scale Tokenized Deposit Network
article_excerpt:
Cari has raised $32.5 million in the first tranche of its initial external funding round , with all of the capital coming from banks.

Investors include all six of Cari’s Design Partner Banks: First Horizon Bank, Huntington Bank, KeyBank, M&T Bank, Old National Bank and SouthState Bank , along with other institutions including Glacier Bank.

Cari is developing a bank-governed digital money network that allows regulated financial institutions to bring deposits on-chain and provide programmable, always-on financial services.

The company’s relationship with its Design Partner Banks began in September 2025, with the institutions helping co-develop the network’s technology, operations, governance and use cases.

Cari launched its first minimum viable product on March 31 and delivered a full product suite on July 31.

The platform now includes programmable capabilities, a front-end wallet and an operational portal allowing participating banks to complete the mint, transfer and burn cycle for tokenized deposits .

More than 30 banks have joined the network , while another 40-plus institutions are in active discussions to participate. Together, the current network and pipeline represent institutions with more than $10 trillion in combined assets .

Cari plans to use the funding to move the network toward production, accelerate bank onboarding and integrations, develop additional programmable money products and use cases and expand capabilities supporting banks’ digital asset strategies.

Gene Ludwig, Founder and CEO of Cari

Bryan Jordan, Chairman, President and CEO of First Horizon Bank

General Atlantic and QED Investors co-led the round. Evolution Equity Partners, Airtree, Forestay Capital, Y Combinator, FT Partners, Latitude, Inception Fund, and 13Books Capital also participated.

AI Agents For Financial And Professional Services

Founded by brothers and repeat entrepreneurs Chaz and Arnie Englander, Model ML provides personal AI agents for bankers, consultants, and investors.

The platform is designed to understand each user’s clients, active transactions, preferred processes, and work formats. Its agents operate continuously within a firm’s existing systems and become more personalized through repeated interactions.

Rather than waiting for a user to submit each request, the platform can monitor developments, determine which information is relevant, evaluate its implications, and prepare completed work.

For example, when news emerges about a company covered by an investment banker, Model ML’s agent can assess whether the development is significant and prepare an analysis using the firm’s preferred format. The company said this process can reduce work that previously took days to minutes.

Model ML reported that annual recurring revenue increased twelvefold year over year during the third quarter of 2026. Daily active users increased by 26 times over the same period.

Flexible And Secure Enterprise Deployment

The company said customer data is never used to train AI models. Model ML is certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit.

The platform is not tied to a single AI provider. Model ML evaluates models on real financial assignments and routes each task to the option it determines offers the best combination of accuracy, speed, and cost.

A growing portion of customer work runs on the company’s internally fine-tuned open-source models. Model ML said these models complete applicable workloads at approximately 2% of the cost of frontier models and are generally five times faster, while matching or exceeding frontier-model accuracy for those tasks.

Model ML is headquartered in London and maintains offices across North America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Its advisory board includes former HSBC Group Chief Executive Sir Noel Quinn and former UBS Chairman Axel Weber.

article_title: Variational Raises $110 Million Series B At $1.5 Billion Valuation To Expand On-Chain Derivatives Trading Infrastructure
article_excerpt:
Variational has raised $110 million in Series B financing at a $1.5 billion valuation to expand its on-chain derivatives trading infrastructure and increase access to traditional financial markets.

Bain Capital Crypto led the round, with participation from Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV, 50T Funds, and other investors.

Since launching in early 2025, Variational has processed more than $475 billion in trading volume and accumulated over $1.3 billion in open interest across more than 100,000 accounts. The company said traditional markets now account for more than half of the platform’s daily volume.

The new capital will support additional market listings and allow Variational to raise open-interest caps that traders are increasingly reaching.

Connecting Traditional And On-Chain Liquidity

Variational powers Omni, a leveraged trading platform covering more than 550 cryptocurrency and traditional markets. Unlike platforms that depend entirely on on-chain liquidity, Omni aggregates liquidity from both digital-asset venues and traditional financial institutions.

That structure supported the September 2026 launch of swaps, an instrument designed to give on-chain traders access to traditional financial liquidity. Variational said swaps are intended to provide tighter spreads, deeper liquidity, and more predictable holding costs than existing on-chain derivatives.

More than $80 billion in swap volume has been processed since the product launched.

Omni uses an internal liquidity provider known as OLP to quote prices across every listed market. OLP connects with cryptocurrency exchanges and traditional financial institutions, aggregating liquidity from existing markets.

The model enables Omni to offer trading without transaction fees, while OLP earns the spread between quoted prices.

Expansion Plans

Variational plans to broaden OLP’s counterparty network, introduce additional swap markets, and move toward continuous trading across stocks, commodities, foreign exchange pairs, and other traditional assets.

Its remaining 2026 roadmap includes launching a trading API, adding more swap markets, and progressing toward round-the-clock swap trading.

Variational was built by professionals with experience at Google, Meta, Virtu, IMC, and Jane Street. The company cautions that leveraged derivatives carry a high risk of loss and that its platform is unavailable to restricted persons, including U.S. persons.

KEY QUOTES:

Earlier this year, we said that the only way to bring quality execution for traditional markets on-chain is to aggregate liquidity from where it already exists. Swaps are proving that thesis. Lucas Schuermann, CEO of Variational

Variational is one of the first teams to bring derivatives liquidity from traditional finance directly on-chain. It has all of the benefits you’d expect from a traditional trading platform – hundreds of markets, no trading fees, deep liquidity – with the transparency and rapid settlement of crypto rails. This round gives Variational the capacity to keep growing, with higher open interest caps and more markets.

Stefan Cohen, Partner at Bain Capital Crypto

company_description: Global Kiwi Labs has raised $4 million in seed funding to expand TheHUB, a colocation infrastructure platform designed to provide digital asset market participants with equal access to exchanges and trading systems.
article_title: Global Kiwi Labs Raises $4 Million To Build Fair-Access Digital Asset Infrastructure
article_excerpt:
Global Kiwi Labs has raised $4 million in seed funding to expand TheHUB, a colocation infrastructure platform designed to provide digital asset market participants with equal access to exchanges and trading systems. Valor Capital Group led the round, with participation from Adderall Capital, Keyrock, Staking Facilities, and a group of angel investors.

Global Kiwi Labs used the funding to establish TheHUB’s first location inside the Equinix TY15 data center in Tokyo. The site is now live and onboarding exchanges, trading firms, and blockchain validators.

The company will also use the capital to expand its engineering team and bring the platform into additional geographic markets.

Creating Equalized Connections For Digital Asset Markets

TheHUB applies the fair-access colocation architecture used by major traditional exchanges to digital asset markets.

In conventional financial markets, colocation systems are structured to prevent one participant from purchasing a shorter or faster physical connection to an exchange’s order book. Digital asset trading venues have not consistently adopted comparable infrastructure, potentially allowing larger companies to pay for greater proximity and lower latency.

Latency can affect the order in which market participants receive information and submit trades. A company receiving price information first may have an opportunity to trade before another participant can update an existing quote.

This difference can also affect market participants beyond high-frequency trading firms. Market makers exposed to uncertain execution speeds may widen their bid-and-ask spreads to compensate for the risk that prices will change before their orders reach the market.

TheHUB is intended to reduce that uncertainty by giving every participant an equalized connection to its central network switch. Each connection uses exactly 1,000 meters of fiber and is measured to within 10 millimeters, according to the company.

The structure is designed to prevent one participant from gaining a proximity advantage by placing its systems physically closer to a market’s matching engine.

Combining Colocation, Timing, And Market Data

TheHUB incorporates four principal components of traditional exchange infrastructure.

First, the platform equalizes the length of each participant’s physical connection to the central switch. Second, a GPS-synchronized master clock timestamps orders as they enter the network, creating a basis for sequencing them according to their arrival times.

Third, TheHUB distributes market data simultaneously to subscribers using open standards already employed by traditional exchanges. This is intended to reduce differences in when individual firms receive pricing and trading information.

Finally, the platform records order sequencing and execution data on-chain. This creates a public audit trail that can be used to verify activity within the network.

As more exchanges and infrastructure providers connect to TheHUB, market participants may be able to reach a larger trading ecosystem through shared infrastructure instead of establishing separate connections and equipment for every venue.

Leadership With Exchange Infrastructure Experience

Global Kiwi Labs CEO Jamie Brown has approximately 30 years of experience in capital markets infrastructure.

Brown spent nearly a decade designing fair-access colocation systems for exchanges including CME, Nasdaq, the New York Stock Exchange, IEX, and the Singapore Exchange. He also worked as a consultant to global exchanges and within infrastructure teams at high-frequency trading firms.

Brown designed TheHUB’s equalization system using the same core technology applied in traditional exchange environments.

Chief Strategy Officer Thiago Rudiger previously spent nine years at Brazilian hedge fund Squadra Investimentos. He later moved into digital assets, serving as CEO of the Tanssi Foundation and vice president of growth at Moondance Labs.

article_title: Nakamoto: $165 Million Kraken Loan Maturities Extended Into 2027 With No Scheduled Principal Due In 2026
article_excerpt:
Nakamoto, a Bitcoin-focused company operating businesses across media, financial services, and advisory markets, has amended its loan agreement with Payward Interactive, the operator of Kraken, extending the maturity of 60 million USDT in outstanding debt from December 4, 2026, to December 4, 2027. The amendment eliminates the company’s scheduled principal maturities under the loan for the remainder of 2026.

The agreement applies to Nakamoto Holdings, a wholly owned subsidiary of Nakamoto, and modifies the repayment schedule for its existing 165 million USDT loan.

Following the amendment, 105 million USDT of principal is scheduled to mature on June 30, 2027, while the remaining 60 million USDT is scheduled to mature on December 4, 2027.

USDT is a U.S. dollar-referenced stablecoin, meaning the loan’s stated principal corresponds to approximately $165 million at its intended dollar peg.

The amended schedule provides Nakamoto with additional time to manage its liquidity and operating priorities without a scheduled principal payment on this loan during 2026.

The arrangement also modifies the collateral supporting the financing.

Under the updated agreement, the net value of certain Bitcoin derivatives positions held in Nakamoto’s pledged Kraken trading account can be included in the collateral calculation.

The eligible derivatives value cannot contribute less than zero and remains subject to limitations under the amended agreement.

The inclusion of these positions is intended to provide additional flexibility in managing collateral requirements.

However, their contribution depends on the value and eligibility of the positions, and the modification does not eliminate the risks associated with Bitcoin price volatility.

Nakamoto’s financing arrangements remain exposed to fluctuations in the market value of its Bitcoin holdings and other collateral.

Substantial declines in Bitcoin prices could affect the company’s ability to maintain required collateral levels and could create additional repayment or collateral obligations.

The extension also moves repayment requirements into 2027 rather than eliminating the underlying debt.

Nakamoto said the revised agreement will allow management to focus more closely on its operating businesses and Bitcoin holdings.

The company owns and operates a portfolio of Bitcoin-native businesses spanning media, information services, asset management, and advisory activities.

Its subsidiaries include BTC Inc, which operates Bitcoin Magazine, The Bitcoin Conference, and Bitcoin for Corporations.

Nakamoto also owns UTXO Management, an investment manager focused on public and private market opportunities across the Bitcoin ecosystem.

These businesses provide Nakamoto with operating activities tied to Bitcoin adoption, industry information, and financial services.

The financing amendment comes as the company manages its capital structure alongside the volatility associated with digital assets.

By extending the December 2026 maturity to December 2027 and expanding the categories of eligible collateral, Nakamoto is seeking greater flexibility to navigate market conditions.

The company will still need to repay or refinance the outstanding amounts in 2027 and comply with its ongoing loan obligations.

KEY QUOTE:

“This amendment extends our runway and makes our collateral position more resilient. It gives us more flexibility to manage through Bitcoin price volatility so we can put our full attention on what we control: building our operating businesses and managing our Bitcoin holdings so that we can continue to grow through this market cycle. We are grateful to Kraken for being a supportive financing partner.”

Tyler Evans, Chief Investment Officer Of Nakamoto

company_description: Daisytuner has raised €6 million in seed financing and launched Daisyflow, an AI inference engine designed to improve the performance of artificial intelligence models across different computing chips.
article_title: Daisytuner Raises €6 Million And Launches Daisyflow AI Inference Engine
article_excerpt:
Daisytuner has raised €6 million in seed financing and launched Daisyflow, an AI inference engine designed to improve the performance of artificial intelligence models across different computing chips. The financing round was co-led by Elaia and LEA Ventures, with participation from APEX Ventures and Seedcamp.

The company is developing a self-learning compiler platform that uses AI agents to identify and test performance optimizations directly on hardware. The technology is intended to help organizations run AI models more efficiently while reducing the engineering work traditionally required to optimize software for different processors.

The launch comes as demand for AI inference continues to increase, with businesses deploying increasingly sophisticated models across a growing range of applications.

Inference refers to the process of running a trained AI model to generate predictions, responses, or other outputs. As organizations scale their use of AI, inference performance becomes an important factor in determining computing costs, application responsiveness, and infrastructure efficiency.

Unlike model training, which involves developing or refining an AI system, inference occurs whenever the deployed model processes new requests. Improvements in inference efficiency can therefore have a significant cumulative impact for businesses operating AI applications at scale.

One of the challenges facing AI infrastructure providers is the diversity of computing hardware available for running models.

Different processors have different architectures, memory systems, and computational capabilities. Software that performs efficiently on one type of chip may require additional optimization to achieve comparable results on another.

This creates an ongoing challenge for developers, who must adapt applications as new AI models and hardware platforms enter the market.

Daisytuner is seeking to address this complexity through Daisyflow, which automates portions of the optimization process.

Daisyflow uses AI agents to explore potential optimizations and evaluate their performance directly on the computing hardware where an AI model will run.

Rather than relying exclusively on manually developed optimization techniques, the platform tests different approaches to identify configurations that can improve execution speed.

Its compiler checks whether each proposed optimization produces correct results before accepting it.

This verification process is an important component of the technology because performance improvements must not come at the expense of computational correctness.

Once a successful optimization has been identified and verified, Daisyflow stores the result for future use.

Over time, this process is intended to build a collection of validated optimizations that can support additional workloads and reduce repeated engineering efforts.

The approach combines automated experimentation, performance measurement, and compiler-based verification.

Daisytuner’s objective is to make AI inference optimization more adaptive as computing hardware and model architectures evolve.

Traditional optimization processes can require specialized engineering expertise and substantial testing whenever organizations introduce new models, processors, or infrastructure configurations.

By automating more of that work, Daisyflow is designed to reduce the amount of manual intervention needed to improve AI performance.

The platform’s self-learning capabilities could also help organizations adapt more quickly to changes in the AI hardware ecosystem.

Daisytuner reported that the Qwen 2.5 AI model can run up to 18% faster using Daisyflow than with vLLM, an established open-source inference serving engine, on AMD Instinct graphics processors.

The benchmark provides an early example of the performance improvements the company is targeting.

Fractile, an AI hardware company developing high-performance processors for artificial intelligence workloads, has raised $720 million in Series C funding led by Thrive Capital, Lightspeed, Redpoint, and Founders Fund. The financing will support continued development of the company’s semiconductor technology and preparations to ship its first chips and systems in 2027.

Fractile Founder and CEO Walter Goodwin announced the investment in a LinkedIn post, highlighting the company’s ambition to develop AI computing hardware capable of delivering substantially faster model execution.

The financing also attracted participation from numerous new and existing investors, including Factorial Funds, CapitalG, Felicis, DST Global, BlackRock, Accel, Georgian, Bain Capital Ventures, SV Angel, Sovereign AI, Balderton, Shopify Ventures, T. Rowe Price, British Business Bank, Kindred Capital, Gigascale Capital, and Conviction.

The investment comes as AI infrastructure developers increasingly focus on improving the performance and efficiency of hardware used to run large artificial intelligence models.

Fractile is developing technology designed to address performance constraints associated with memory systems and other components of AI computing infrastructure.

Developing High-Performance AI Processors

Fractile is building a computing platform intended to accelerate the execution of artificial intelligence models.

The company’s engineering work spans semiconductor development, software, and complete computing systems.

This approach allows its team to address different components of AI hardware performance rather than focusing exclusively on individual processor capabilities.

One of the company’s key technical areas involves improving the speed at which data can be accessed and processed.

Memory performance has become an important consideration in AI hardware development because sophisticated models require substantial amounts of information to be transferred between memory and computing resources.

These data movements can limit overall system performance, even when processors have significant computational capacity.

Fractile is developing technology intended to address these constraints and improve the speed at which AI workloads can execute.

Fractile Reports 20-Fold DRAM Performance Breakthrough

Goodwin highlighted Fractile’s work on extracting substantially higher performance from dynamic random-access memory, commonly known as DRAM.

According to the company, its technology has achieved speeds 20 times higher in this area.

DRAM is a widely used semiconductor memory technology that stores information required by computing systems.

In AI applications, the movement of model data can be a significant factor influencing inference performance.

Inference refers to the process of running a trained AI model to produce predictions, responses, or other outputs.

Fractile believes improving memory-related performance can help address some of the limitations encountered by conventional AI hardware.

Goodwin described the company’s DRAM work as an important technical achievement in its efforts to make AI models run faster.

The announcement did not provide detailed benchmark methodology or comparative hardware specifications for the reported 20-fold improvement.

The company’s broader objective is to translate its technical advances into commercially available chips and computing systems.

First AI Chips And Systems Planned For 2027

Fractile plans to ship its first chips and systems in 2027.

The Series C financing will support the engineering and commercialization work required to reach that milestone.

Semiconductor development involves multiple stages, including chip architecture, design, manufacturing preparation, testing, and system integration.

Bringing new AI hardware to market can also require extensive software development to support model execution and application compatibility.

company_description: Kalshi has raised $1 billion in Series G funding at a $40 billion post-money valuation as the prediction market company expands into a broader range of financial products and international markets.
article_title: Kalshi Raises $1 Billion Series G At $40 Billion Valuation For Prediction Market Platform
article_excerpt:
Kalshi has raised $1 billion in Series G funding at a $40 billion post-money valuation as the prediction market company expands into a broader range of financial products and international markets. The round was co-led by Wellington and Sequoia. Additional investors included Baillie Gifford, Stripes, Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, Layer Global, Morgan Stanley Investment Management, Sequoia Global Equities, CapitalG, Hudson River Trading, and Balyasny Asset Management.

Kalshi plans to use the financing to expand its exchange, introduce new asset classes, increase institutional adoption, and grow internationally.

The company said its annualized trading volume now exceeds $1 trillion, while non-sports annualized revenue has surpassed $1 billion. More than 30 million Kalshi accounts have been created, and the company said it represents more than 75% of prediction market trading volume.

Kalshi began with prediction markets but has been expanding into politics, cryptocurrency, economics, commodities, and perpetual futures.

Its commodities business reached more than $100 million in annualized trading fees within three months. Crypto trading volume has reached about $140 billion annualized, while political markets have surpassed $8 billion annualized.

Kalshi’s international retail operation is approaching $100 million in annualized trading fees about one year after launching in more than 140 countries.

The company’s perpetual futures business has also reached $83 billion in trading volume and attracted more than 500,000 traders since launching several months ago.

Institutional participation is increasing as well. About 500 entities were active on Kalshi in September, and institutional entities, excluding market makers, accounted for about 25% of total exchange trading volume.

Kalshi’s partner ecosystem includes Interactive Brokers, Marex, Clear Street, Cantor Fitzgerald, S&P, Nasdaq, Stripe, Public.com, Plus500, Wealthsimple, Alpaca, PayPal, and Block.

The company intends to accelerate development of additional products, including indices, single-stock perpetual futures, and compute markets. Kalshi recently announced a partnership with S&P to develop prediction-market-based indices.

The new capital will also support institutional sales, distribution, infrastructure, and product development aimed at hedge funds, proprietary trading firms, financial institutions, and other sophisticated market participants.

Kalshi additionally plans to expand internationally, with Latin America and Europe identified as priority markets.

The company said its broader objective is to evolve from a prediction market platform into a diversified financial exchange that allows individuals, businesses, and institutions to trade directly on events and risks that traditional financial products may not address.

article_title: PERPTools Raises $5 Million Seed Round At $80 Million Valuation For Decentralized Perpetual Futures Trading Platform
article_excerpt:
PERPTools has raised a $5 million seed round at an $80 million fully diluted valuation, bringing the AI-native perpetuals trading platform’s total funding to $8 million across two token rounds. The seed round brought in BigBrain Holdings, NEAR, Animoca Brands, Sfermion and Shima Capital as key stakeholders. It followed a $3 million pre-seed round completed at a $30 million fully diluted valuation and led by DEXTools Ventures and Orderly Network. Fundraising began in November 2025, with the pre-seed closing the following month and the seed round following in early 2026.

PERPTools was built by the team behind DEXTools and combines AI-native trading agents with decentralized perpetual futures infrastructure. The company said its fundraising strategy was designed to add investors that can contribute distribution, liquidity and ecosystem alignment in addition to capital.

The pre-seed brought together Orderly Network’s omnichain liquidity infrastructure with DEXTools’ established trading platform and user base. PERPTools is embedding trading directly into the DEXTools ecosystem, giving users the ability to move from token and market discovery into execution without leaving the platform.

PERPTools said the platform already has access to a potential audience of 30 million DEXTools traders and has generated $240 million in trading volume during its beta period.

The company is led by CEO Evgen Tokarev, who previously built trading infrastructure at DEXTools and has nine years of experience developing trading systems. CTO Denys Hrechko, formerly of Everstake, oversees the PERPTools platform, while CMO Wael Rajab also serves as CEO of DEXTools Ventures and leads distribution efforts.

PERPTools is built on Orderly Network’s omnichain liquidity engine, an orderbook-based trading infrastructure that provides shared liquidity across supported chains without requiring users to bridge assets. Orderly Network is also a stakeholder and strategic partner in PERPTools.

The company is targeting the decentralized perpetual futures market, which the release said generates more than $10 billion in daily trading volume across decentralized exchanges.

PERPTools has already launched three products ahead of its planned Token Generation Event.

Its Perp DEX is a non-custodial perpetual futures exchange operating on mainnet. It supports long and short positions, leverage and cross-margin trading, with transactions settled through Orderly’s omnichain central limit order book.

The company’s AI Arena is a marketplace for autonomous on-chain trading agents. Users can create an agent in approximately five minutes by selecting a risk profile, establishing leverage constraints and describing a trading strategy in natural language. Agents then trade continuously using liquidity from the same Perp DEX.

Other users can allocate USDC to agents they want to follow, while agent rankings are based on verified 30-day on-chain profit and loss data.

PERPTools has also launched Tap Prediction, a real-time prediction product based on live perpetual-market feeds. Users select cells on a price grid and can stake as little as $0.10 for potential payouts of up to 25 times their stake. The product has a prize pool exceeding $1 million and is already generating revenue ahead of the company’s TGE.

With both funding rounds completed, PERPTools plans to shift its emphasis toward product execution and growth. The company is preparing for a Q4 2026 Token Generation Event and intends to further integrate market discovery and trading execution within the broader DEXTools ecosystem.

company_description: Liquid Compute has raised $15 million in seed funding to build a marketplace and financial infrastructure platform for buying, selling, pricing and managing AI computing capacity.
article_title: Liquid Compute Raises $15 Million Seed Round To Build Regulated AI Infrastructure Marketplace
article_excerpt:
Liquid Compute has raised $15 million in seed funding to build a marketplace and financial infrastructure platform for buying, selling, pricing and managing AI computing capacity. FirstMark and Chemistry co-led the round, with participation from K8 Capital, Night Capital, TrueBridge, Brainchild Holdings, UFO Holdings and investor Dmitry Balyasny.

The New York-based company, formerly known as Pluto, is developing what it describes as a physical grid for compute alongside a planned regulated financial market that could allow companies and investors to trade contracts tied to the price of AI infrastructure.

Liquid Compute has applications pending with the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission for Designated Contract Market and Derivatives Clearing Organization status.

If approved, those registrations would allow the company to develop regulated cash-settled markets tied to prices established through its underlying compute marketplace.

The company was founded by Ronit Jain and Aarav Patel, who met while studying engineering at the University of California, Berkeley.

Liquid Compute participated in Y Combinator’s Winter 2024 program.

The founders developed the business around the idea that computing capacity increasingly resembles electricity infrastructure more than a conventional commodity such as oil.

AI compute is not completely interchangeable.

Different GPU configurations, data center locations, power environments, network connections and deployment schedules can make one unit of computing capacity substantially different from another.

Compute is also time-sensitive because unused GPU capacity during a particular period cannot necessarily be stored and sold later in the same way as a physical commodity.

Liquid Compute is therefore developing a marketplace intended to match supply and demand across hardware, geography, infrastructure and time.

The company wants to connect otherwise fragmented pools of computing capacity into a more transparent market where AI companies, enterprises and other buyers can locate infrastructure while suppliers can monetize unused capacity.

The $15 million financing will support the buildout of Liquid Compute’s matching and clearing infrastructure while helping the company expand the amount of compute available through its network.

Liquid Compute is also developing pricing and market data around its physical order book.

That data could give buyers, sellers, traders and lenders greater visibility into how computing capacity is priced and how AI infrastructure is financed.

The company sees that information becoming increasingly important as AI infrastructure spending expands and computing capacity becomes a larger component of corporate capital expenditure.

AI model developers and enterprises can face significant uncertainty around future compute requirements and pricing.

GPU infrastructure providers, meanwhile, need to determine how much capacity to build, where to deploy it and how to monetize periods when infrastructure is not fully utilized.

Liquid Compute believes a more standardized marketplace could help both sides manage those challenges.

Above the physical marketplace, the company plans to establish a financial layer through which participants could eventually manage exposure to changes in compute prices.

Liquid Compute compares the opportunity with the development of established financial markets around other strategically important resources.

Its long-term ambition is to become financial infrastructure for computing capacity in a similar way that established exchanges helped create transparent pricing, hedging and risk management markets around energy and other commodities.

The company’s pending CFTC applications are central to that strategy.

article_title: Implicity Raises $40 Million To Expand AI Cardiac Remote Monitoring Platform
article_excerpt:
Implicity has raised $40 million in growth equity funding to accelerate U.S. expansion and further develop its AI-powered cardiac remote monitoring platform. The round was led by European technology growth investor IRIS alongside Five Arrows, the alternative assets arm of Rothschild & Co.

Implicity already works with more than 250 medical centers and monitors more than 120,000 patients daily across the United States, France and Germany.

The company provides a universal remote cardiac monitoring platform that brings together information generated by multiple cardiac devices and monitoring systems.

Rather than requiring clinicians to move among separate systems associated with different medical device manufacturers, Implicity aggregates, normalizes and analyzes cardiac data within a single platform.

The system also integrates with electronic health records, helping care teams incorporate remotely generated cardiac information into existing clinical workflows.

Implicity uses artificial intelligence to prioritize clinically important information and reduce the amount of time healthcare professionals spend manually reviewing alerts and navigating fragmented data.

Remote monitoring has become increasingly important in cardiology as patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices and heart failure generate larger amounts of health information outside hospitals.

While that data can give physicians earlier insight into potential problems, it can also increase the operational burden on clinical teams.

Implicity is designed to identify meaningful signals within those growing datasets so clinicians can spend more time on patients requiring intervention.

The company has built its technology around proprietary algorithms that have received FDA clearance.

According to Implicity, patients monitored using its platform have experienced a 26% reduction in mortality and a 4% reduction in hospitalizations compared with conventional remote monitoring.

Its SignalHF heart failure prediction algorithm is designed to provide earlier visibility into a patient’s risk of heart failure deterioration.

The company’s ECG Analyzer can also reduce false alarms by as much as 76%, potentially decreasing the amount of time clinicians spend reviewing non-actionable alerts.

The new funding will be used to expand Implicity’s U.S. business from its Cambridge, Massachusetts base.

The company plans to add commercial employees, expand its relationships with U.S. healthcare providers and develop features specifically for the American market.

Implicity will also increase investment in its AI roadmap, including the next generation of heart failure prediction algorithms.

The company has already established a substantial position in Europe and plans to build on that presence while scaling in the United States.

The funding gives Implicity additional resources to move from remote monitoring toward increasingly predictive cardiac care.

Rather than simply alerting clinicians after a cardiac event or abnormal signal occurs, predictive algorithms could potentially identify changes earlier and allow healthcare providers to intervene before a patient’s condition becomes more serious.

For hospitals, the platform is also intended to address workforce pressures by reducing the administrative burden associated with reviewing cardiac monitoring data.

Implicity’s universal architecture allows it to work across device manufacturers, potentially giving hospitals a single operating layer for managing patients whose cardiac devices come from different vendors.

IRIS and Five Arrows are backing the company as it moves into its next phase of international growth.

Five Arrows manages more than €34 billion in assets and operates as Rothschild & Co’s alternative assets business.

article_title: iPremom Raises €15 Million Seed Round Led By Amadeus Capital Partners
article_excerpt:
iPremom has raised €15 million in seed funding led by Amadeus Capital Partners , with participation from Asabys Partners and APEX Ventures, to advance its molecular diagnostics platform for the early prediction of pregnancy complications.

The Valencia, Spain-based company plans to use the financing to support clinical validation and commercialization of MaiRa , a blood-based platform designed to identify molecular signals associated with pregnancy complications during the first trimester.

MaiRa analyzes cell-free RNA and applies predictive modeling to assess risks including preeclampsia months before symptoms may become apparent.

The platform is based on more than a decade of research by iPremom co-founders Professor Carlos Simón, M.D., Ph.D., Chairman, and Dr. Tamara Garrido, Chief Scientific Officer .

For preeclampsia, the company’s research has identified detectable molecular signals in maternal blood as early as nine to 14 weeks into pregnancy .

MaiRa has been developed using data from more than 26,000 samples linked to 10,000 pregnancies included in the PREMOM study, one of Spain’s largest prospective clinical trials.

The company expects to add molecular signals associated with additional pregnancy complications to the platform over time.

Led by CEO Guillermo Ferrando Huertas , iPremom currently makes MaiRa available in Spain through its laboratory.

The new funding will support commercial rollout, completion of additional validation studies, and regulatory approval efforts in the European Union and United States .

KEY QUOTES:

“Pregnancy complications have been under-diagnosed and under-treated for generations, because the field was looking in the wrong place at the wrong time. Our ambition is not just to build a better preeclampsia test, it is to give every pregnant woman a comprehensive, early molecular picture of her pregnancy. This funding is a critical step toward making that a clinical reality.”

Professor Carlos Simón, Co-Founder and Chairman of iPremom

“We are delighted to partner again with Prof. Simón, after the success of Igenomix which transformed IVF genetics. iPremom is poised to do the same for prenatal care, an even larger market opportunity. By predicting risk from the first weeks of pregnancy based on a simple blood test, it will inform and prepare millions of expecting couples, arm clinicians with unparalleled insights for targeted intervention, and give every baby the best possible start in life. We are proud to be leading this round.”

Pierre Socha, Partner at Amadeus Capital Partners

company_description: Polymarket is raising $1 billion in a new funding round led by 1789 Capital that values the prediction-market platform at $21 billion on a post-money basis, according to a Bloomberg report .
article_title: Polymarket Reportedly Raises $1 Billion At $21 Billion Valuation In 1789 Capital-Led Round
article_excerpt:
Polymarket is raising $1 billion in a new funding round led by 1789 Capital that values the prediction-market platform at $21 billion on a post-money basis, according to a Bloomberg report .

The financing represents another substantial increase in Polymarket’s valuation as investor interest in prediction markets continues to accelerate.

Polymarket completed a previous funding round in April at a $15 billion valuation, bringing D.E. Shaw and venture capital firm G Squared into its investor base. The new $21 billion post-money valuation therefore represents a 40% increase from that valuation in only a few months.

1789 Capital has an existing relationship with Polymarket. The investment firm made a strategic investment in the company in 2025, when Donald Trump Jr., a partner at 1789 Capital, also joined Polymarket’s advisory board. Terms of that earlier investment were not publicly disclosed at the time.

The latest financing substantially deepens that relationship. Separate reporting indicates that 1789 Capital is investing approximately $300 million as part of the $1 billion round, following roughly $200 million of previous investment in Polymarket.

Polymarket operates markets that allow participants to trade based on the outcomes of future events spanning politics, sports, economics, culture and other topics.

Prediction markets have attracted growing amounts of institutional capital as their trading volumes, mainstream visibility and potential applications as real-time indicators of market expectations have increased.

The latest financing also highlights the increasingly competitive environment between Polymarket and Kalshi.

Kalshi raised capital at a $22 billion valuation in May, placing the two major prediction-market platforms at comparable private-market valuations. Bloomberg noted that Polymarket has faced operational and legal challenges this year while Kalshi has continued expanding.

Donald Trump Jr. serves as an adviser to both companies, while also working as a partner at 1789 Capital.

Polymarket has simultaneously been increasing its focus on market surveillance and integrity. The company recently appointed former FBI investigator Shana Bautista as its global head of investigations and intelligence and has been using machine learning, blockchain analytics and other tools to identify potentially suspicious activity on its platform.

The company has also been rebuilding its position in the U.S. market following the acquisition of a federally regulated exchange, giving it a pathway to operate domestically after previously restricting U.S. users.

At $21 billion, the latest valuation places Polymarket among the world’s most highly valued private fintech and crypto-related companies and underscores how quickly prediction markets have moved from a relatively niche trading category into a heavily funded financial technology sector.

The $1 billion capital raise also gives Polymarket additional resources as it competes with Kalshi, develops its U.S. business and expands the technology, liquidity and infrastructure supporting its global prediction-market platform.

article_title: Breedr Raises $27 Million Series B As Platform Tracks 2+ Million Cattle And Nearly $500 Million In Livestock Transactions
article_excerpt:
Breedr has raised $27 million in Series B funding to expand its digital livestock platform as the company works to build a global system of record for the beef supply chain. Partech led the financing through its impact fund, with participation from Latitude, the growth-stage fund of seed investor LocalGlobe, and existing investor Outsiders Fund, which led Breedr’s Series A. The round brings Breedr’s total funding to $46.6 million.

Breedr plans to use the capital to expand its team, bring additional ranchers and farmers onto the platform and capture more information about individual animals, including genomic data.

Partech General Partner Arnaud Minvielle and Latitude’s Remus Brett will join Breedr’s board.

More than two million cattle are already tracked through Breedr, and nearly $500 million of livestock has been transacted through the platform during 2026.

Customers range from family-owned ranches to larger operators handling more than 100,000 cattle annually.

Breedr creates a digital record for each animal that can follow it through the beef supply chain, including the multiple farms and ranches a cow may pass through before reaching market.

Records can incorporate information such as weight, health and family history.

The company is targeting a cattle industry that still relies heavily on paper records despite increasingly tight supply conditions.

The U.S. cattle herd entered 2026 at its lowest level since 1951, while this year’s calf crop is projected to be the smallest on record.

Breedr believes more detailed data can help producers generate more value from each animal as beef demand continues rising.

The company’s marketplace also enables producers to sell cattle using digital records rather than relying solely on traditional auctions where buyers assess animals visually.

Breedr’s AI-powered growth prediction model is designed to help producers identify the optimal time to sell.

A separate cattle fund managed by Breedr can also advance capital against livestock, providing producers with liquidity while they continue raising their animals.

Breedr said its data-driven approach can help cattle reach market weight as much as five months sooner than traditional approaches and generate more than $500 in additional value per animal.

The company estimates that shorter production cycles can also reduce methane emissions by approximately 20% to 30% per animal.

Breedr was founded in the U.K. in 2018 by Ian Wheal, who grew up on a cattle farm in Australia.

The company has been headquartered in Texas since 2022 and operates across the U.S., U.K. and Australia, with a growing presence in New Zealand and Europe.

Breedr ultimately aims to become the system of record across major livestock-producing regions worldwide, connecting animal data, commerce and financing across the beef supply chain.

KEY QUOTES:

“We built Breedr to bring value back to the people who raise the cattle. Demand for beef is climbing while the herd is the smallest it has been in 75 years. The industry has to get more value from every animal, and you cannot do that on paper.”

“If you have bought beef from a major retailer in the United States or UK, there is a good chance it has moved through a Breedr-powered supply chain. We already do the same in Australia and New Zealand, and this round enables us to expand connected supply chains globally, where every animal tells its own story and every producer gets paid for the quality they raise.”

Ian Wheal, Founder And CEO Of Breedr
