Walker & Dunlop arranged a $122.1 million refinancing for 530 Fifth Avenue, a fully leased retail condominium in Midtown Manhattan. Rialto Capital Management provided the floating-rate, interest-only loan.

Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team served as exclusive adviser to Aurora Capital Associates and AVRS Partners. Aaron Appel, Dustin Stolly, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre arranged the financing.

Five Tenants Occupy The Three-Level Property

The 58,989-square-foot condominium spans the west side of Fifth Avenue between 44th and 45th streets, with approximately 200 feet of storefront frontage. Its five tenants are Chase Bank, Walgreens, Five Below, Vans and UGG.

The property sits between Upper Fifth Avenue’s luxury retail corridor and shopping destinations farther south. Nearby offices, hotels and transit connections bring foot traffic to the area, as do Grand Central Terminal, Bryant Park, Times Square and Rockefeller Center.

Walker & Dunlop said its Capital Markets team sourced more than $13.9 billion from non-agency capital providers in the first half of 2026, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties.

“530 Fifth Avenue’s combination of prime frontage, established tenancy, and location within one of the world’s most recognized shopping destinations make it a highly attractive asset. We appreciate the opportunity to work with Aurora Capital, AVRS Partners, and Rialto Capital Management on this transaction.”

company_description: BrightAI has raised $97 million to expand its Physical AI platform across energy, water, waste, and heavy industrial operations.
article_title: BrightAI Raises $97 Million To Scale Physical AI For Essential Infrastructure
article_excerpt:
BrightAI has raised $97 million to expand its Physical AI platform across energy, water, waste, and heavy industrial operations. Smith Point Capital led the investment. Cobalt Capital, Marlinspike Partners, Zero Infinity Partners, GE Vernova, Khosla Ventures, Inspired Capital, and Upfront Ventures also participated.

The financing brings BrightAI’s total capital raised to $184 million.

Improving Infrastructure Visibility

BrightAI is addressing what it calls the Observability Problem—the limited ability of operators to continuously monitor the physical condition of critical infrastructure.

The company cites research estimating that infrastructure failures cost approximately $2.5 trillion annually. BrightAI’s analysis of 12,158 operators across 16 essential-service industries found that 98% lacked what it considers adequate visibility into their assets.

Its Stateful platform monitors infrastructure, identifies potential causes of problems, provides field crews with corrective guidance, and learns from completed work.

The platform incorporates edge sensors installed on infrastructure such as pipelines, poles, compressors, and tanks; autonomous robots and drones for remote or hazardous inspections; and wearable copilots that provide guidance to technicians.

BrightAI said Stateful operates across more than 50,000 locations, integrates millions of sensors and connected systems, and processes tens of trillions of sensor readings.

Supporting International Expansion

GE Vernova’s participation is expected to support the use of BrightAI technology across its Power, Wind, and Electrification businesses.

Other customers and development partners include Reworld, Osmose Utilities Services, Azuria Water Solutions, and Kodiak Gas Services.

BrightAI estimates that nearly 60% of its addressable market is outside North America, particularly in Europe and Asia. It plans to establish offices and field operations in additional international markets.

The company has also opened a 25,000-square-foot Palo Alto headquarters, an operations center in Midland, Texas, and a briefing center in Washington, D.C.

KEY QUOTES:

Our infrastructure is under more strain than it has ever been, and Physical AI has finally become reliable enough to work in the field. Bringing those two facts together is a once-in-a-generation opportunity. The hardest problems of this century – rising energy demand, water scarcity, an aging grid, a workforce retiring faster than it can be replaced – will not be solved in a data center. They will be solved by the operators who run these systems, and by what we put in their hands. We built Stateful end to end so that what it learns about their operations belongs to them. Giving these operators everything they need to meet what the world is asking of them – that is the point.

Alex Hawkinson, Founder and CEO of BrightAI

For decades, enterprises have used software to transform how they run every part of their business – but the critical infrastructure that powers the world was left behind, considered too complex to change. That era is over. BrightAI has proven the technology works in the hardest operating environments there are. Our team of operators are excited to help Alex and his team scale to serve the largest enterprises on earth.

Keith Block, Founder and CEO of Smith Point Capital

article_title: Iconic Raises $10 Million To Build AI Software For Capital Projects
article_excerpt:
Iconic has raised $10 million in seed funding to expand an artificial intelligence platform that reviews technical and commercial information for large capital projects. Peak Capital led the round, with participation from Bridford Group, Common Magic, Graduate Ventures, NP-Hard, and Tiny VC.

The Amsterdam-based company will use the capital to expand its commercial and project-delivery teams, enter Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and extend its software across additional stages of the capital-project lifecycle.

Iconic was founded in mid-2025 by Krijn de Nood and Richard Stronkman. The company has already signed five customers in energy, infrastructure, and AI infrastructure.

Supporting Large And Complex Projects

Iconic’s initial customers include a global energy company, a major European utility, a European airport, a European rail infrastructure owner, and an international contractor that builds semiconductor fabrication plants and data centers.

Each customer spends more than $1 billion annually on capital projects, according to Iconic.

Capital projects include major infrastructure, manufacturing facilities, energy systems, airports, rail networks, semiconductor plants, and data centers. These developments involve large numbers of technical documents, contracts, designs, schedules, and organizations.

Iconic estimates that approximately $15 trillion is invested in capital projects each year. However, the company says fewer than 3% are delivered on time, within budget, and according to the original plan.

Delays and cost overruns can result from engineering problems, but they can also occur because project information is distributed across documents and systems managed by owners, contractors, consultants, and engineering firms.

Important details may be inconsistent, missing, or difficult to identify before construction begins. Once work is underway, correcting an issue can require redesign, contract changes, new procurement, or additional construction.

Connecting Engineering And Commercial Information

Iconic’s software connects design, engineering, commercial, and contractual information within a project.

The platform analyzes these materials to identify potential contradictions, missing information, design problems, and project constraints. The objective is to surface issues while they can still be addressed without causing substantial rework, claims, or delays.

In one review, Iconic identified that a proposed industrial plant’s plot plan placed part of the facility inside a safety boundary where construction was prohibited.

Because the issue was detected during the design stage, the project team could address it before construction began. Iconic said this avoided the possibility of redesign work and months of delay.

The example illustrates how the company plans to use AI for more than storing or retrieving project documents. Its software is designed to understand relationships between different files and identify inconsistencies that may not be visible when each document is reviewed independently.

Iconic has not disclosed performance data demonstrating how consistently its software identifies these issues across different project types. Human engineers and project leaders will still need to evaluate the system’s findings and determine whether corrective action is required.

Creating Reusable Project Knowledge

Iconic also plans to help organizations preserve lessons from completed and ongoing capital projects.

Project knowledge can be difficult to retain when it remains with individual employees, consultants, or contractors. When those people move to other assignments, later teams may repeat earlier mistakes.

The company’s platform applies previous lessons and organizational standards to new project materials. Iconic intends to develop blueprints tailored to specific types of capital projects so that information gathered from one development can improve future work.

article_title: From Rs 3,800 crore to Rs 16,000 crore in 18 months: Angel One-backed Ionic Wealth raises Rs 177 crore
article_excerpt:
Ionic Wealth, the wealth management platform backed by Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in a strategic funding round led by Angel One and a group of marquee families.
The fresh capital takes the total it has raised since starting operations in 2024 to around Rs 466 crore.
All investors from the previous round participated again. The company said its backers include business families, Bollywood personalities, fintech entrepreneurs, global CXOs, board advisors and media houses.
Where the capital will go
Ionic Wealth said the capital will be used to strengthen its portfolio-led proposition, integrate AI into its platform, expand its ultra-high-net-worth individual (UHNI) business, hire specialised talent and grow its presence in India and overseas markets.
It plans to scale its high-net-worth individual (HNI) business through technology and build a dedicated UHNI proposition for India's leading families. It also wants to strengthen global investing through GIFT City, where its business is registered with the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).
The company also plans to expand product access through the Accredited Investor framework and Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs).
Introduced by SEBI to bridge the gap between mutual funds and portfolio management services (PMS), SIFs operate under a regulatory framework that came into effect on April 1, 2025.
Under SEBI's SIF framework, investors must maintain a minimum aggregate investment of Rs 10 lakh across all SIF strategies offered by a single asset management company, while accredited investors are exempt from this requirement.
How fast it has grown
Ionic Wealth said it has crossed Rs 16,000 crore in assets under management (AUM). It now serves more than 2,900 HNI and UHNI clients across more than 12 cities through a team of over 100 private bankers.
In March 2025, the company had an AUM of around Rs 3,800 crore and about 680 clients. Both numbers have grown a little more than four times in roughly 18 months. At current levels, the average client has about Rs 5.5 crore invested with the firm.
Much of that growth has come recently. In its results for the September 2026 quarter, announced on 15 October, Angel One reported Ionic Wealth's AUM at Rs 16,000 crore, up 19.1% from the previous quarter, with more than 2,975 clients.
That puts AUM at the end of June 2026 at roughly Rs 13,400 crore. Ionic Asset, the group's proprietary asset management offering, had an AUM of Rs 1,760 crore.
In May 2025, Subramanian told PTI that 75% of the then Rs 3,800 crore AUM was recurring, and that the company employed about 165-170 people. At that point it operated in nine cities: Mumbai, Delhi, Gurugram, Chennai, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, Baroda, Kolkata and Pune.
From Angel One Wealth to Ionic Wealth
Angel One set up the business in March 2024 as Angel One Wealth, bringing in a team of wealth managers as co-founders. Subramanian, who was previously at Kotak Cherry, the digital wealth arm of Kotak Mahindra Bank, joined as co-founder and CEO.
Shobhit Mathur joined as co-founder to lead wealth-tech and customer excellence, while co-founder Dharmendra Jain brought experience in investment solutions and product development.
In mid-2024, Angel One announced a Rs 250 crore investment in the wealth arm to fund technology, AI and analytics, and market expansion. The business has since been renamed Ionic Wealth. Its first Rs 290 crore came from Rs 250 crore put in by Angel One and Rs 40 crore from 10 Indian families.

company_description: Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities.
article_title: AidenAI Nets $32 Mn To Scale Enterprise AI Workflows
article_excerpt: Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities. The fresh capital will be used to invest in its platform and engineering talent as it looks to scale its global enterprise AI business. “With A91 as our partner, we are excited to invest in our people and platforms and help shape the next wave of enterprise technology services,” AidenAI founder and CEO Srinivas Kamadi said. How AidenAI Builds Its Enterprise AI Business Kamadi founded AidenAI in 2023 after spending nearly two decades with Infosys. Drawing on his experience of leading digital transformation at the company, Kamadi launched AidenAI to solve a recurring bottleneck faced by large enterprises: enterprise AI was stuck in the experimentation phase because outdated legacy systems made digital transformation too slow. The New Jersey-based startup, whose majority of workforce is based out of Hyderabad, helps large enterprises integrate AI into existing applications, data infrastructure and business workflows. Its proprietary AI Builder Platform is designed to help businesses move beyond AI experimentation and deploy AI applications within their existing tech infrastructure. This platform connects with an enterprise's existing systems and AI models, providing tools for AI agents. The startup also offers AiDAP, an AI-driven technology modernisation platform that helps enterprises modernise legacy software systems. This positions AidenAI in the enterprise AI implementation market, where businesses are increasingly looking for solutions to integrate AI into business-critical operations rather than deploy standalone tools. “While enterprise AI adoption is still in its early stages, AidenAI has spent the last 3 years helping over 30 large enterprises turn the promise of AI into live, measurable business outcomes," said A91 Partners' partner Kaushik Anand. AidenAI's Bet On Frontier AI Engineering Alongside its platform expansion, AidenAI plans to build a team of more than 1,000 frontier AI engineers through its AidenAI Builder Academy. The academy is designed to develop forward-deployed engineering talent that can work directly with enterprise clients to build and deploy production-ready AI applications using the company's platform and frontier AI models. The expansion comes as enterprises increasingly explore agentic AI applications to automate complex, multi-step workflows across functions such as finance, insurance, healthcare and human resources. AidenAI aims to tap this demand by combining AI agents, enterprise software modernisation and specialised engineering services. This comes as the broader Indian enterprise AI market, which was valued at $11 Bn in 2025, is projected to reach $71 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s Bharat AI Startups Report 2026. The Inc42 Take: Can AidenAI Scale Its Enterprise AI Platform? As more companies adopt GenAI in their daily operations, demand is growing for providers that can build and deploy AI solutions at an enterprise scale. AidenAI is positioning itself at this intersection via its AI Builder Platform and engineering-led deployment model. Its presence across six countries and a client base of over 30 enterprises provide an early indication of market traction. However, the startup’s ability to scale will depend on how effectively it can standardise its platform across enterprise customers with different technology infrastructure and business requirements.

FinTech Funding July 2026: Indian FinTechs raise USD 124.4 Mn across 8 deals
                    The largest deal of the month came from Veriqus, which raised USD 40.1 million from Norwest and Peak XV Partners, followed by BusinessNext's USD 40 million fundraise from ServiceNow.
                                    
Indian FinTechs raised USD 124.4 million across 8 deals in July 2026, according to data collated by 1Lattice.
The month witnessed funding activity across wealth management, asset management, financial services, lending, digital banking, fintech infrastructure, artificial intelligence and insurance technology.
The largest deal of the month came from Veriqus, a provider of wealth management, asset management and business advisory services, which raised USD 40.1 million from Norwest and Peak XV Partners.
This was followed by BusinessNext, a provider of composable platforms for CRM, data management, lending and AI agent solutions, which secured USD 40 million from ServiceNow.
Together, the three largest transactions accounted for USD 116.4 million, or nearly 94 per cent of the total funding raised during July.
Among the other deals during the month:
Savemfi, a financial services provider offering accessible microcredit solutions, raised USD 4.2 million from Indian Overseas Bank and Northern Arc Capital.
Spense, a provider of APIs and SDKs for fintech and digital banking, secured USD 2.8 million from Arkam Ventures, Razorpay and Talivorra Capital.
Hop, a digital bank for individuals, raised USD 0.8 million from Zaggle.
NeuralKart, a developer of artificial intelligence platforms for industrial risk insurance automation, raised USD 0.2 million from Inflection Point Ventures.
At the early-stage segment:
BimaKavach, a provider of digital insurance brokerage services for various business risks, raised an undisclosed amount from Beyond Capital Ventures.
Funding activity in July was significantly lower than the previous month, with total funding declining to USD 124.4 million across 8 deals, compared with USD 935.5 million across 10 deals in June 2026.
The sharp month on month decline was largely due to the absence of a mega round comparable to CRED's USD 900 million fundraise in June, which accounted for more than 96 per cent of that month's total funding.

article_title: Yulu raises funds $93 million round of equity and debt for expansion, new business
article_excerpt:
Yulu, a mobility-as-a-service startup platform, raised $87.5 million as part of its Series C round in a mix of equity and debt to expand its electric vehicle operations, the company said on Wednesday.
“Over the next two years, we plan to quadruple the number of vehicles on the road from 50,000 to 200,000,” company co-founder and chief executive Amit Gupta said in an interview with Mint. “A portion of those vehicles will be bought through the equity we've raised, but the rest through debt or leasing.”
Of the $93 million round, $57.5 million came from global private equity firm GEF Capital Partners, which focuses on backing companies combating climate change and pollution.
A secondary component of $5.5 million from GEF gave some of the company’s early institutional investors an exit, according to Gupta. Among the investors in Yulu's $2.62 million seed round in 2017 were Firebolt Ventures, 3one4 Capital, Wavemaker Partners, Blume Ventures and Incubate Fund Asia.
The 2017 round saw participation from angel investors as well, including Freshworks' Girish Mathrubootham, Flipkart's Binny Bansal and InMobi Group's Naveen Tiwari.
Debt of $30 million was raised from two European lenders that Gupta declined to identify, citing non-disclosure agreements.
Venture capital and private equity firms have become increasingly bullish on India's energy transition market, ranging from electric vehicles to energy storage solutions. This even as funding into the sector has fallen consistently since 2023, when it stood at $3.12 billion across 279 deals. The sector has raised $1.6 billion across 101 deals so far this year.
Nonetheless, global investment firm Brookfield said last month it would deploy $600 million through a renewable energy platform for solar, wind and battery storage projects. Transition VC, an energy-focused fund, announced a ₹1,500 crore second fund, almost double its maiden ₹800 crore investment vehicle.
Yulu’s fundraise comes just over a year after it closed its Series B round. Last year, it raised an extension to its Series B at $11.3 million, led by Magna International. Overall, Yulu raised $113.6 million as part of its Series B round, setting its post-money valuation at $222 million, according to startup intelligence platform Tracxn.
The Bengaluru-based EV startup operates in 12 cities—through four company-owned entities across Bengaluru, Mumbai, the National Capital Region and Hyderabad, and eight franchises in regional markets.
“Over the next 12 months, we should be live in 20 cities through a combination of company-owned and franchises,” said Gupta.
The new cities will be chosen based on delivery-density data from quick-commerce partners and bike taxis and not through a fixed regional strategy, given that the company is launching a new business vertical called Yulu Express.
Yulu launched its new business vertical via a pilot of 500 e-bikes last year, and with the new infusion of capital, plans to scale it up. This business, instead of catering to quick-commerce gig workers, will focus on e-commerce logistics, bike taxis and express parcel delivery, extending beyond the low-speed two-wheelers in its core fleet.
Even though it’s a new business line, Gupta said the fundamental strategies don't shift, just that a new market is being targeted.
“My customer remains the gig worker. Platforms are my partners who bring me demand,” Gupta said. “This actually leads us to be a zero CAC business.”
CAC, or customer acquisition cost, is the combined sales and marketing effort needed to win new paying customers over a time period. Lower CAC means less money spent and better unit economics.
For the time being, Yulu plans to roll out Express where it already has the infrastructure before starting in new markets. After two years, Gupta said he expects two-thirds of the startup's fleet to consist of its core low-speed Dex delivery vehicles, and the remainder will consist of its mid-speed ones.

article_title: Cosine Robots Bags ₹22.4 Cr To Scale Robotics Hardware Production
article_excerpt: Bengaluru-based robotics hardware startup Cosine Robots has raised ₹22.4 Cr (about $2.4 Mn) in a funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors. The startup will use the fresh capital to scale its new R&D and production facility in Bengaluru, expand its engineering team, and accelerate development of its integrated servo actuator portfolio. Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas in 2024, Cosine Robots develops actuators and motion systems for robotic applications. Actuators convert energy into physical movement, helping control how precisely robotic joints move and how much turning force, or torque, they produce. “Our goal is to make high-quality robotics more accessible. This funding will help us strengthen our research and development and establish production capabilities for actuators designed and built by our team,” cofounder and CEO Koshy said. Building Robotic Motion Hardware Cosine Robots’ integrated servo actuators combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics, and proprietary control software into a single system. The startup said developing these components together allows it to optimise precision, reliability, torque response, and cost. Its modular portfolio includes cycloidal and planetary actuators, which use different gearbox designs to address varying torque requirements. These are designed for applications ranging from industrial robotic arms and collaborative robots to quadrupeds and humanoids. The startup said its proprietary control architecture combines dual-position sensing with a 25 kHz control loop, executing 25,000 updates per second to regulate movement and torque. Cosine Robots aims to supply global robot manufacturers with an alternative to established actuator suppliers, competing on performance and cost. The funding comes at a time when investments in robotics and automation startups are picking up. Last week, Botsync raised $11 Mn in an IvyCap Ventures-led round to upgrade its factory automation software and mobile robots, and expand its engineering and project delivery teams in India. Earlier this year, industrial robotics startup Anscer Robotics raised ₹45 Cr in its Series A round to advance its product platform, scale US market operations, expand global partner network, and deepen international footprint.

article_excerpt:
HIFI raises $37M Series A to expand tokenized capital markets infrastructure
Photo: David Yu / Pexels
The Jersey City startup is building plumbing for onchain repo trades and stablecoin payments, and Wall Street is starting to notice
Tokenized capital markets got another vote of confidence this week. HIFI, a two-year-old infrastructure company based in Jersey City, closed a $37 million Series A round led by Left Lane Capital, with participation from Antler, Arcanum Capital, Exitfund, and Side Door Ventures.
What HIFI actually does
HIFI offers a composable API platform that lets businesses move, convert, route, and orchestrate value across stablecoins and conventional bank systems simultaneously. The platform handles inflows and outflows, programmable workflows and controls, and real-world asset tokenization. HIFI is registered as a money services business and works alongside existing banking partners rather than trying to replace them.
Since January 2025, the platform has processed more than $227 million in stablecoin payments across over 6 million transactions on Polygon. For a 35-person company, that throughput is meaningful.
The repo trades that matter
In June 2026, HIFI executed a live onchain repo trade involving tokenized U.S. Treasuries. The transaction used atomic delivery-versus-payment settlement on the Canton Network, Digital Asset’s private distributed ledger platform, with DRW, Marex, and Tradeweb as counterparties. Atomic DvP means both legs of the trade, the asset transfer and the cash payment, settle simultaneously with no gap between them.

Index Industries announced on November 10, 2026 that it had emerged from stealth with a $50 million seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Polychain Capital, Galaxy Ventures, Wintermute Ventures and other institutional investors also participated. The company is building technology and infrastructure intended to make U.S. housing a broadly investable asset class.
Its platform combines a daily-reporting index, tokenization technology, and real-estate and capital-markets services to support third-party housing-linked investment products. USHP, based on Index Industries’ U.S. Home Price Index and issued by USHP Limited, is planned as the first investment product built on the platform.
A Daily Benchmark for U.S. Home Prices
The USHP Index is designed to be calculated daily and integrate data from major housing indices into one national measure. Its intended uses include housing-market research, reporting, portfolio monitoring and housing-related financial products. Index Industries describes the planned USHP asset as offering liquid exposure to U.S. home-price movements without requiring an investor to buy, finance or maintain a property.
Those product plans have not yet become launches. The release said the USHP Index was expected to launch imminently, while USHP Limited planned to release USHP on Ethereum in 2026 and expand to Solana in 2027.
Index Industries characterizes U.S. housing as a $55 trillion market and says broad exposure to national home prices has remained difficult to obtain through traditional financial products.
The company’s website presents direct property investment as capital intensive, with high transaction costs and transactions that can take weeks or months. It also contrasts property-specific and local-market exposure with its proposed national-index approach.
Co-founder and CEO Josh Rosenthal said indexing “reduces the expertise and cost barriers to investing in an entire market, which is what U.S. housing needs.”
Separate Issuer and Non-U.S. Eligibility
USHP Limited is a British Virgin Islands company and a subsidiary of the USHP Foundation, a Cayman Islands foundation company.
The USHP product site identifies Index Industries as a technology infrastructure and services provider to the USHP Foundation, not the issuer of USHP or an affiliate of the issuer. Index Industries does not offer, sell or distribute USHP. Any offering would be made solely by the issuer under definitive offering documents, only to eligible non-U.S. persons outside the United States, subject to eligibility verification and applicable law.
That structure separates Index Industries’ index and technology work from the issuance and distribution of the proposed investment product.
Founders and Lead Investor
Rosenthal previously served as President and General Partner of Polychain Capital. Co-founder and Chairman Brian Hardecker founded Longmark and serves as its CEO; he was previously a Principal in Blackstone’s Real Estate & Private Equity Group. Longmark was formed in 2021 and reports $2 billion in U.S. residential assets under management.
Lightspeed partner Justin Overdorff said the firm’s decision to lead the round reflected Index Industries’ combination of institutional real-estate experience and tokenization technology, as well as its partnership with Longmark.

article_title: Ionic Wealth Raises ₹177 Cr as AUM Crosses ₹16,000 Cr
article_excerpt:
Mumbai-based wealth-tech company Ionic Wealth has raised ₹177 crore in fresh funding from parent company Angel One and a group of existing investors, bringing its cumulative capital raised to approximately ₹466 crore. The investment comes as the company expands its AI-powered wealth management services and looks to strengthen its presence among affluent investors in India and overseas.
The company has also reported a sharp increase in assets under management (AUM), which crossed ₹16,000 crore as of September 2026, compared with approximately ₹3,800 crore in March 2025.
Ionic plans to use the latest capital to strengthen its portfolio management capabilities, expand its ultra-high-net-worth individual (UHNI) business, invest further in artificial intelligence, and develop international investment services through GIFT City.
The funding reflects Angel One's continued investment in wealth management as the financial services group expands beyond its traditional stockbroking business.
For Ionic Wealth, the next challenge is scaling personalized investment services while using technology to improve portfolio analysis, customer engagement, and the efficiency of its advisory operations.
Angel One Backs Ionic Wealth's Expansion
The ₹177 crore round saw participation from Angel One and investors who had backed the company previously.
According to the funding announcement, all investors from the earlier round participated again. The investor group includes business families, fintech entrepreneurs, global executives, and other private investors.
The investment brings Ionic Wealth's total capital raised since its establishment in 2024 to approximately ₹466 crore.
The company was co-founded by Srikanth Subramanian, Shobhit Mathur, and Dharmendra Jain.
It operates a wealth management platform that combines digital investment tools with personalized advisory services for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
Ionic intends to strengthen its portfolio-led wealth management offerings rather than focus solely on selling individual financial products.
The strategy involves helping clients manage investments across different asset classes while providing research, portfolio analysis, and access to specialized investment opportunities.
The company also plans to recruit additional professionals and expand its operations in domestic and international markets.
However, Ionic has not disclosed its valuation in the latest announcement or provided a detailed breakdown of how the ₹177 crore will be allocated across its expansion priorities.

Ionic Wealth's latest funding follows rapid growth in its client base and assets under management.

Ionic has not disclosed its latest revenue, profitability, or the proportion of AUM growth generated through new client inflows.
Those figures would provide a clearer picture of how the company's expanding client base is contributing to its financial performance.

article_title: Kerala startup mistEO raises Rs 18 crore to expand climate risk intelligence for lenders and insurers
article_excerpt:
Thiruvananthapuram-based climate and weather intelligence startup mistEO has raised Rs 18 crore in a seed round led by MGF-Kavachh, a SEBI-registered Category II Alternative Investment Fund that invests in defence and strategic technology companies.
Bengaluru-based Seafund and other investors also participated. Key Venture was the financial adviser to the transaction.
The startup announced the round on Thursday at Huddle Global 2026, the eighth edition of the startup festival organised by Kerala Startup Mission, which is being held at Kovalam from 12 to 14 November.
Scaling CDI platform
mistEO will use the capital to scale its Climate Decision Intelligence (CDI) platform for banks, insurers and agri-value chains in India and Asia, improve its forecasting and risk models, and grow its team. It also plans to build a partnership-led presence across Asia, alongside its existing work in Australia and Central Asia.
CDI combines physics-based numerical weather modelling with AI and machine learning, and fuses satellite, radar, IoT and ground-sensor data. The aim is to show a client how the weather will affect a specific farm, asset or loan, and what action to take.
The forecasts come from mistEO's proprietary model, Indra, which currently delivers forecasts at 3 km spatial resolution across three windows: 0-6 hours, 6-24 hours and 24-48 hours.
The startup is also developing applications for port and maritime operations, solar and wind generation forecasting for grid operators, weather routing for mobility and logistics fleets, and flood and heavy-rainfall intelligence for disaster response.
"A missed forecast can mean a loss of life, a failed crop, a stressed loan or an unplanned claim," said Samuel John, Founder and CEO of mistEO.
"Climate risk is experienced at the level of a farm, a branch, an asset, not a national average. Lenders and insurers need physical-risk data they can price, lend and pay out against, and that is what we deliver for an individual borrower, branch or insured asset," he said.
"With a very strong El Niño expected to persist into early 2027, the need for such capabilities is growing," John added.
Where its products are used
In India, mistEO works with NABARD and UNDP on DiCRA, or Data in Climate Resilient Agriculture, an open-access platform that provides climate resilience data for agriculture and its sub-sectors.
In Australia, its livestock early warning system alerts cattle farmers to heat-stress conditions up to seven days in advance. The company said the system protects more than AUD 1 billion of livestock assets. Its website cites Rangers Valley, which it describes as one of Australia's largest cattle operations, as a customer that uses the platform to index heat-stress exposure and hedge mortality risk.
In Uzbekistan, mistEO is deploying a weather-based parametric insurance stack, in which forecast-based weather triggers start payouts to livestock and crop farmers.
The startup is also building a thunderstorm nowcasting model for the Indian Air Force as an iDEX awardee, and is working on early warning systems for the Indian Navy and for a mobility OEM.

article_title: Everful Raises $48.5m Series A to Expand AI-Powered Global Sourcing Platform
article_excerpt:
Everful, a startup developing artificial intelligence infrastructure for global commerce, has raised $48.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, according to an announcement.
The round was also backed by existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.
The San Francisco-based company said the proceeds would support its expansion in the US, its largest market, and Europe, while strengthening its AI technology and fulfilment network.
Founded in 2024 by former Alibaba executive Sisi Song and AI entrepreneur Kevin Han, Everful connects retailers and brands with manufacturers through an AI-powered sourcing and supply chain platform.
The company currently ships more than 5 million items monthly to customers in over 60 countries and works with more than 30,000 vetted factories.
Its product catalogue has grown to more than 20 million items, and it expects to reach $100 million in annualised revenue by the end of 2026.
Everful is targeting inefficiencies in global sourcing, where retailers often rely on intermediaries, manual communications and fragmented supplier information to procure products.
These processes can lead to higher costs, large minimum order requirements and excess inventory.
Its platform uses large language models and computer vision to analyse supply and demand data, identify trending products, assess manufacturers, and coordinate orders.
The system also draws on quality information from factory inspections to evaluate suppliers.
Retailers can source products through wholesale, dropshipping and customisation arrangements, with Everful managing fulfilment.
“AI lets us turn that team into software,” Song said, referring to the traditional reliance on overseas sourcing personnel.
She said the platform aims to give businesses access to global sourcing capabilities without having to build their own teams.
Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India Senior Executive Director Jessica Koh said smaller retailers often face difficulties finding reliable suppliers, while January Capital Partner Alex Rankin pointed to the company’s growing transaction data as a potential competitive advantage.
Everful said each order, inspection and delivery adds information to its proprietary model of global supply and demand, allowing its AI systems to improve supplier matching and sourcing decisions over time.
The latest financing brings together investors backing the company’s efforts to build an AI-driven alternative to traditional wholesale sourcing and procurement networks.

Marble, a capital markets startup founded by former BitGo and Galaxy Digital executives, announced its launch on November 10, 2026, with an $11 million Series Seed round led by Polychain Capital. The company is building private-credit infrastructure for AI compute operators alongside an institutional trading platform spanning digital assets, prediction markets and compute.
Maven 11, Ripple, Susquehanna Crypto, Lattice and Blockwall Ventures participated, together with other venture and strategic investors and a group of AI-focused angel investors. Marble plans to use the proceeds to hire across compute financing, trading, risk, legal and operations and to establish the trading, custody and banking connectivity behind Marble Markets.
Co-founders Matt Ballensweig and Leon Marshall serve as co-CEOs. Ballensweig was most recently BitGo’s global head of trading and previously co-headed trading and lending at Genesis. Marshall was CEO of Galaxy Digital’s European business and previously worked at Genesis, Apollo and Trafigura.
Credit for Mid-Market AI Operators
Marble Compute is designed as an asset-management platform connecting institutional investors with independent AI cloud providers, or neoclouds, and GPU operators. The founders say the largest neoclouds and hyperscalers can finance growth through public markets and major banks, while smaller operators have fewer and less flexible options even when customers have committed to purchasing their capacity.
Marble Compute is not designed to lend from its own balance sheet. Instead, it will source opportunities, conduct diligence and underwriting, and structure each financing for investors. Its underwriting will examine the hardware, the creditworthiness of contracted customers and the operator’s ability to service debt, while seeking diversified customer commitments so that financing is supported by contracted cash flows.
Subject to regulatory approvals, the planned sequence begins with loans syndicated directly between operators and institutional lenders. Later stages would add single-opportunity off-chain vehicles and on-chain vaults for individual GPU operators, followed by diversified multi-opportunity funds as deal flow and a track record develop.
Principal Trading and Shared Collateral
Marble Markets is planned around principal trading: clients would face Marble directly, with Marble trading from its own capital. Client assets would remain with their existing custodians, brokerages and banks. A high-touch desk would handle trading, backed by a client platform showing positions, collateral and exposure in one place.
The planned product set includes digital-asset spot trading, borrowing, lending and derivatives; large-block bilateral prediction-market trading; over-the-counter compute forwards; and, over the longer term, tokenized equities and equity swaps. Rather than requiring clients to prefund each counterparty separately, the design would let them use one pool of eligible digital and traditional collateral across markets. Marble says its Markets lending would be overcollateralized, meaning backed by collateral exceeding the loan’s value.

Analytics Insight Releases India FinTech Funding Report for H1 2026, Companies Raise $2.2 Billion
PNN
Hyderabad (Telangana) [India], August 13: Analytics Insight has released its India FinTech Funding Report for H1 2026, providing an analysis of funding activity, investor behavior, and capital flows across India's fintech ecosystem during the first half of the year.
According to the report, the country's fintech segment raised $2.2 billion in aggregate funding during H1 2026, indicating that this is one of its best-performing six-month periods in terms of fintech investments since H1 2023.
Contrary to a resurgence in the high number of investments recorded during previous years, this trend indicates a more strategic approach by investors in their funding for the segment, as they are beginning to concentrate their money on businesses that have already developed a sustainable business model.
Key Findings from India FinTech Funding Report H1 2026
The report highlights several major trends shaping India's fintech funding landscape:
-        $2.2 Billion in Funding: Indian fintech companies raised $2.2 billion in H1 2026, the highest half-year funding level since H1 2023.
-        Late-Stage Fintechs Dominate: More than 70% of total funding went to late-stage fintech companies, including CRED, Weaver Services, Juspay, Ecofy Finance and Namdev Finvest.
-        Lending Leads Sector Funding: Lending emerged as the largest-funded fintech segment, followed by Payments. Together, the two sectors accounted for more than three-quarters of total funding during the period.
-        Wealthtech Gains Investor Interest: WealthTech also emerged as an important area of investor interest during H1 2026.
-        Bengaluru Leads Geographically: Bengaluru retained its position as India's leading fintech funding hub, attracting almost 70% of total funding, followed by Mumbai.
-        Capital Concentrated in Mature Companies: Unicorns accounted for more than half of the capital invested in India's fintech ecosystem during the first half of 2026.
-        Institutional Investors Remain Active: Institutional investors were the most active investor group, while domestic investors continued to participate across different financing stages.
-        Foreign Capital Targets Mature Fintechs: International investors showed stronger activity in mature fintech companies, particularly at the growth stage.
-        Strategic Capital Gains Prominence: Corporate and strategic investors increased their participation, reflecting a broader shift towards investments linked to strategic business objectives and long-term industry opportunities.
The report also looks at structural shifts in India's fintech investment ecosystem, including investment concentration, investment themes, strategic investments, and exits via IPOs and acquisitions.
The fintech investment ecosystem in India has therefore gone past being a pure growth funding ecosystem. Observations in the first half of 2026 show that investors are increasingly looking at the fundamentals of the business, maturity, and sustainable growth of fintech companies.
"India's fintech sector continues to demonstrate resilience while entering a more mature phase of capital deployment. The $2.2 billion raised in H1 2026 is significant not only because it marks the strongest half-year performance since H1 2023, but also because the funding reflects greater investor selectivity," said Ashish Sukhadeve, CEO, Analytics Insight.
He further added, "Our H1 2026 report provides a data-driven view of where capital is moving, which fintech segments are attracting investor attention, and how the investor landscape is changing. The growing concentration of funding in mature companies, the strength of lending and payments, Bengaluru's continued dominance and the increasing role of strategic investors offer important signals for founders, investors and other stakeholders planning for the next phase of India's fintech growth."

article_excerpt:
India's fintech sector raises $2 bn in H1 2026, led by late-stage funding
Funding in India's fintech sector rose 42 per cent year-on-year to $2 billion in H1 2026, with late-stage companies accounting for four-fifths of the total capital raised
Listen to This Article
	India's fintech industry raised $2 billion in the first half of calendar year 2026 (H1 2026) across 106 rounds, a 42 per cent rise from the $1.4 billion raised across 186 rounds in H1 2025, according to data from market intelligence platform Tracxn.
	Sequentially, funding nearly doubled from $1.1 billion across 120 rounds in H2 2025.
	In H1 2026, Cred raised $900 million in a Series H round, followed by KreditBee's $280 million Series E round and Weaver's $156 million Series D round.
	About 80 per cent, or $1.6 billion, of the funding raised in H1 2026 went to late-stage companies, followed by 18.35 per cent, or $367 million, to early-stage firms. The remaining $68.6 million was absorbed by seed-stage startups.
	The period also saw two companies go public — Kissht and Turtlemint. Square Yards and KreditBee emerged as unicorns.
	Fintech companies recorded seven acquisitions in H1 2026, a decline of 30 per cent from 10 acquisitions in H2 2025 and 56 per cent from 16 acquisitions in H1 2025, the report said.

article_title: India's capital markets raise Rs 10 lakh crore annually, m-cap tops $5 trillion: SEBI Chairman
article_excerpt:
India's capital markets raise Rs 10 lakh crore annually, m-cap tops $5 trillion: SEBI Chairman
Equity market cap crosses $5 trillion as IPOs, corporate bonds and AIFs fuel business financing
Follow The Hawk on Google News+ Follow
Advertisement
Mumbai: India's capital markets have emerged as a major source of business financing as companies have raised around Rs 10 lakh crore annually through equity and debt instruments over the past decade, Tuhin Kanta Pandey, Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), has said.
Addressing the CII Financing Summit 2026 here, Pandey said the country's capital markets have witnessed significant expansion, supported by strong economic growth, rising investor participation and sustained regulatory reforms.
Advertisement
He noted that India's equity market capitalisation has crossed $5 trillion, equivalent to nearly Rs 500 lakh crore, during the current financial year.
Also readMaha govt targets $100 billion infrastructure investment over next five years
Highlighting primary market activity, Pandey said 235 companies have collectively raised around Rs 1.5 lakh crore through initial public offerings (IPOs) so far in FY27, underscoring robust investor appetite for new listings.
According to him, corporate bonds continue to play a crucial role in diversifying financing sources for businesses and reducing dependence on traditional bank lending.
Outstanding corporate bonds stood at approximately Rs 62 lakh crore as of August 2026 which is nearly 55 per cent of the bank credit extended to industry and services sectors, adds Pandey.
Also readNew NHAI guidelines to boost emergency response on National Highways
Companies have raised more than Rs 5 lakh crore through bond issuances during the current financial year so far, he said.
The SEBI chief also highlighted the growing role of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) in providing risk capital to emerging enterprises and businesses that may not yet be ready to access public markets.
He said cumulative investments by AIFs had reached around Rs 7.5 lakh crore by September 2026, while committed capital exceeded Rs 18 lakh crore.
Advertisement
On infrastructure financing and capital recycling, Pandey said Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) have enabled developers to monetise operational assets and redeploy capital into new projects while offering investors access to income-generating assets. Assets managed by REITs and InvITs have grown to more than Rs 10 lakh crore, according to him.
He said India's capital markets today cater to a wide spectrum of financing requirements, ranging from corporate expansion and venture funding to infrastructure development and long-term capital formation.
Pandey also stated that continued economic growth, broader investor participation and policy reforms have strengthened the capital markets ecosystem and positioned it as a key pillar supporting India's investment and development agenda.

company_description: Tiger Global-backed fintech startup BharatPe has raised Rs 135 crore (about $14 million) in debt funding ahead of a potential initial public offering (IPO).
article_title: Exclusive: BharatPe secures Rs 135 crore in debt, rejigs payment aggregator biz ahead of IPO
article_excerpt:
Tiger Global-backed fintech startup BharatPe has raised Rs 135 crore (about $14 million) in debt funding ahead of a potential initial public offering (IPO).
The round was led by InnoVen Capital and also saw participation from Neo Group and Alteria Capital.
BharatPe’s board allotted 13,500 non-convertible debentures, with a face value of Rs 1 lakh each, to raise the aforementioned sum, according to its regulatory filings with the Registrar of Companies.
InnoVen led the round with an investment of Rs 80 crore. Neo Group invested Rs 40 crore through two of its alternative investment funds, while Alteria participated with Rs 15 crore.
This comes months after BharatPe secured Rs 90 crore in a debt funding round led by RevX Capital.
1. BharatPe is set to merge its payment aggregator businesses: Separately, BharatPe has also received shareholder approval to combine its payment aggregator (PA) online and PA physical businesses into a single entity.
As part of the restructuring, Resilient Payments Private Limited, which secured an online PA licence from the Reserve Bank of India last April, will be merged into Resilient Innovations Private Limited, BharatPe’s parent entity.
“In view of the Master Directions on Regulation of Payment Aggregators dated September 15, 2025, since both online and offline payment aggregation activities are regulated, it is intended to consolidate the PA business in the group into a single entity,” BharatPe said.
Post-merger, Resilient Innovations Pvt Ltd will undertake both online and physical PA activities. Currently, it only serves as an offline PA, facilitating merchants in accepting payments via UPI QR codes and point-of-sale (PoS) devices.
2. BharatPe IPO is in the offing: This comes at a time when BharatPe is preparing for a potential public listing. In September 2025, CNBC-TV18 reported that the company had started scheduling meetings with bankers for a possible IPO.
While the report was scant on details about the size of the IPO, the fintech major could file its IPO documents by the end of FY27.
According to CEO Nalin Negi, BharatPe is prioritising profitability and would go public when market conditions are favourable.
“There will be a pre-IPO funding round, while an IPO is not on the cards for FY26. Anything beyond that is a fair game, once the market conditions are right,” Negi was quoted as saying by PTI.
3. A number of fintech startups are making a beeline for Dalal Street: PhonePe, which recently received a licence from the Central Bank of the UAE to launch operations in its first overseas market, filed its updated IPO prospectus with SEBI last year. In May, MediaNama exclusively reported that Razorpay received shareholder approval to raise over Rs 2,700 crore through its planned IPO.
While PhonePe earlier put its listing plans on the back burner amid the US-Iran war and ensuing market volatility, it is likely to restart its IPO process following the government’s decision to bring back the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on large UPI transactions, according to a Mint report. The company is now targeting a listing between February and March 2027.
Last week, the National Payments Corporation of India said businesses will have to pay 0.4% MDR on UPI person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions above Rs 2,000 from October 15, capped at Rs 300 for transfers of Rs 75,000 and more.
The new MDR regime exempts merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes.
According to Bernstein estimates, a 40-basis-point MDR on eligible UPI transactions could create an industry revenue pool of Rs 22,000 crore by FY28, with banks cornering the largest share at an estimated Rs 14,000 crore and third-party app providers (TPAPs) such as PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm, BharatPe and MobiKwik capturing around Rs 7,000 crore.

article_excerpt:
Four battery-electric articulated haulers are helping build what is set to be Britain's first major infrastructure program with carbon-neutral construction.
ESKILSTUNA, Sweden, Nov. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Volvo Construction Equipment (Volvo CE) has delivered the world's first A40 Electric articulated haulers to BMJV for the Lower Thames Crossing. The four machines arrived on the Essex worksite this autumn and are helping build the foundations and structures for the road and entrance to the new tunnel under the Thames.
BMJV, a joint venture between Bouygues Travaux Publics and J Murphy & Sons, is operating the haulers. They are charged on site by generators fuelled by British hydrogen produced from renewable energy.
Shaun Pidcock, Lower Thames Crossing Programme Director, said: "Going electric today is no longer about compromise, it's about the benefits. These remarkable machines show that even the heaviest jobs can be done cleanly, and in a way that is better for those working on or living near our sites."
The A40 Electric was the world's first battery-powered articulated hauler in its class to go into serial production. With a 39-tonne payload and a 540kWh battery, it can run for around six hours on a charge, depending on application. SMT GB, Volvo CE's dealer in the UK, supplied and will support the machines.
Darren Fitch, Head of Electromobility Sales Europe at Volvo CE, said: "The Lower Thames Crossing is a showcase for low-carbon construction in action. Our A40 Electric haulers are proving that electrification can meet the demands of major construction projects, with zero exhaust emissions, lower noise and a lower total cost of ownership. Projects like this help reshape expectations for tomorrow."
Part of the biggest investment in the UK's road network for a generation, the Lower Thames Crossing includes 2.6 miles of tunnels under the Thames. Diesel has not been used on its worksites since 2025.

article_title: Exclusive: Univest to raise Rs 75 Cr at Rs 1,500 Cr valuation
article_excerpt:
Stock market advisory platform Univest is in advanced talks to raise around Rs 75 crore (around $8 million) in a fresh funding round at a valuation of Rs 1,500 crore, according to sources familiar with the development.
“An undisclosed family office is leading the round, while Bertelsmann and stand up entertainer Zakir Khan are also participating,” sources told Entrackr.
The new round would value the company at nearly 2.4 times its previous post-money valuation of Rs 615 crore. Univest has achieved an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of around Rs 230 crore in November and is on track to turn PAT positive this month, sources added.
Co-founded in 2022 by Pranit Arora and Avneet Dhamija, Univest is a retail advisory platform that offers general recommendations through its SEBI-registered research analyst (RA) entity, Uniresearch. It provides trading advice across stocks, derivatives and commodities.
The startup raised $10 million in a Series A in December 2024, led by Bertelsmann India. In June 2025, it also concluded its first employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buyback worth Rs 1.61 crore.
Univest competes with several retail investment advisory platforms, including StockGrow, Liquide, Waya, TejiMandi, Stoxbox and INDmoney.
“The transaction is nearing completion, and if nothing goes wrong, the round will be announced soon,” sources said.
BII declined to comment on the story, while Univest did not respond to Entrackr’s queries until the time of publication. The story will be updated if the company responds.
While Univest has yet to file its annual financial statements for FY26, the firm reported Rs 41 crore revenue and Rs 31.84 crore loss in FY25.
A fresh funding round would be a vote of confidence in the firm and its future plans, which could include getting into wealth management directly perhaps. The subscription-based advisory business is obviously counting on a continuation of the rising trend of market participation by retail investors, besides growing affluence of course. To that end, fund raises by a startup like Univest goes well beyond just a financial punt, and is a broader bet on the Indian economy per se.

OSSO plans to expand its presence across NCR in 2027, with five to six additional clinics and surgical units. It also plans to onboard more orthopaedic surgeons as it builds a doctor-led platform focused on orthopaedic care.

AI-powered vendor recovery platform Lawvek has raised $550K in a pre-seed funding round led by Neon Fund, with participation from Inzas Ventures.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its enterprise customer base and strengthen its platform’s ability to identify and recover money owed to businesses by their vendors, Lawvek said in a press release.
Co-founded this year by Amrit Khandelwal and Sudip Chhatui, Lawvek helps enterprises recover vendor overcharges, missed rebates and service credits. It uses AI agents to reconcile contractual terms with invoices, usage data and service records.
The problem stems from enterprises having pricing agreements, discounts and service commitments spread across contracts, billing records and operational data. This makes it difficult to track whether vendors have fulfilled their obligations.
According to McKinsey, unmet supplier commitments can cost large enterprises roughly 2% of their spending. For a company with $1 billion in annual expenditure, this could translate into approximately $20 million in annual losses.
Lawvek’s platform analyses vendor contracts against billing, usage and service records to identify discrepancies. These include price hikes beyond agreed caps, volume discounts missing from invoices and prepaid capacity that businesses may not fully utilise.
When the platform identifies money owed through rebates or service credits, it calculates the amount, collects supporting evidence and submits claims on behalf of customers. It also follows up with vendors and verifies whether the recovery has been reflected in invoices or received as a refund.
The startup is currently helping enterprises in the US identify instances of vendor overpayments and cases where they receive less than what was agreed in their contracts.

article_excerpt:
Gurugram-based everyday silver jewellery brand Zavya has raised Rs 22.6 crore ($2.5 million) in a pre-Series A funding round from Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment arm of Daksham Capital, and existing investor Orios Venture Partners.
The funding round values the company at around Rs 191.5 crore on a post-money basis.
The fresh capital towards accelerating digital growth, strengthening brand building and expanding into physical retail, Zavya said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2021 by Poem Kabra and Ravi Malani, Zavya focuses on everyday 925 sterling silver jewellery, combining contemporary designs with a digital-first distribution strategy. The company said it has achieved EBITDA profitability while scaling its business through a capital-efficient approach.
The latest investment also marks the entry of Daksham Growth Ventures, while Orios Venture Partners has continued to back the company.
Zavya plans to strengthen its presence across direct-to-consumer (D2C) and quick commerce channels, invest in brand building and make its initial foray into physical retail, according to the company.
The funding comes amid changing jewellery consumption patterns in India, with rising gold prices and evolving consumer preferences driving interest in alternative precious metals. Younger consumers are increasingly exploring hallmarked 925 sterling silver jewellery as a more accessible option for everyday wear, combining precious-metal value with contemporary designs.
While silver jewellery has an established presence in international markets, the category remains relatively underpenetrated in India, particularly across organised and online retail channels, presenting an opportunity for design-led brands.
Zavya sells through its own website and mobile application, quick-commerce platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto, and marketplaces including Amazon, Myntra and Nykaa, where it claims to be among the top brands in its category.

Tanglin Ventures will lead the round with an investment of Rs 48 crore. Existing investors Kalari Capital, Endiya Ventures, Bharat Tech Fund and IIFL Fintech Fund will invest Rs 14.4 crore each. Foster Ventures and Tetration Ventures will contribute the remaining amount.

Following the round, Tanglin Ventures will emerge as the largest shareholder in the company with a 10.75% stake. Kalari Capital and Endiya Ventures will hold 10.22% each, while Bharat Tech Fund and IIFL Fintech Fund will own 3.23% each, the filings showed.
Matters.AI had previously raised Rs 55 crore in its seed funding round in 2025, led by Kalari Capital and Endiya Ventures.

Its platform provides real-time data tracing, lineage and fingerprinting, along with endpoint visibility and control. It also offers GenAI governance across tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot, and supports both on-premises and SaaS deployments.
The platform integrates with enterprise software and cloud services, including Zoho, Snowflake, Salesforce, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Databricks.
The company operates in the growing data security and governance market, where it competes with players such as Cyera, Orca Security and Palo Alto Networks.

company_description: Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank.
article_title: InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO

Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round.
The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer service, and diversify into micro-mortgage products, InPrime Finserv said in a press release.
The company also plans to deepen investments in agentic AI and AI co-pilots to improve credit assessment and customer engagement.
Founded by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh in 2021, InPrime began operations in 2023. The company is an AI-first non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on India's emerging middle class, particularly customers operating in the informal economy, including kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour owners, small retailers and micro-entrepreneurs.
InPrime uses AI-driven underwriting, data analytics and an on-ground presence to serve customers who often struggle to access formal credit despite owning property and running established businesses.
The company's AI capabilities are already deployed in its operations. Four in-house AI co-pilots support its credit team, while three agentic AI voice agents handled more than 126,000 customer calls between April and September 2026.
Currently, InPrime operates 46 area offices across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh. It has served more than 27,000 households and disbursed Rs 516.92 crore in loans to date.
As of September 30, 2026, the company's assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 332.8 crore, while its gross non-performing assets (GNPA) were at 0.80%. With the latest fundraise, InPrime's total funding has reached Rs 190 crore.
InPrime's existing investors also include Info Edge Ventures, Kettleborough VC and Titan Capital.

article_title: Disseqt AI raises $8 Mn led by Gresham House Ventures, Rahul Dravid joins round
article_excerpt:
AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.
The round also saw participation from angel investors, including senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, along with former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.
The fresh funds will be utilized to expand its enterprise customer base globally and hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, Disseqt said in a press release.
Founded in late 2025 by Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt AI provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents.
Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their behaviour. It can also block outputs that violate organisational policies while maintaining audit trails for compliance and oversight.
The platform allows enterprises to test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information or exhibiting other vulnerabilities before being deployed in business operations.
The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenues exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier.
Disseqt said it has already deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases. In a project involving a global sports league's fan engagement agent, which serves 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. It added that no unsafe outputs were detected when the original failing tests were repeated after fixes.
The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank.
The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, as enterprises look to deploy autonomous AI systems across customer interactions, financial services and internal business operations.

company_description: Dialysis care provider VitusCare has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors,
article_title: Dialysis care provider VitusCare raises $3 Mn in Series B round
article_excerpt:
Dialysis care provider VitusCare has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, along with several angel investors.
The Gurugram-based company had previously raised $2.7 million in a Series A round led by Tomorrow Capital in April 2024 and Rs 10.83 crore in a seed round in 2019.
The fresh capital will be deployed towards expanding its dialysis centre network, technology development, workforce training and international expansion, VitusCare said in a press release.
The fundraise comes as VitusCare has nearly tripled its revenue since its previous funding round in 2024. The company has expanded its network from 22 to more than 60 dialysis centres across nine states and over 50 cities.
So far, VitusCare has treated more than 35,000 patients and conducted over 8 lakh dialysis sessions. Its workforce has also grown from 110 to 300 employees.
The company said it reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26, supported by faster breakeven at newly opened centres and same-centre growth of over 30%.
Founded in 2017 by Prabhat Shrivastava, VitusCare operates through a capital-light ‘shop-in-shop’ model. It partners with existing hospitals to provide specialised dialysis services instead of setting up standalone facilities.
The company aims to expand its network to more than 100 centres by the end of FY27. It is also exploring opportunities in select Asian markets.
VitusCare is also developing AI-native business modules to improve healthcare delivery and plans to establish a Technician Academy to train dialysis professionals.
The company competes with players such as NephroPlus, Apex Kidney Care, DCDC Kidney Care, 7Med and Rahi Care.
Under the shop-in-shop model, dialysis providers supply equipment, trained medical professionals, technology and operational support while using hospitals’ existing infrastructure. This allows them to expand their reach with lower capital expenditure, particularly in Tier II and III cities.
Other players in the segment include DCDC Kidney Care, which raised Rs 150 crore from Temasek-backed ABC Impact in March 2025, and The Renal Project, which secured $1.3 million in a pre-seed round led by JITO Angel Network in September 2026.

company_description: parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union
article_title: Style Union raises Rs 485 Cr in Series E round led by Elev8 Venture, Venturi Partners
article_excerpt:
Nexon Omniverse, the parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore (approximately $52 million) in a Series E funding round led by Venturi Partners and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners. The round comprises a mix of primary and secondary capital.
The proceeds will be used to expand Style Union's physical store network across key metropolitan markets. This will take the retailer beyond its southern India base into western and northern markets, Nexon Omniverse said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Ekta Biyani, wife of businessman Rakesh Biyani, Style Union is a fast-fashion and value-retail brand that offers affordable everyday apparel, athleisure, ethnic wear, accessories and makeup for men, women and children through online and offline channels.
The company currently operates 200 stores across Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR.
Style Union has scaled its store network from 41 outlets in FY23 to 158 in FY26. Its net revenue grew from Rs 123 crore in FY23 to over Rs 1,150 crore in FY26.
The company is also backed by investors such as B2V Ventures, Manish Chokhani, Rafique Malik of Metro Brands, Ashish Kacholia, Sharrp Ventures, Elcid Investments and the Capri Global family office, among others.
Style Union competes with established players such as Tata Group-owned Zudio, Reliance Retail's fashion brands Trends and Yousta, and Tata Group's Westside. Competition in the segment has increased as retailers expand their store networks and focus on affordable, trend-led fashion for price-conscious consumers.
Style Union has maintained a gross margin of around 47% between FY23 and FY26 and expects to sustain this level in FY27. Meanwhile, its store-level EBITDA margin has improved from approximately 10% in FY23 to 16% in FY26. The company expects this margin to rise further to around 19% in FY27, which would indicate better store-level profitability.

company_description: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt.
article_title: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47 Mn in equity and debt
article_excerpt:
Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt.
According to the press release, Accel led the equity round, which also saw participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading, and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.
The remaining $21 million venture debt was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Founded in 2026 by Manish Agarwal, former CEO of Nazara Technologies, and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs works with AI research labs and robotics companies that need real-world data to train their systems. The founders had earlier co-founded KGeN, a platform focused on building a network of verified users.
The startup collects data by recording how people perform everyday tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. This information is processed and shared with companies developing robots, helping them understand how humans perform different jobs and interact with their surroundings.
Humyn Labs claims to have crossed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of starting operations. It currently runs data collection and processing operations across more than 20 countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.
As per the release, the fresh capital will be used to expand its operations in Brazil, South Korea and India, strengthen its data collection hardware and processing capabilities, and build a larger presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
Earlier in April 2026, the company had announced a $20 million commitment towards expanding its data collection infrastructure across India, Southeast Asia, Latin America and West Asia.
The company is looking to tap the growing demand for real-world data as robotics companies work towards developing machines that can perform tasks in everyday environments.

company_description: Bengaluru-based circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore through a combination of equity and debt.
article_title: Circular economy startup Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 Cr through equity and debt
article_excerpt:
Bengaluru-based circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore through a combination of equity and debt. The round comprises Rs 36.25 crore in equity and Rs 20 crore in debt, with participation from Samara Capital founder and CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global and Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust, associated with Sunrise Foods.
Existing investors, including the family office of Chaitanya Kejriwal of Parkson’s Packaging and Ganesh Natarajan, chairman of 5F World, also participated in the round.
The funds will be used to build recycling infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand its operations in Karnataka. The investment will support industrial processing facilities, distributed pre-processing centres and technology for material traceability and quality control.
Founded by Viral Chhajer, Kunal Kumar, Aayush Killa and Sharan Subaiah, Recove focuses on recycling high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP). It operates a distributed sourcing and pre-processing network, with larger facilities handling washing and granulation.
Recove has signed 10-year memoranda of understanding with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, each involving planned investments of over Rs 500 crore.
Along with its commitments in Karnataka, the company plans to invest more than Rs 2,000 crore across the four states over the next decade. The current fundraise will support the first phase of this expansion in Maharashtra and Karnataka, while the company is pursuing its next opportunity in Uttar Pradesh.
Its washing facility at Harohalli, Bengaluru, has been operational since late 2025 and procures around 600 tonnes of post-consumer plastic every month. A granulation line at the same location started operations in October 2026. The company is also setting up a 1,100-tonne-per-month HDPE and PP granulation plant at Jalgaon MIDC, Maharashtra, which is targeted for commissioning in early FY27.
Recove serves over 30 paying recyclers and converters, with a repeat-order rate of around 90%. It has crossed an annualised revenue run-rate of Rs 40 crore.
