article_title: Exclusive: Shree Anandhaas raises Rs 110 Cr, valuation jumps to Rs 1,900 Cr
article_excerpt:
Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas has raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Ayra Ventures, with participation from existing investor A91 Partners, Waterfield Advisors, the company’s co-founders and other investors.
The company’s board has allotted 12,870 equity shares and 22,523 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 31,079 per share to raise the capital, according to documents reviewed by Entrackr.
Ayra Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 45 crore, while Waterfield Advisors invested Rs 15 crore and A91 Partners infused Rs 10 crore. Ithought Financial Consulting LLP invested Rs 10 crore through an equity allotment in August 2026, while the co-founders collectively invested Rs 7.2 crore. The remaining amount came from several other investors.
The proceeds will be utilised to fund the company's growth and expansion plans, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the latest allotment values Shree Anandhaas at around Rs 1,908 crore, a 3.3X jump from its Series A valuation of Rs 575 crore. However, this appears to be part of a larger funding round, and the company’s valuation could change depending on further investments.
In August 2025, the company closed its Rs 175 crore Series A funding round led by A91 Partners.
Founded in 1998 as a restaurant business, Shree Anandhaas entered the sweets and savouries retail segment in 2017. The family-owned company operates a chain of sweets and snacks outlets across Tamil Nadu.
Following the latest allotment, A91 Partners remains the largest external shareholder with a 26.24% stake, followed by Spring Marketing Capital with 2.41%, Ayra Ventures with 2.36% and Waterfield Advisors with 0.79%. Meanwhile, the co-founders M. Manikanden, N.V. Nammalwar, A. Narayanan, K. Venkatesh and M. Amutha collectively hold a 56.54% stake in the company.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, Shree Anandhaas reported a 20.9% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 284 crore. Its net profit surged 7.1X to Rs 7.64 crore in the same period.

company_description: AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors.
article_title: AI video production startup Lemonpeel raises $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by Shastra VC
article_excerpt:
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Startups and Claude Startup programmes.
The proceeds will be utilized to develop multi-agent platforms for video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery, marketing and go-to-market capabilities to reach more enterprise creative teams, and build intellectual property around faces and creative workflows, Lemonpeel said in a press release.

It works with customers in India and the UAE.
The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A quality control layer helps maintain consistency in characters, logos and products.
The platform supports translation and subtitles in more than 100 languages and can also be used from inside AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The company is turning the production steps its team currently handles into product capabilities.
Lemonpeel is focused on media execution end-to-end: editing, maintaining visual consistency and preparing content for approval at scale. This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.
Startups in this space are developing AI-led platforms that automate video production workflows, generate multilingual and personalised videos, enable automated editing, and ensure quality and consistency before content is delivered across digital channels.
Meanwhile, Clueso raised $10 million in a Series A round in Oct. this year, led by Dharana Capital, to strengthen its AI agents and automate enterprise video creation and editing workflows.
TrueFan AI also secured $10 million in Series A funding in June this year, led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners, to scale its enterprise video-generation infrastructure. It also recommends investments and financial products based on users' risk profiles and facilitates transactions with their consent.

The funding comes amid growing interest in retirement planning and the Financial Independence, Retire Early (FIRE) movement among India's working population. Through its platform, finny.club aims to make financial advisory services accessible to mass-affluent Indian households, a segment that has traditionally had limited access to such services.
The startup launched its paid advisory offering earlier this year.

Pinegap addresses this by building custom AI agents tuned directly to each fund’s workflow–learning how a specific fund thinks, then delivering earnings previews, company primers, thesis updates, and news summaries proactively, before the analyst asks. I brought my analyst experience (which includes years at JP Morgan) to the table while Deepak brought the engineering instinct to automate it. Together we developed Pinegap and by early 2025, we launched it commercially.  As of now, we have deployed more than 1,000 agents across 100+ institutional clients, generating upwards of 50,000 research reports per month.

article_title: KelAI Raises $5M to Build an Autonomous Research Engine for Hedge Funds
article_excerpt:
Institutional investing has long operated on a simple but costly constraint: research capacity scales with headcount, and headcount scales slowly. The world’s largest systematic hedge funds – managing assets that collectively exceed $5T globally – built their edges by deploying armies of quantitative researchers, yet even elite teams at firms like Millennium Management and WorldQuant face limits on how many signals they can test, how many datasets they can explore, and how quickly losing hypotheses get retired. The result is a fragmented research process where valuable insights scatter across siloed systems, live signals decay undetected, and portfolio managers receive feedback loops measured in weeks, not hours. KelAI addresses this directly by offering an autonomous AI research engine that runs the full investment research loop – from idea generation and backtesting through signal validation and live monitoring – inside a single agentic platform that compounds knowledge with every iteration. The company’s signals have been running with an institutional investor since October 2025, moving the platform beyond theory into production alpha.

AlleyWatch sat down with KelAI Founder & CEO Jeremie Cohen to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent funding round, and much, much more…

Who were your investors and how much did you raise?

We raised a $5M seed round from Frst, Y Combinator, Robinhood Ventures , and a group of angel investors from the AI and finance industries.

Tell us about the product or service that KelAI offers.

KelAI is an AI research engine for hedge funds and institutional investors. We help investment teams expand their research capabilities.

What inspired the start of KelAI?

After spending years inside leading hedge funds, I saw how much investment research remained limited by human time. Advances in AI created an opportunity to rethink that.

How is KelAI different?

KelAI combines advanced AI with deep investment expertise. It was built specifically for hedge funds by people who understand how institutional research works.

What market does KelAI target and how big is it?

We serve hedge funds and institutional asset managers. It is one of the world’s largest industries, managing well over $100 trillion globally.

What’s your business model?

KelAI operates an enterprise software model.

How are you preparing for a potential economic slowdown?

We are staying  focused on building something the industry needs in every market environment.

What was the funding process like?

It was intense and highly focused. We chose investors who share our long-term view of AI’s role in institutional investing.

What were the biggest challenges you faced while raising capital?

We were fortunate to have a smooth process. Our focus was choosing partners who understood both AI and institutional investing and shared our long-term vision.

What factors about your business led your investors to write the check?

Our domain experience, clarity of vision, and speed of execution.

What milestones do you plan to achieve in the next six months?

We will continue improving the product, grow our New York team selectively, and execute with focus.

What advice can you offer companies in New York that do not have a fresh injection of capital in the bank?

Protect your runway, stay close to customers, and focus on work that creates measurable value.

Where do you see the company going over the near term?

We are focused on building KelAI into a category-defining company at the intersection of AI and institutional investing.

What’s your favorite summer destination in and around the city?

I enjoy escaping to the Hudson Valley or nearby Connecticut. Both are close to the city and offer a refreshing change of pace.

article_title: Axle Raises $9M to Give Investment Banks an Operating System for Corporate Access
article_excerpt:
Corporate access has become a multi-billion-dollar driver of Wall Street revenue because the meetings that put institutional investors in front of public company executives, analysts, and industry experts shape where clients send their business. Demand for those meetings keeps growing, but the coordination behind them has not scaled, as banks juggle investor priorities, executive calendars, and room capacity across event CRMs that log activity and spreadsheets that handle everything else. Axle built an operating system for sell-side corporate access that puts client intelligence, event management, scheduling, logistics, and reporting in one platform. Its AI agents build complex meeting schedules in minutes and use engagement history and institutional holdings to pick targets, and invites, schedules, and reports wait for a person’s review and approval before they go out. More than a dozen sell-side firms, including three of North America’s largest banks, now run on the platform, and customers replace two to three legacy systems each. Next, Axle plans tools that measure and value each investor interaction, so banks can show clients what their access is worth.

AlleyWatch sat down with Axle Cofounder and CEO Sam Shapiro to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent funding round, and much, much more…

Who were your investors and how much did you raise?

We just announced a $9M Seed round. The financing was led by Eniac and Bonfire Ventures, and we were also thrilled to bring on Teamworthy Ventures, which was founded by Thomas Lehrman , the co-founder of GLG.

Tell us about the product or service that Axle offers.

At its core, Axle is the operating system for sell-side corporate access. Investment banks connect institutional investors with public companies, research analysts, and industry experts through flagship conferences, roadshows, field trips, and other high-value interactions. Behind these experiences is an incredible amount of complexity. Axle provides an end-to-end platform that brings client intelligence, event management, scheduling, logistics, and reporting together in one place. Essentially, we give banks AI-native infrastructure to orchestrate these interactions seamlessly, helping investors access the people and insights that inform their investment decisions.

What inspired the start of Axle?

Having worked on the corporate access desk at Goldman Sachs, I saw firsthand how valuable these interactions are to banks and their clients, but also how much work goes into making them happen. Looking across Wall Street, I recognized enormous untapped demand for access, constrained by the manual complexity of coordinating and delivering it. I saw a massive opportunity to unlock the distribution networks banks have spent decades building, giving them the intelligence and infrastructure to connect the right people at the right time and deliver access at a scale that simply wasn’t possible before.

How is Axle different?

Most financial AI tools focus on analysis, modeling, or content creation. Axle is different because its AI agents turn data into action. Outpatient practices are running on thinner margins than they have in years, with support staff salaries and benefits consuming roughly 25% to 30% of revenue while reimbursements stay flat. Corporate entities now own about 30% of U.S. physician practices, according to the AMA, and those multi-site groups carry the same labor shortages and fragmented systems across dozens of locations, yet they still staff phones, fax queues, and payer calls with people, and hiring more of them no longer closes the gap. Confido Health builds AI agents that finish that administrative work across patient access and revenue cycle, instead of only storing the information. Its CareOS platform works across phone, text, email, and fax in more than 20 languages, scheduling appointments, verifying insurance, working prior authorizations, managing refills, and calling patients about open balances, then writes every completed task back to the practice’s EHR. The agents connect to more than 50 existing systems, so practices keep their tech stack, go live in four to six weeks, and gain capacity equal to three to five full-time employees on average within three months. Today the company supports about 3,200 providers across more than 1,500 sites in 27 states, and it grows by selling to private equity sponsors that roll it out across their portfolio companies.

AlleyWatch sat down with Confido Health cofounder and CEO Chetan Reddy to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent funding round that brings the company’s total funding to $25.5M, and much, much more…

Who were your investors, and how much did you raise?

We closed a $12.5M Series A extension led by Z47 , bringing the total Series A round to $22.5M.

Tell us about the product or service that Confido Health offers.

Where systems of record store information, Confido’s seamlessly integrated AI agents act on it, creating an operational system of action that runs a practice from end to end.

Our AI agents work across phone, text, email and fax, in more than 20 languages. They schedule and confirm appointments, verify insurance, handle prior authorizations, process faxes and referrals, manage refills, and call patients about open balances. Every completed task is written back to the practice’s EHR. We integrate with 50+ systems of record, so a practice keeps its existing tech stack and most go live in four to six weeks.

Today we work across more than 1,500 sites of care in 27 states, reaching about 3,200 providers. Roughly one in 50 U.S. patients can now reach their provider through Confido’s agents.

What inspired the start of Confido Health?

When my wife was diagnosed with scoliosis, I saw firsthand how hard it is just to get care. It was a struggle to get calls answered, get clear instructions, and follow up after appointments. When I raised it with her doctor, he was candid: the practice simply didn’t have enough staff to give patients the support they needed. That conversation stuck with me, because it showed a problem far bigger than one office. Outpatient providers across the country are stretched thin by staffing and capacity problems.

So I went to see it for myself. Over 15 months, I visited practices across the U.S. and worked in their front offices. That time convinced me that healthcare providers need better ways to handle administrative work and help patients navigate their care.

Three things.

First, we complete the work instead of routing it. Our agents follow through end-to-end on workflows that connect patients, providers, payers, and pharma. company_description: Small and mid-sized companies make up most of the physical economy: 99.3% of US motor carriers run fewer than 100 trucks, and 93% of US manufacturers employ fewer than 100 people.
article_title: Evos Raises $9M to Put Autonomous Operators to Work Inside the Systems Businesses Already Use
article_excerpt:
Small and mid-sized companies make up most of the physical economy: 99.3% of US motor carriers run fewer than 100 trucks, and 93% of US manufacturers employ fewer than 100 people. Their most valuable asset is the judgment of employees with 20 years on the job, and software that only records what already happened captures almost none of it, so that knowledge leaves when those veterans retire. Evos builds autonomous operators that learn a job from a company’s most experienced people, prove they can match those people’s decisions, and then do the work inside the TMS, WMS, ERP or shared inbox the business already runs. Each operator starts in shadow mode, takes over a function only after its decisions consistently match the team’s, and gives the business control over how much autonomy to grant. One freight brokerage uses an Evos operator to audit every LTL carrier invoice against its TMS, and the operator made nearly 3,500 audit decisions at 97% accuracy in two months and closed out more than $600K of invoice value in the last five weeks alone. Evos passed $1M in ARR four weeks after its first deployments, and every customer has added operators beyond its first.

AlleyWatch sat down with Evos Founder and CEO Urav Shah to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent funding round, and much, much more…

Who were your investors and how much did you raise?

We raised $9M in pre-seed funding. The round was co-led by Uncork Capital and Field Ventures , with participation from Crosslink Capital, Utopia Capital Management, Sandwith Ventures , and a group of angel investors.

Tell us about the product or service that Evos offers.

Evos builds autonomous operators for the businesses that make, move and power the economy: freight brokers, carriers, 3PLs and manufacturers. An operator learns a job from a company’s most experienced people, proves it can match their decisions, and then does the work itself inside the systems the business already runs, whether that is a TMS, a WMS, an ERP or a shared inbox. It replaces nothing and sits on top of what is already there.

For a freight brokerage, that means operators that audit carrier invoices, track loads, handle check calls and work exceptions. For a carrier, it is broker communication, dispatch support, status updates and billing. For a 3PL, it is order and shipment exceptions, customer updates and inventory reconciliation. For a manufacturer, it is production scheduling, supplier follow-ups, quality non-conformance and the procurement paperwork that eats a planner’s week. In every case the operator learns the job from the person who does it today, starts in shadow mode, and only runs on its own once its decisions consistently match the team’s.

The difference from most AI tools is that an operator is given a function, not a prompt. Nobody has to ask it, review it and act on every answer. One freight brokerage has an operator auditing every LTL carrier invoice against its TMS: nearly 3,500 audit decisions at 97% accuracy in its first two months, and more than $600,000 of invoice value closed out in the last five weeks alone.

What inspired the start of Evos?

The story is partly my own. My family ran a manufacturing business in Nairobi for decades, and I spent much of my childhood on factory floors. I went into tech early, started my first company at 18, and by 23 had founded four and exited two, across generative world models, quantum computing and modular data centers.

After my last exit I went home and started consulting for businesses like my family’s: small and mid-sized companies in the physical economy. What struck me was how little had been built for them. Their software was a system of record that logged what had already happened, while the real work happened outside it, with people. article_title: Wally Raises $25M to Give Members Unlimited Cleanings and Diagnostics for $249 a Year
article_excerpt:
American dentistry pays practices to repair decay, so the industry has little reason to prevent it, and insurance reimbursement rules and private equity consolidation push that incentive even harder. The result is a system where only 40% of U.S. adults see a dentist each year, even though more than 80% say they want more care, because visits bring surprise bills, rushed appointments, and the discomfort of metal scraping. Wally answers that gap with a $249 annual membership that covers unlimited cleanings, exams, diagnostics, and whitening, and it takes insurance out of the equation entirely. The company builds its clinics inside co-working spaces instead of standalone dental offices, which lets it open a location in weeks, and a proprietary AI platform runs scheduling and operations while it guides clinicians through each appointment. Swiss AIRFLOW cleaning technology replaces metal scraping and cuts visit times by about half, while digital X-rays, 3D scans, and AI detection show members their own health data. Members rate Wally 4.9 stars and visit three times a year on average, and the company, which now counts more than 50,000 members across New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Illinois, plans to grow from 15 locations to 100 by the end of 2027.

AlleyWatch sat down with Wally cofounder and CEO Tyler Burnett to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent funding round that brings the company’s total funding raised to $28.1M, and much, much more…

Who were your investors and how much did you raise? We raised a $25M Series A led by Maveron with participation from Bling Capital as well as notable angel investors, including Jack Abraham , the cofounder of Hims.

Tell us about the product or service that Wally offers. Wally is a preventative, subscription-based oral healthcare membership. For $249 a year, our members get unlimited cleanings and advanced diagnostics without the hassle of traditional insurance. We use Swiss AIRFLOW technology which eliminates harmful bacteria and stains without any of the painful metal scraping. On top of that, we utilize digital X-rays, 3D intraoral scans, and AI-powered detection so patients can actually see their objective health data. We also offer popular procedures and services including non-invasive cavity reversal, aligners, and custom nightguards at a fraction of the cost of traditional competitors.

What inspired the start of Wally? The inspiration came from a mix of personal frustration and inside perspective. Years ago, after moving from Canada to the US, I went to a new dentist who told me I needed eight cavities filled. I went out and got second and third opinions and learned that seven of those recommended fillings were entirely unnecessary. Around the same time, I was dating my now-wife, who was a recent dental school graduate, so I got an inside look at how the industry operates. My cofounders, Stipe Latkovic and Chelsea Patel , and I realized that the U.S. dental system was fundamentally trapped in an insurance model that forces practices to maximize reimbursements rather than focus on patient health. We wanted to build a company that profits from preventing decay, rather than fixing it.

How is Wally different? We take insurance completely out of the equation. Traditional dentistry runs on a reactive model: get someone in the chair, find something to fix, and bill the insurance. Wally is entirely proactive and transparent. By charging a flat membership fee, we align our incentives with the patient’s actual health. Furthermore, we locate our studios in co-working spaces for ultimate convenience and use a proprietary AI platform to guide clinicians through every appointment, which takes the operational burden off of our dental professionals. That’s a huge reason why we have a 97% hygienist retention rate.

Rising losses and softening prices shrink the margin for error on every decision, AI-native competitors enter the market built for speed, and most insurers still apply AI to isolated administrative tasks that never touch the core calls about which risks to write and how to price them. Kalepa builds Professional Grade AI for insurance, with agents that perform and coordinate work across operations, underwriting, pricing, and portfolio management instead of automating one step at a time. The platform matches the level of autonomy to each task and its risk, brings in people where expertise or approval is needed, and verifies every result so insurers can trace and audit it, a requirement in a regulated industry where decisions carry consequences for years. Insurers using the platform report a 960-basis-point improvement in combined ratio, and the volume of work running through it grew fourfold in the past year as customers such as W.R. Berkley, Bowhead Specialty, and AmRisc expanded their use. That traction positions Kalepa to become the core system insurers run their businesses on across a $7T global market, starting with property and casualty and extending through the full insurance value chain.

AlleyWatch sat down with Kalepa CEO and Founder Paul Monasterio to learn more about the business, its future plans, and recent funding that brings total funding to $91M, and much, much more…

Kalepa coordinates AI, software, and people, matching autonomy to the work and the insurer’s requirements, with verification and traceability built into the process.

Our customers range from global insurance groups such as W.R. Berkley to specialty insurers such as Bowhead Specialty and managing general agents such as AmRisc, which underwrite on behalf of insurers.

Insurance makes much of modern life possible. It helps people protect their families and homes, enables businesses to invest and grow, and gives society the confidence to take risks. It is also critical to innovation: new industries, from AI to commercial space, need new insurance coverage to develop and scale.

We believed one of AI’s most valuable applications would be improving how insurers understand and underwrite risk.

We founded Kalepa in New York in 2018 around that conviction. Underwriting and operations were our starting point, and our ambition has grown with what the technology can accomplish.

article_title: Adaptive Raises $30M to Expand Its AI Workforce Across the $2T Construction Market
article_excerpt:
In construction, the numbers that determine whether a job is profitable rarely live where the accounting happens: a project’s true cost to complete, the cost code a change order belongs to, and what a subcontractor is owed this month typically sit in a superintendent’s head, a daily log, or a text thread rather than in the books, and closing that gap has always meant someone in the office calling, texting, and emailing the field, then typing the answers in by hand. Past attempts to fix this largely asked the field to change its behavior, adding another login for a super or project manager to check between running a job site and coordinating subcontractors, which is part of why so much of that coordination still happens by phone call instead of software. Adaptive takes the opposite approach, sending AI agents out to reach supers and project managers by voice, text, and email on their own schedule, then routing what comes back into job costing, accounts payable, billing, work-in-progress, and compliance without anyone at a desk chasing it down or re-entering it. The agents operate inside a contractor’s existing accounting system rather than replacing it, and every action still passes through a human before it posts to the ledger, a design that has let Adaptive sell not only to general contractors, specialty trades, and developers but to the more than 40 accounting firms that manage books on their behalf. More than 750 construction companies, ranging from $5M to $1B in annual revenue, now run their books on Adaptive across more than 10 accounting systems, from QuickBooks to Sage and Acumatica. As that field-to-ledger record accumulates project by project, the company is positioning it as something contractors can eventually draw on to flag which kinds of jobs tend to run into trouble before they bid the next one, not just to close the books faster.

AlleyWatch sat down with Adaptive Cofounder and CEO Matt Calvano to learn more about the business, its plans for the future, recent funding round, and much, much more…

Who were your investors and how much did you raise?

We raised $30M in Series B funding, led by Tidemark , with participation from our existing investors: Emergence Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Pathlight, Definition, and 3KVC . That brings our total raised to $57M.

Tell us about the product or service that Adaptive offers.

Adaptive is an AI-native accounting platform built for construction. Our agents connect what’s happening in the field with the financial side, so job costing, AP, billings, WIP, forecasting, change orders, and compliance stay current instead of catching up at month end. We’re not replacing anyone’s ERP, we sit on top of it and feed clean, reviewed numbers back in.

What inspired the start of Adaptive?

Adaptive started as a completely different product, a zoning tool for real estate developers. While calling GCs to get rough cost estimates for that, I started asking about the biggest problems in their businesses, and kept hearing the same things: “I never know where profit is going to shake out until the end.” “I double paid my subs.” “I forgot to bill for a change order on a project that’s already closed.” My co-founders and I pivoted, but instead of building software right away, we rented an Airbnb and ran an actual bookkeeping firm for local construction companies for a couple of months to learn the problem from the inside. What we found was that the software that existed was painfully manual, and if a system is a pain to use, the field just won’t use it. That’s what led us to build something that does the accounting work itself.

We don’t ask field teams to learn new software. article_title: Uniti AI Raises $12M to Put AI Agents in Every Corner of Property Operations
article_excerpt:
Real estate is one of the world’s most operationally intensive industries, yet the work of running a portfolio – answering leasing inquiries, chasing overdue payments, coordinating maintenance, managing renewals – still falls largely on human teams stretched across dozens or hundreds of properties. The problem compounds as operators grow: every new site adds complexity, and the communication volume that sustains occupancy and resident satisfaction scales faster than headcount can. Most software sold to real estate operators has digitized records without automating the work itself, leaving property managers to close the gap manually across phone, email, SMS, and chat, often after hours and across time zones. Uniti AI addresses this gap by functioning as an orchestration layer that sits above the property management systems operators already use, deploying a suite of AI agents – covering leasing, customer service, maintenance, collections, payments, renewals, and reviews – that execute each operator’s existing playbook across every channel, 24/7, without replacing the underlying software stack. The platform deploys in 30 to 45 days, integrates with 15-plus property management and CRM systems, and serves operators across self-storage, manufactured housing, multifamily, senior living, and flexible workspace in more than 10 countries.

AlleyWatch sat down with Uniti AI Cofounder and CEO Francesco De Camilli to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent funding round, and much, much more…

Who were your investors and how much did you raise?

We raised a $12M Series A led by Pathlight, with participation from MetaProp and existing investor Prudence . Angel investors include Gokul Rajaram , Lenny Rachitsky , and Romain Huet . Pathlight Partner Mahdi Raza joined our board as part of the round.

Tell us about the product or service that Uniti AI offers.

Uniti is an AI agent platform for real estate operators. Our agents handle leasing and sales, customer service, maintenance requests, payments, collections, and resident communications across voice, email, SMS, and chat. They sit above the property management systems and CRMs operators already use, reading data and writing actions back, rather than replacing the underlying software. Today we serve operators across self-storage, manufactured housing, senior living, multifamily, and flexible workspace.

What inspired the start of Uniti AI?

My cofounder Emre Altinok and I met as freshmen at Yale, then spent the next decade on parallel tracks: he went deep into machine learning, I went deep into real estate operations at companies like Bisnow, Knotel, and Colliers. When large language models got good enough to hold a real conversation, we both saw the same thing from opposite sides. Real estate is one of the most operationally intensive industries in the world, and most of that work is communication: answering calls, qualifying leads, chasing payments, coordinating maintenance. Operators already know how to run their businesses. They didn’t need new software to learn; they needed their existing playbook executed perfectly, at all hours, on every channel. That’s what we built.

How is Uniti AI different?

Most AI in real estate is a point solution: a leasing chatbot here, an answering service there. Uniti is built as an operating layer. Operators codify their actual process — qualification questions, escalation rules, tone, pricing logic — and the agent runs that process across every channel and every workflow, from first inquiry through collections. We also go deep on integrations with the systems each vertical actually runs on, which is why we can deploy in 30 to 45 days and why our pilots convert to paid contracts at a 94% rate. Mumbai based wealthtech firm Veriqus Group has raised Rs 387 crore (around $40 million) in a funding round led by Norwest Venture Partners.
The firm plans to use the fresh capital to expand its network of wealth creators, strengthen its AI enabled wealth management platform, and deepen its presence across Tier II and other high growth cities in India.
Founded by Ashish Gumashta and Roshi Jain, Veriqus provides technology and wealth management solutions for financial advisors and wealth creators. Its platform combines investment products, portfolio management, and AI driven tools to help advisors manage and grow client assets.
The company currently works with more than 500 wealth creators, who collectively manage assets worth over Rs 1.2 lakh crore. It aims to expand this network while increasing its presence beyond metro cities, where demand for professional wealth management services is rising.
According to Veriqus, the funding will also support product development, including AI capabilities designed to improve advisor productivity, portfolio insights, and client engagement.
As per data compiled by Entrackr, Indian wealthtech startups raised more than $634 million across 51 funding deals involving 39 startups during 2024 and 2025. article_title: Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group raises $40 Mn led by Norwest, Skegen Asset Management
article_excerpt:
Precision manufacturing and deeptech company Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group (RVAG) has raised $40 million (around Rs 400 crore) in Series B funding round co-led by Norwest and Skegen Asset Management. The round also saw participation from Indus Bridge Ventures, GJNX Ventures, and Ashish Kacholia.
According to the company's press release, the fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity across its facilities in India, the UK, and the US, accelerate the development of its upcoming integrated manufacturing facility, and strengthen its Mission Systems, Deep Tech, and Autonomous Systems businesses.

The company supplies components and sub assemblies to global aerospace OEMs, including GE Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, Honeywell, Safran, and Collins Aerospace. It also serves energy companies such as Baker Hughes, Halliburton, SLB, and GE.
The company said it currently has an order book exceeding Rs 2,500 crore.
RVAG provides end to end aerospace manufacturing capabilities spanning design, engineering, manufacturing, testing, and assembly. Its capabilities include CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, composites, electronics, gears, fasteners, and NADCAP approved special processes.
Beyond contract manufacturing, the company has expanded into mission systems and deeptech. It develops micro turbojet engines, aircraft hydraulic pumps, missile subsystems, and autonomous platforms, including IC and jet powered drones and unmanned ground vehicles for the Indian armed forces.
RVAG has also partnered with institutions such as the IITs and IIITs, along with research organisations including ARCI and defence agencies such as ADA and DRDO.

article_title: Dhan parent Raise Financial to rebrand insurance arm GIBL as Pluto Insurance
article_excerpt:
Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stock broking platform Dhan, has rebranded GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL), the insurance broker it acquired in May this year, as Pluto Insurance, according to sources familiar with the matter.
The move comes as the company doubles down on the insurance distribution space and prepares to invest Rs 100 crore in the newly rebranded entity. The investment aligns with Raise’s earlier commitment to invest $15 million in the insurance business following the acquisition.
Raise had acquired the IRDAI registered insurance broker in an all cash and stock deal for an undisclosed amount. At the time, the company had said the acquisition would help it build a consumer focused insurance distribution platform with an emphasis on technology, product innovation, and customer experience.
Founded in 2013 by Subir Mukherjee, GIBL operated across more than 50 cities and towns in East and North East India through an offline distribution network, working with over 60 insurers across life, health, motor, and travel insurance segments.
With the rebranding, Pluto.hq will spearhead Raise’s insurance ambitions and operate as its dedicated insurance platform.
Led by Pravin Jadhav, Raise operates platforms including Dhan, Upsurge, Fuzz AI, ScanX, and Stratzy. The company is backed by investors such as Hornbill Capital, MUFG, BEENEXT, and 3one4 Capital.
The insurance business adds to Raise’s growing portfolio of acquisitions. Recently, the company acquired algorithmic trading and investing platform Stratzy in a cash and stock deal and took over new age financial media startup Filter Coffee in January 2025. It is also set to acquire wealthtech startup Infinyte Club.
On the financial front, Raise reported a 13.8% increase in net operating income to Rs 905 crore in FY26 from Rs 795 crore in FY25, according to an ICRA rating report. However, its profit after tax declined 20.1% to Rs 326 crore in FY26 from Rs 408 crore in the previous fiscal.
Entrackr has reached out to Raise Financial for comments.

article_title: Speakeasy Raises $18.8M to Unify Ticketing, Reservations, and Payments for Live Experiences
article_excerpt:
Consumers have spent the past three years shifting their spending from material objects to experiences, and McKinsey reported that global spending on experiences grew 2.6% between 2023 and 2025, more than three times the 0.8% growth in nonessential goods. Yet the venues, restaurants, and festivals that capture that demand still run on a patchwork of ticketing, reservation, payment, and email tools that operate within their own silos and never share data, leaving operators without a clear read on guest value, retention, or marketing return. Speakeasy replaces that disjointed system with one platform that unifies ticketing, reservations, premium experiences, payments, guest CRM, and direct marketing, so every booking, tab, and return visit feeds a single, actionable guest profile. The company built each of those core functions before layering AI on top, because intelligence only compounds once the data underneath it is clean and consolidated. That AI layer now helps operators personalize guest experiences, uncover new revenue streams, and automate routine work, turning guest data from a byproduct of operations into an engine for growth. Clients such as TAO Group Hospitality, E11EVEN, Cipriani, Breakaway Music Festival, and Off Grid @ F1 rely on the platform across 45+ cities, and with Goldman Sachs projecting global live music revenue to grow from $37.4B in 2025 to nearly $65B by 2035, Speakeasy is positioning itself as the source of truth for the in-real-life economy.
AlleyWatch sat down with Speakeasy cofounder and CEO Alex Manavi to learn more about the business, its future plans, recent $18.8M Series A round that brings total funding to $27M, and much, much more…
Who were your investors and how much did you raise?
We raised an $18.8M Series A led by VMG Technology, with participation from Capital One Ventures, Positive Sum, and Yamaha Music Innovations Fund. The financing follows consecutive quarters of accelerating growth against an increasingly favorable macroeconomic backdrop for the IRL economy in an AI-driven world.
Tell us about the product or service that Speakeasy offers.
Speakeasy is the operating infrastructure powering live experiences. Venues, hospitality groups, festivals, and event organizers rely on our platform for critical functions across ticketing, reservations, payments, CRM & direct marketing, with an AI layer that streamlines operations, unlocks new revenue streams, and helps deliver more personalized guest experiences.
What inspired the start of Speakeasy?
We started this business out of the University of Chicago. Collectively, we had experience operating, investing, and building in the space + adjacent industries. That led us to feel strongly that operators needed purpose-built tools and a platform that consolidated the key functions required to put on a live experience, agnostic to end market, backed by a team maniacally focused on product and clients.
Our buildout began with replacing solutions that didn’t work with products we felt were truly beautiful and served critical needs within the very tight time constraints inherent to our space. We were very fortunate to build these solutions alongside top operators who were incredibly gracious with their live and honest feedback. From there, we consolidated those products into one platform, unlocking efficiency and data gains and ultimately doubling down on aggregating and building intelligence on top of this data. We are now integrating deeply into existing enterprise workflows & systems, and have since aggressively built on top of each core pillar of our platform with lots ahead in terms of new capabilities and end markets.
We felt strongly that this sequencing was critical. Before prioritizing AI, we knew that, if we wanted to be the full stack operating system, we needed clean data structures, functional tools, and a consolidated platform.
